jobs.title: Manufacturing Technician I, MD Fill - B2 Shift
jobs.description:
This is our MD Fill - Aseptic Gown - B2 night shift:  6pm-6:30am Wednesday - Friday & every other Saturday

Performs functions associated with cGMP manufacturing operations within the biologics production facility, including working with engineers in set-up and calibration tasks, as well as performing rework and quality testing related to the production of parts, components and final materials. Uses sophisticated programs (such as LIMS, SAP, automated control systems, etc.) to collect and evaluate operating data, which can be used to conduct on-line adjustments to products, instruments or equipment. Determines and may assist in developing methods and procedures to control or modify the manufacturing process.

Responsibilities

• Must have the ability to become aseptic gown certified.
• Shipping finished materials.
• Maintaining inventory levels.
• Sampling of in process and raw materials.
• Running glass washer / autoclave.
• Buffer / media preparation.
• Equipment preparation (CIP / SIP).
• Cell culture (from vial thaw to production scale).
• Column chromatography.
• Tangential flow filtration
• Wear an aseptic gown during an 8 hr shift. This gown covers the full body.
• Willing to complete a lot cleaning sanitation during the work shift
• Follow all clean room entry and exit procedures
• Wear the required aseptic gowning and PPE correctly at all times
• Perform hand hygiene and sanitization before entering the clean room
• Maintain aseptic technique to prevent contamination of materials and products
• Sanitize work surfaces, tools, and equipment on a frequent and consistent basis
• Minimize movement, talking, and unnecessary activity in the clean room
• Inspect gowning and PPE for proper fit and integrity before use
• Report any contamination concerns, spills, or equipment issues immediately
• Handle sterile materials only in approved areas and in a controlled manner
• Follow all environmental monitoring and cleaning requirements
• Dispose of waste and contaminated materials according to procedure
• Complete all required documentation accurately and on time. Good hand writing will be a huge plus.

Please note that the YouTube video is not owned, produced, or sponsored by AbbVie and does not accurately depict AbbVie’s aseptic processes and procedures. The video is provided solely as an example of the aseptic gowning process.

• High School diploma (or equivalent experience), with 2+ years experience. Associates degree in science, with 1+ years relevant experience. Bachelor's Degree with 0+ year relevant experience.

• Works on assignments that are routine in nature, requiring limited judgment.
• Has the ability to recognize when accepted practices are deviated from.

jobs.title: Program Director, Biobanking
jobs.description:
The Colossal Foundation is looking for an experienced program leader who will build and run the operational engine behind BioVault, Colossal's endangered species biobanking program. The role's first and largest commitment is Colossal's partnership with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: a multi-year effort to collect, process, and cryopreserve living cell lines, reproductive tissue, and genomic material from endangered and threatened species across the United States. The role also directs Colossal's other biobanking efforts, including collaborations with zoological institutions, universities, and international conservation partners, and the Colossal Foundation's genetic rescue programs.

This role sets BioVault's annual species targets, builds the partner network of refuges, zoos, state agencies, universities, Tribal nations, and international institutions that supplies samples, and holds the schedule and reporting commitments under the USFWS MOU and Colossal's other biobanking agreements. This role works closely with Colossal Foundation staff, including the Partnerships Manager, and with Colossal's Animal Operations, Embryology, and Assisted Reproduction teams and external partners to keep every program on time and aligned with BioVault's sample-completeness standards. This position reports to the Executive Director of the Colossal Foundation.

This position is based out of Dallas, TX and relocation assistance is provided.

Duties and Responsibilities:

• Own program delivery under the Colossal–USFWS MOU: annual species batches, collection schedule, throughput, and the completeness tier (Minimum / Target / Gold) achieved for each species.

• Direct Colossal's other biobanking collaborations with zoological institutions, universities, and international conservation partners, applying the same standards, systems, and chain-of-custody practices established under the USFWS program.

• Build and manage the partner network that performs or hosts sample collection, including USFWS refuges and field offices, state wildlife agencies, zoological institutions, universities, Tribal partners, and international collaborators; own partner agreements, training, kit logistics, and quality control on incoming material.

• Lead a cross-functional program team spanning field collection, biorepository operations, partner enablement, data management, and logistics; hire and develop the program's staff through its first two phases.

• Serve as Colossal's day-to-day counterpart to USFWS program leads on joint work plans, quarterly reporting, species prioritization reviews, and issue escalation, and as the primary program contact for other biobanking partners.

• Set and track program metrics (species sampled, cell lines established, tiers achieved, time from collection to banked material) across all BioVault efforts and report to Colossal and Colossal Foundation leadership.

• Coordinate protocol hand-offs for reproductive tissue and gamete cryopreservation with Colossal's Embryology and Assisted Reproduction teams without diverting their capacity from core programs.

• Represent BioVault with conservation partners and the scientific community, in coordination with Colossal Foundation staff.

• Travel to field sites, partner institutions, and USFWS offices, including some international travel, up to 30%.

Required Skills and Abilities:

• Demonstrated success leading a multi-site, multi-partner wildlife, conservation, or field biology program at regional or national scale, with direct ownership of staff and delivery.

• Working knowledge of the Endangered Species Act and the federal, state, and Tribal permitting landscape for handling listed species; this role works closely with Colossal's registrar and permitting staff, who hold and administer program permits.

• Experience building and running partner networks with government agencies and zoological or academic institutions, including negotiating agreements and setting shared standards.

• Operational fluency with sample chain-of-custody, cold-chain logistics, and laboratory intake workflows, or demonstrated ability to learn them quickly.

• Strong program management discipline: work plans, milestone tracking, risk management, and clear written reporting to executives and agency partners.

• Strong communication skills (written/verbal), including presenting to agency leadership and external partners.

• Ability to work across Colossal Foundation staff and Colossal's Animal Operations, Embryology, and Assisted Reproduction teams, including veterinarians, scientists, and animal husbandry experts.

• Must be able to travel up to 30%.

Education and Experience:

• B.S. in biology, wildlife science, conservation biology, or a related field required; M.S., Ph.D., or D.V.M. preferred.

• At least ten years of experience in wildlife conservation, zoological, or field research programs, including at least five years directly managing programs and staff.

• Experience working with or inside USFWS, state wildlife agencies, or zoological institutions strongly preferred.

• Experience with biobanking, genetic resource banking, or wildlife genomics programs preferred.

What Colossal Offers Full-Time Employees:

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Excellent paid time off and company holidays so you can rest and recharge

• Flexible spending accounts (FSA)

• Company matched 401k retirement plan

• Paid parental leave at 100% salary for up to 12 weeks

• Education reimbursement

• An opportunity to help us return the Earth to a healthier state

The team at Colossal is committed, colorful, passionate, intelligent, collaborative, creative, experienced, scientific and world-class. That sounds like a lot to fit into one building. That’s why we are spread out in several locations that include laboratories, test facilities, academic institutions, libraries and offices.

Through it all, however, we maintain a culture of positivity, hope, happiness and belief that we’re doing something big. Something Colossal.

Colossal is proud to be an equal employment opportunity workplace. We welcome people from all backgrounds as well as celebrate and support diversity. We are committed to providing an inclusive environment of mutual respect that is free from discrimination and harassment so everyone can thrive.

jobs.title: Client Partner
jobs.description:
Description

Verista’s 500 experts team up with the world’s most recognizable brands in the life science industry to solve their business needs. The nature of our business is to empower growth and innovation within the scientific community and to help researchers, organizations, and companies solve some of the world’s most pressing healthcare challenges. Verista provides innovative solutions and services that empower informed decision-making and are the result of our significant investment in our people and our capabilities.

Our ability to grow is driven by world-class people who thrive in a team environment and share our mission to enable life sciences clients to improve lives. Our talented and dedicated professionals are committed to making an impact every day.

Company Culture Guidelines & Values:

• We empower and support our colleagues

• We commit to client success at every turn

• We have the courage to do the right thing

• We encourage an inclusive environment where our colleagues feel respected, engaged, and challenged.

• We constantly acquire new skills and learn from our experiences to enhance our collective expertise

The Client Partner role is responsible for both direct client contract value retention as well as growth through contract expansion and the introduction of new products and services solely or through a delivery manager and supporting service delivery team.The responsibility of the role is typically focused on large, multi-site strategic accounts and high upside smaller accounts while supporting upstart, new logo sales accounts. This position is responsible for driving new business within an account base, with defined objectives for account growth, margin.

The primary areas of focus for this role include client satisfaction, revenue growth, account level oversight of delivery managers and onsite teams specific to service delivery, management of current and new business operations, business development for new and existing clients with the overall goal to lead your team to growth and achievement of the executive leadership’s goals and vision.

The account base may include but is not limited to the following employee roles: delivery managers, business unit managers, account managers, project managers, project engineers, automation engineers and validation engineers. The role is expected to guide each unit and all employees to drive solutions and decisions based on Verista mission, vision, and values. The Client Partner is a cross functional leader that must work with the Service Line Team and Executive Leadership Team to develop and ensure quality execution of engineering services and new business opportunities.

The position is to set an example of Verista Culture of hard work, positive attitude, commitment to satisfy the customer, and strong interpersonal skills.

Primary Duties/Job Responsibilities:

• Responsible for creating and directing strategy for large or growing accounts including driving and coordinating selling and relationship activities

• Responsible for detailed understanding of large, global account client business strategy, drivers, goals and initiatives and translating these into Verista selling opportunities:

• Account management with outcome of increased customer satisfaction and increase in retention & account growth Growth goal responsibility aligned to specific account baseProficient in strategic account management & planning

• Manage forecast accuracy on a monthly/quarterly/annual basis

• Partner with Service Lines to implement and track strategies that ensure delivery teams meet and exceed sales, utilization, and growth goals

• Ensure all engineering projects, initiatives, and processes are in conformance with organization's established policies and objectives.

New Business Development:

Verista is positioned well to grow our business and the Client Partner has primary responsibility in this area including the startup of new accounts or new areas so Verista maintain and improve upon our great name and reputation.

• Be open and supportive of resource transfers to and from your business unit to support overall company growth.

Assume the role of Primary Contact for Client Manager and Partner levels (C-level) with the following responsibilities:

• Strengthen existing relationships with clients.

• Establish new client relationships within existing client area.

• Ensure quality of work from the delivery team remains high. Manage proposal development and volume to keep your team at acceptable utilization levels.

In collaboration with the Service Line Management, drive 95% utilization levels for your entire group including new and transferred resources.

Manage all active and open purchase orders and ensure that units remain funded at all times.

• Verify all Service Line Directors are updating resourcing plans and seeking funding prior to full expenditure of existing funding.

• Ensure your account personnel are only working on funded projects

Actively manage and document new and existing client opportunities including overall total revenue, forecasts, and resource planning strategies.

• Regularly (monthly) visit existing clients and target clients to maintain a presence, obtain feedback, ensure quality, and realize new growth opportunities.

Sales responsibilities:

• Responsibility for hitting Sales Quota for growth at assigned Accounts in conjunction with Service Line Director/Senior & Delivery Manager

• Manage Salesforce Leads/Opportunities/Bookings with support of Service Line / Senior /Delivery Manager

• Maintain sufficient pipeline total and weighted to achieve results (generally total pipeline should be 2-3x the sales required)

• Support Verista growth goals at each existing account. Generally, 20% but could be significantly higher or lower depending on account

• Ownership of Strategic Account Management Plans in assigned Accounts in direct collaboration with the Service Line / Senior /Delivery Manager

Resourcing responsibilities:

• Working closely with other Directors and VP on a weekly basis to identify resource needs and gaps and assigning best resource

• Communication with HR Manager and Recruiter about resource needs including skillset required and timing

• If necessary, interviewing prospective candidates and making recommendations to VP/COO

• Work closely with Sales to make sure we have resourcing in place for potential new/solid opportunities

• Work with sales to close identified opportunities and develop account management strategies at new accounts (<12 months)

• Manage travel expectations for employees travelling over 50% for over three months

• Provide regular updates to the Executive Leadership on resourcing projections, sales, and metrics

• Develop strategic partnerships and help develop new accounts, as necessary

• Raise awareness within leadership team of those who are unbillable, or who will become unbillable or whose contract ends in less than 3 months

• Actively seek and communicate customer feedback – key strengths and improvement areas

• Manage team resourcing and outlook to ensure effective and appropriate staffing levels. Clearly and effectively communicate staffing needs (positive or negative) in a timely manner to allow for effective sales

Provide leadership within your group to improve the following areas:

• Work with Executive Leadership Team to set goals and expectations for his or her group

• Define clear, measurable goals and expectations within your employees’ performance management plans, including working with management to define career paths for supervisory and technical growth opportunities in your team

• Promote team concept within own group first, but also within other Service Line groups

• Attend quarterly service line meetings with Team Building activities

• Challenge employees to do their best. Have high expectations!

• Hold employees accountable who do not meet expectations and provide feedback appropriately

• Motivate team members to perform at a high level

• Develop and build a team environment with high morale and positive corporate culture

• Manage and develop strategy for engineering processes, procedures, and training

• Focus upon ensuring standards and consistency with each and every employee and client. Verista must focus on providing a consistent, quality service regardless of the client, employee, or their processes

• Be open to take on and develop new talent

Qualifications:

Required Knowledge and Experience:

• Experience working in a fast paced, results driven organization

• Experience in Project Management; managing numerous small projects (5+) of <$50K or large projects in excess of $500K.

Preferred Skills:

The following skills are preferred:

jobs.title: Robotics Controls Engineer Lead
jobs.company: Galactic Resource Advancement Mechanism Technologies Corporation
jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, United States
jobs.description:
About the company

GRAM Corporation scales skilled labor for the physical economy. We design, manufacture and operate insectoids, general-purpose machines not built in our image. They work in large populations on the critical infrastructure nations depend on. The electric grid comes first. Our research is in how those populations coordinate and keep themselves running. The goal is Self-Replication (SR), the point where a population of machines delivers more labor than it takes to build and run.

The role

You will own locomotion controls for GRAM’s multi-legged robot, from the low-level actuator loops to whole-body control on uneven terrain. Model-based control is the priority, and learning-based control experience is a bonus. This is a hands-on role: you will write the controllers yourself, tune and prove them on the robot, and work closely with the Autonomy, Simulation and Systems Integration teams. You start as an individual contributor, with a path to build and lead a controls team as the company grows

Responsibilities:

• Develop and implement model-based locomotion control systems for multi-legged robots.

• Write and optimize low-level actuator loops and whole-body control algorithms.

• Test and validate control systems on physical robots in various terrains.

• Collaborate with Autonomy, Simulation, and Systems Integration teams for seamless integration.

• Contribute to the research and development of innovative control strategies.

• Provide technical leadership and mentorship as the team expands.

Required Skills:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• Strong expertise in model-based control systems for robotic platforms.

• Experience with low-level actuator loop development and optimization.

• Proficiency in programming languages such as C++ and Python.

• Knowledge of learning-based control methods is a plus.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• Strong teamwork and communication skills.

What you will do:

• Own locomotion and whole-body control for the multi legged robot on uneven terrain, and the body state estimation from IMU, joints and contact that it runs on.

• Own low level actuator control and system identification of actuators and contact.

• Set measurable targets for tracking, stability, disturbance rejection and latency, and prove them on hardware.

• Tune, debug and validate controllers on the robot, working with the Autonomy, Simulation and Systems Integration teams.

What you bring:

• Model predictive control or whole-body optimization-based control, deployed on physical hardware with measured results.

• Solid grounding in rigid body dynamics, forces, contact stability and latency.

• Strong C++ and Python.

• Experience with state estimation for legged or floating base robots.

• 8+ years of hands-on controls work on physical robots. A PhD in controls or robotics lowers the experience bar

Nice to have:

• Legged robot experience strongly preferred.

• Experience integrating learned policies with a model-based controller

• Trajectory optimization and reduced order models for legged locomotion.

• Torque controlled or quasi direct drive actuators.

• Footstep planning and integration with terrain perception.

• Tuning hardware and controllers for repeated impact loading.

• Tools such as Drake, Pinocchio or MuJoCo.

Why join

• A clean slate: define how a new multi-legged robot moves.

• Early equity, included in the package

• The chance to own a domain and build a team around it as the company scales.

• A hands-on culture where engineers work directly on the core technology.

jobs.title: Lead GTM Talent Partner
jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US

incident.io http://incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.




THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

We're looking for an exceptional GTM recruiting leader to help us build one of the best teams in San Francisco. Someone who can hire incredible people, lead and develop a brilliant recruiting team, and become the go-to talent partner for our US leadership. You'll have huge ownership, loads of freedom, and the chance to help put incident.io http://incident.io on the map in SF.




WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

We've built an incredible reputation in London and one of the best teams in the city. Now we want to do the same in San Francisco.

We've got around 35 people in SF today, and we're planning to grow that significantly. Building an exceptional team here is one of our biggest company priorities, and we need someone brilliant to lead the charge.

You'll report to our Head of Talent in London, which means for most of your working day, you're running the show in SF. You'll be the go-to person for our CRO, sales leaders and hiring managers, driving hiring plans, challenging decisions, keeping everyone accountable, and making sure we're hiring exceptional people at pace.

You'll also lead and mentor our growing US GTM recruiting team. We want someone who loves developing people, sets incredibly high standards, and knows how to get the best out of a team. You'll own the hiring numbers, understand exactly what's happening in the funnel, and make sure we're always one step ahead.

But this isn't a role where you just manage from the sidelines. We want someone who loves recruiting and is exceptional at it. You'll be hands-on, building relationships with incredible talent, running searches, and showing the team what great looks like.

And we're not a talent team that just posts jobs and waits for applications. In London, we've thrown events, built creative branding campaigns, and even set up coffee kiosks to get in front of people we want to hire. Now we want to go bigger in SF.

Think world-class events, run clubs, billboards, brilliant swag, creative partnerships, and whatever else gets people talking about incident.io http://incident.io. You'll help shape our talent brand in the city, build an incredible network, and find new ways to get in front of people who aren't actively looking for a job.

It's a big job, with a huge amount of ownership. You'll have the freedom to build things, try new ideas, and make a real impact on how we grow in the US.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You're an exceptional GTM recruiter. You've got a track record of hiring brilliant sales talent, from ambitious early-career reps through to senior commercial leaders. You know what great looks like and have the results to prove it.

 - You're a natural leader. You've led or mentored recruiters before, you love helping people get better, and you know how to set high standards without micromanaging. You lead by example and aren't afraid to get stuck in.

 - You can hold your own with senior leadership. You're confident partnering with CROs, VPs and sales leaders. You're comfortable challenging hiring managers, pushing back when something isn't working, and having difficult conversations when needed.

 - You take complete ownership. You don't wait to be told what to do. You spot problems, come up with solutions, and make things happen. You're organised, commercially minded, and always know your numbers.

 - You've got an incredible eye for talent. You can spot exceptional people, ask brilliant questions, and see potential others might miss. You've got great instincts and an incredibly high bar.

 - You love the thrill of the hunt. You get a buzz out of finding brilliant people, getting creative with sourcing, building relationships, and convincing someone who wasn't looking to take a conversation.

 - You're creative and a bit scrappy. You've got big ideas and the energy to execute them. Whether it's an amazing event, a clever campaign, or something nobody's tried before, you love finding new ways to get in front of great people.

 - You thrive with autonomy. You're excited by the idea of being the most senior talent person on the ground in SF. You make good decisions, move quickly, and don't need someone looking over your shoulder.

We don't mind whether you've built your career in agency or in-house. We're looking for someone with serious drive, brilliant instincts, leadership potential and a track record of hiring exceptional people.

If you're ambitious, love building things, and want to play a huge part in scaling one of the most exciting startups in SF, we'd love to meet you.




SUPPORTING YOU

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

 - Market-leading private medical insurance. The proper kind, so you're never weighing up your health against a bill.

 - Competitive PTO. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

 - First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

 - Enhanced 401k. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

 - Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

 - Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

 - Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

 - Two budgets that have your back. $1000 to invest in your setup, $500 a year to invest in yourself.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter, Warehousing (Contract)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a key member of Anduril's Talent Acquisition team, you will be responsible for the company's talent management as we continue to rapidly scale and grow. Your work will be hands-on and involve collaborating with Warehousing and Global Logistics leaders to define the hiring needs, influence process improvements and efficiencies, and set a high bar of talent and performance. To achieve this, you will be given the autonomy and tools to execute, build, and develop Anduril's world class team. We are looking for someone who can handle every aspect of recruiting and talent mapping, excited to be part of lean and nimble team on one mission together, where no task is too big or too small.

This role will be hybrid in Costa Mesa, CA. This is a 6 month contract with the ability to extend up to 18 months. Opportunity to be converted to a full-time employee based on performance, impact, and business need.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Act as a subject matter expert in prospecting techniques and tools used for information retrieval, data extraction, web-scraping, continuous process improvement, process automation, and candidate management

• Own and drive hiring strategy full-cycle, providing effective, clear communication and reporting

• Conduct a high volume of interviews, demonstrating ability to anticipate and influence hiring manager preferences through successful interview-to-offer conversion ratios

• Engage and source passive candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean strings, referrals and SOBO campaigns

• Build talent maps to generate market insights to inform your engagement strategy

• Drive diverse talent into the organization ensuring a positive candidate experience at every touchpoint

• Represent the company's brand and recruiting team internally and externally at the highest caliber

• Leverage internal resources, team mates, and cross functional partners to build strategy around selling our value proposition and impacting hiring practices

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 6+ years experience as a high-volume full-cycle recruiter evaluating and hiring top tier talent

• Experience working with senior level leaders and stakeholders, reporting on progress, creating and advising on hiring/talent strategies

• Experience recruiting at an agency and fast-paced startup, hiring exempt roles for Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Production, or Manufacturing Engineering

• Ability to be onsite/hybrid at Costa Mesa office.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience working at an agency or fast-paced startup environment

• Knowledge of ITAR policies around hiring practices

• Experience acting in a consultative manner where your guidance has led to improved outcomes and positive candidate experiences

• Clear and effective communication with candidates to understand motivation, drivers, and fit within the organization

• Experience managing various high-volume pipelines of candidates and keeping track of their progress throughout the recruitment process

• Highly autonomous, collaborative, and adaptable

US Hourly Range

$60—$75 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Field Sales Representative - Doncaster
jobs.description:
Field Sales Representative

Location: Doncaster, covering Doncaster or surrounding areas such as Mexborough, Thorne or Bawtry (fully field-based)

£50,000–£90,000 OTE (£30,000–£54,000 base salary + uncapped commission, based on experience) + £800 monthly car allowance and a comprehensive benefits package

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re ambitious, enjoy meeting new people and want to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We’re looking for ambitious, driven people to join our growing Field Sales team and help bring Teya to more local businesses across the UK.

As a Field Sales Representative, you’ll take ownership of your own territory, getting out into your local community, meeting business owners face-to-face and showing them how Teya can help their businesses thrive.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the field, building relationships and winning new business. You’ll have the freedom to manage your territory, the support of a team that wants you to succeed, and the opportunity to build a rewarding career in sales.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Own your territory: Proactively identify and engage local businesses through face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals and other opportunities to generate new business.

 - Build meaningful relationships: Get to know business owners, understand their challenges and identify how Teya’s products and services can make their lives easier.

 - Win new Members: Use a consultative, value-led approach to demonstrate Teya’s solutions, build trust and turn conversations into long-term customer relationships.

 - Deliver results: Take ownership of your sales performance, maintain a healthy pipeline and consistently work towards your commercial targets.

 - See things through: Take responsibility for your Members’ experience from the first conversation through to onboarding, ensuring they’re set up successfully and ready to start using Teya.

 - Keep learning: Develop strong knowledge of our products, competitors and sales methodology through structured training, coaching and feedback.

 - Represent Teya: Be a trusted face of Teya in your local community, delivering the genuine care and hospitality that we want every Member to experience.

 - Help us improve: Share insights from the field to help us continuously improve our products, sales approach and Member experience.

Your Story

We believe great salespeople come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might already be an experienced field sales professional with a strong track record of winning new business. Or you might be earlier in your career, with the ambition, drive and potential to become an exceptional salesperson.

What matters most to us is your mindset, your ability to connect with people and your willingness to learn and improve.

We’re looking for people who bring:

 - Ambition and drive: You’re motivated to succeed, enjoy working towards challenging goals and take pride in delivering great results.

 - A competitive mindset: You enjoy winning, hold yourself to high standards and are always looking for ways to improve.

 - Resilience and determination: You’re comfortable with rejection, stay positive when things get tough and don’t give up easily.

 - Strong people skills: You enjoy meeting new people, build rapport naturally and can have meaningful conversations with business owners from all walks of life.

 - Curiosity and commercial awareness: You ask good questions, listen carefully and want to understand what makes a business successful.

 - Coachability: You’re open to feedback, willing to challenge yourself and committed to developing your skills.

 - Ownership and self-discipline: You’re organised, proactive and comfortable managing your own time and priorities in a field-based role.

 - A genuine care for others: You understand that great sales isn’t just about closing a deal. It’s about doing what’s right for the customer and building trust that lasts.

Experience in field sales, business development, payments or financial services is an advantage, but not essential for every level. We care just as much about your potential as your experience.

You’ll also need:

 - Fluency in English.

 - A full UK driving licence and access to a car.

 - The right to work in the UK.

 - Willingness to work in a fully field-based role, travelling regularly throughout your territory.

The Perks

We believe great performance should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

 - £30,000–£54,000 base salary, depending on your experience and demonstrated capability.

 - Uncapped commission.

 - £800 per month car allowance (£9,600 annually), on top of your salary and commission.

jobs.title: Index Analyst Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
About Syntax Data
Syntax LLC is a financial data and technology company that codifies business models into a relational system we call Affinity Data™. Syntax operates through three segments: Affinity Data™, Syntax Direct™, and Syntax Indices™. Using its patented FIS® technology inspired by systems sciences, the Affinity Data™ segment offers the most comprehensive, granular, and accurate product line revenue data available on the market. The Syntax Direct™ segment then uses this abundance of data to facilitate the near instantaneous creation and ongoing management of boundless direct indexing solutions and rules-based equity portfolios through a fully automated platform. The Syntax Indices™ segment offers customized and proprietary indices, including core global benchmarks and micro- and macro-thematic, smart beta, defined outcome, and target volatility indices. These indices are foundational for a range of financial products, such as ETFs, UITs, and structured products.

About the Role
The Index Intern will support our team by assisting with the research, creation, and development of market indices.

jobs.description:
Room Attendant

As a Room Attendant, you play a pivotal role in ensuring our guests experience a comfortable and pristine environment during their stay at our resort. Your attention to detail and commitment to cleanliness contribute to the overall satisfaction of our guests.

What is in it for you:

• Unleash the excitement: enticing rewards and unbeatable benefits are waiting for you!

• Room Preparation: Ensure the cleanliness and readiness of guest rooms, including making beds, replenishing amenities, and arranging furniture to meet established standards.
• Cleaning Procedures: Perform cleaning tasks in various areas of the resort, such as corridors, lobbies, and public spaces, using appropriate cleaning agents and equipment.
• Attention to Detail: Pay meticulous attention to detail when cleaning, organizing, and arranging guest rooms and public areas, maintaining the highest standards of cleanliness.
• Inventory Maintenance: Monitor and report the status of cleaning supplies and amenities to the Housekeeping Supervisor to ensure adequate stock levels for daily operations.
• Guest Interaction: Respond promptly to guest requests for additional services or amenities and assist in resolving any concerns or issues related to housekeeping.
• Team Collaboration: Work collaboratively with fellow housekeeping attendants and other departments to ensure efficient and smooth resort operations.

• Physical Stamina: Ability to perform physically demanding tasks, including lifting, bending, and standing for extended periods.
• Detail-Oriented: Strong attention to detail to ensure all aspects of room preparation and cleaning meet or exceed guest expectations.
• Team Player: Willingness to collaborate with the housekeeping team and other departments to create a positive and cohesive work environment.
• Customer Service: Basic understanding of providing excellent customer service to enhance the overall guest experience.

Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion: We are an inclusive company and our ambition is to attract, recruit and promote diverse talent.

Why work for Accor? We are far more than a worldwide leader. We welcome you as you are and you can find a job and brand that matches your personality. We support you to grow and learn every day, making sure that work brings purpose to your life, so that during your journey with us, you can continue to explore Accor’s limitless possibilities.

By joining Accor, every chapter of your story is yours to write and together we can imagine tomorrow's hospitality. Discover the life that awaits you at Accor, visit https://careers.accor.com/

About Mantis Collection: Mantis is a boutique hospitality group that was founded by conservationist Adrian Gardiner in 2000, with its main focus predominantly in Africa and the Middle East. Mantis grew from Adrian’s vision to restore and rewild degraded farmland which he developed into a widely-acclaimed Private Game Reserve. This was the first private game reserve in the Eastern Cape and the beginning of eco-tourism in a poverty-stricken province that had few opportunities outside of commercial farming. Adrian and the Mantis team successfully created a place where man and nature could co-exist sustainably. From this initial success, the Mantis model was then developed worldwide, understanding that consumers could use the Mantis portfolio as a mark of quality, consistency and character. Today the diverse portfolio of handpicked properties links up to create travel journeys, which offer guests the opportunity to experience the essence of the location in a setting of tailored luxury. Rooted in conservation, Mantis pursues sustainable business practices and develops tourism products that are respectful of the environment and communities in which they operate.

Do what you love, care for the world, dare to challenge the status quo! #BELIMITLES

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - (AI x Greentech) (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
MAKE EVERYTHING JUST WORK

Most jobs ask you to keep the lights on. This one asks you to build the machine that keeps an entire company and its customers running.

At Reonic, we’re building the AI operating system for renewable installers, with competitive pay, growth opportunities and a strong culture based on ambition, impact and ownership. And we’re doing it fast.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’re where our product meets the real world. You work hands-on with renewable energy installers and their technical teams, help them build on our API, and solve the problems that stand between them and a setup that just works. Around 80% of your time is spent with customers. The other 20% goes to making Reonic itself run the way an AI-first company should.

What you'll do

With our customers (~80%)

 - Enable our API users: Work with customers’ technical teams as they build on our API and webhooks. Review their approach, answer the tricky questions and get them unblocked fast.

 - Solve problems end to end: When something breaks, you find out why. Reproduce the issue, work with engineering on the fix and keep the customer in the loop until it’s solved.

 - Connect Reonic to their world: Make Reonic work seamlessly with the tools our customers rely on every day, from Microsoft and Google to their CRM, accounting and automation platforms.

 - Make customers self-sufficient: Write guides, examples and snippets that help customers help themselves.

Inside Reonic (~20%)

 - Run our AI tools: Own our Claude and ChatGPT workspaces, from access and connectors to costs.

 - Make AI part of everyone’s job: Help colleagues build integrations, connectors and automations that save them real time.

 - Own our IT setup: Keep our tools, devices and security running smoothly, so everyone at Reonic can do their best work from day one.

What makes you a great fit

 - Technical understanding: You’re comfortable with APIs, webhooks and authentication flows such as OAuth, and you aren’t afraid to dig into the details.

 - AI and automation enthusiasm: You use tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Zapier or n8n every day and enjoy finding new ways to automate work.

 - Customer orientation: You’d rather solve a problem together on a call than send another ticket reply, and you can explain technical topics in a way non-technical people understand.

 - Microsoft 365 expertise: You have hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, and you’re the person others turn to when something in the Microsoft world doesn’t work.

 - Strong communication: Fluent German and C2 English proficiency are required.

 - Nice to have: TypeScript knowledge, experience with Apple Mobile Device Management, and experience with any of the systems we integrate with, such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Google Workspace, lexoffice or sevdesk.

You’ll thrive here if you…

 - Can’t stand a broken process, and fix it before anyone else notices

 - See a messy setup as a challenge, not a reason to complain

 - Automate anything you’ve done twice

 - Would rather get sh*t done than talk about getting it done

 - Are the one friends and colleagues call when their tech doesn’t work

If you want a quiet IT job with a ticket queue, this isn’t it.
If you want to be the reason things run smoothly at a fast-growing company, you’ll love it.

Why join now

 - Real impact: Help build software that enables businesses to accelerate the transition to renewable energy.

 - A product people use: Our platform is already used by 3,000+ paying B2B customers, so your work reaches real users with real-world impact.

 - High ownership: We’re a growing company, and nothing is set in stone. You’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work, internally and with our customers.

 - Fast-moving environment: Work closely with engineering, product and customer teams, make decisions quickly, and see the results of your work right away.

 - A great international team: We work hard, learn from each other, and make sure we have fun along the way.

 - Gym membership or transportation ticket: Pick between Urban Sports Club or Deutschland ticket.

 - Late nights covered: Uber Eats and Uber rides on us when you finish late.

 - Great setup: MacBook, regular team events, coffee and other perks.

 - Competitive compensation: We offer competitive pay based on your experience and responsibilities.

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply! Imposter syndrome shouldn’t hold you back — we value talent and passion above all.

About Reonic

At Reonic, we’re on a mission to simplify renewable technology.

Our AI operating system helps renewable energy installers run and grow their businesses: from planning and selling solar, battery storage, and heat pump solutions to managing their day-to-day operations.

Location

This is a full-time, on-site position based in Augsburg or Berlin.

Ready to shape the future of renewable energy? Apply now!

jobs.title: Operations Associate, San Francisco
jobs.description:
Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.
From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future.

We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.

 

The role

You’ll run programs across Ambrook: placemaking, events, tech enablement, design program management, research, and special projects. You’ll spot what the team needs, build systems that work across functions, and run the creative projects that make teammates and customers feel taken care of.

You’ll lead placemaking for our San Francisco https://ambrook.com/sf office. You’ll report to our co-founder and Head of Product Dan Schlosser https://www.linkedin.com/in/danrschlosser/ and drive programs across the company. Some of your projects will span all three offices and our distributed team.

You’ll run several programs at once, and that range is a big part of the appeal. You’ll see how every part of a company works, find the work you enjoy most, and lean into it. Your scope grows across functions as you build trust by keeping things moving.

You’ll have an amazing counterpart in Crystal Luo https://www.linkedin.com/in/crystalluo2002/, who runs programs from the New York https://ambrook.com/ny office today, and an incoming counterpart in Denver https://ambrook.com/denver.

Note: this role takes many forms in different companies, so if you think there's a more apt job title for these responsibilities and your career goals, let's talk about it during the interview process!

 

What you’ll do

Craft shows up across this role: a personal touch on a candidate’s onsite, the first batch of Ambrook sweaters, scouting our next office, or visiting customers to bring that same care to the people who run the real economy.

 - Own placemaking in the SF office. Make it a place teammates enjoy working from and where San Francisco's builders, designers, and operators can meet us. Run the small rituals that help teammates know each other, and handle the guests, vendors, supplies, equipment, and access behind it.

 - Partner with founders on special projects. Work with Dan to pick up whatever matters most that month and see it through: prepare for key meetings and hires, run special projects end to end, and drive decisions to done. You’ll get a bird’s-eye view of how a company runs and grows.

 - Shape how customers and candidates meet Ambrook. Recruit customers for research sessions and product pilots, and plan and join trips to see them around the region, from South Bay garlic farms to producers in the hills of Petaluma, plus visits across the country. Run local candidate onsites and organize portfolio reviews from invite to follow-up.

 - Catalyze community with events. We want Ambrook to be one of the places where engineers, operators, and founders meet to share what they’re learning. Plan coffees, intimate dinners, and meetups around the metro area, along with company activations across offices, and curate the guests and topics so each one is worth showing up for.

 - Improve tech enablement. Work with department managers and the other program managers on how teammates get access to the tools they need, from onboarding and offboarding to rolling out new software and AI tools. Write down what works so it holds up as we grow.

 - Create AI systems where things keep breaking. When a process trips people up repeatedly, pause and rebuild it.

 

About you

 - You’ve spent 1 to 8 years in roles like operations, recruiting, hospitality, or production.

 - You’re hospitable and care about craft, from noticing what a guest needs before they ask to the content of an event invite and the interior design of our space.

 - Friction bothers you. You’d rather spend an afternoon improving a system than work around a broken one for months.

 - You’re good with tools. You can set up a new hire’s accounts, fix a conference room, and use AI to save time on recurring work.

 - You know talented people in key SF circles: tech, startups, design, research, and industry. You’re curious and have great stories to show for it.

Details

 - Full-time, based in our SF office in the Mission, at least 4 days a week.

 - Reports to Dan Schlosser https://www.linkedin.com/in/danrschlosser/, co-founder and Head of Product. 

 - Health insurance, 401(k) match, paid parental leave, flexible vacation, and wellness and learning stipends.

jobs.title: Founding GTM Strategy & Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT DAVID AI

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We’re hiring a Founding GTM Strategy & Operations Lead, our first dedicated hire focused on the operating system behind our go-to-market team.

Our customers are the world’s leading AI labs, and our deals move fast. You’ll be the person who keeps every deal moving, makes sure nothing slips through the cracks, and builds systems and automation. Your work will drive better visibility and insight into our sales pipeline while laying the foundation for our GTM team to scale. This is a hands-on role: you’ll own the day-to-day execution yourself while designing how GTM operations should work as we grow.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own our CRM and pipeline forecasting end to end, making the CRM the single source of truth that founders and leadership rely on to run the business.

 - Lead the operating rhythm of our GTM team and be the person who keeps every deal moving. Run deal roll calls and pipeline reviews, and partner closely with Deployment Strategists and founders to ensure each opportunity has a clear next step.

 - Build GTM operations from 0→1, AI-native from day one. Turn ad hoc processes into repeatable systems, and design agents and workflows that automate reporting, follow-ups, and database maintenance.

 - Shape how David AI goes to market. Bring a clear point of view on where the pipeline is at risk and what the team should prioritize, and work directly with leadership on GTM planning.




YOUR BACKGROUND LOOKS LIKE

 - 3+ years of experience in Sales Operations or a Strategy & Operations role.

 - A genuine obsession with automation. You already use AI tools in your daily work and instinctively ask "how do I never do this manually again?"

 - Deep, hands-on experience managing a CRM, running pipeline forecasting, and owning pipeline processes for a sales team.

 - Exceptional organization and follow-through. You keep many moving pieces on track without being asked.

 - The ability to hold stakeholders accountable to next steps. You’re comfortable being the person who asks “where are we on this?”

 - Clear, concise written communication.

 - A bias for action, comfort operating in ambiguity, and excitement about doing the hands-on work required at an early-stage company.




BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience at a fast-growing, AI-native startup.

 - Experience building GTM operations from scratch.

 - Hands-on experience building AI agents or automations for GTM workflows.




BENEFITS

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.

 - FSA & HSA access.

 - 401k access.

 - Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.

 - Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.
   
   


VISAS

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B transfers, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

jobs.title: Senior Enterprise Account Executive - Robotics (Boston)
jobs.description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

Impact In This Role

As a Senior Enterprise Account Executive - Robotics, you'll work with some of the most exciting robotics OEMs, warehouse automation integrators, and companies building industrial robots, cobots, AMRs/AGVs, and humanoid platforms — helping them source precision components (actuators, end-effectors, structural parts, enclosures) as they move from prototype through low-volume and bridge production. You'll dig into each customer's business goals — financial KPIs, vision, key initiatives, org structure, in-house manufacturing capabilities, R&D labs — and their internal decision-making structure, so you can build relationships with the right people. You'll also learn their product roadmaps, requirements, and priorities for bringing products to market, along with their existing partnerships (design partners, contract manufacturers, local shop preferences). With that knowledge, you'll configure the right solution to speed up their time to market — identifying both prototyping opportunities and production-class manufacturing programs that let customers launch products faster than they thought possible. Your leadership will be key to coordinating the full MISUMI Americas team supporting you. You'll deliver sales presentations and lead on-site meetings — sales meetings, quarterly business reviews, tech days — to build confidence, deepen relationships, and grow customer lifetime value.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Build relationships with mechanical/electrical engineers and supply chain leads at robotics and automation companies

• Track industry trends (humanoid robotics, warehouse automation, autonomous mobile robots) to identify new account targets

• Understand robotics-specific manufacturing needs — tight tolerances, lightweight materials, small-batch runs, rapid design iteration as robots move from R&D to scale

• Build credibility and trust with C-suite stakeholders

• Prospect to build and maintain a healthy pipeline

• Meet and exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual sales quotas

• Maintain accurate account and opportunity forecasting in Salesforce.com

• Generate new business opportunities within your target account list

• Build meaningful, long-term relationships with key customer contacts

• Represent the company at trade shows, conferences, and industry events

• Become a true expert in your accounts' product development needs, plans, and challenges

• Help expand MISUMI Americas' reputation as a leader in digital manufacturing

• Spend over 50% of your time traveling to meet customers face-to-face

• Work within a team sales structure

• Collaborate cross-functionally to win complex deals

Desired Traits

• Experience selling specifically into robotics, automation, or advanced hardware companies — not just manufacturing broadly

• Familiarity with robotics components/subsystems (actuators, sensors, grippers, drivetrains) a plus

• Comfortable working with customers who iterate hardware designs quickly and need fast part turnaround

• Minimum of 5 years consistently meeting and exceeding monthly and quarterly targets

• Manufacturing and supply chain industry experience

• BS/BA degree preferred

• Strong grasp of product development and related business requirements

• Experience driving consultative, solution-based sales and expanding within strategic industry verticals

• Track record of quickly building a new pipeline and managing a forecast to consistently exceed quota

• Expertise with modern sales tools (CRM, sequencing, prospecting, collaboration platforms)

• Experience with TAM/SAM analysis

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Standard office and home-office work environment with extensive computer, phone, and video-conference use. Ability to travel by air and drive within assigned territory, including navigating customer plant floors and manufacturing environments during field visits.

Perks and Benefits

• Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401K plan

• Parental leave programs

• Paid volunteer days

• And much, much more!

Salary: $100,000 base per year, $100,000 variable per year (uncapped)

Interested in learning more?  We look forward to hearing from you soon.

We’re actively seeking teammates who:

• Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.

• Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.

• Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.

• Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.

• Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

jobs.title: Head of Field Operations
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

Zipline’s U.S. delivery network brings together autonomous aircraft, field infrastructure, and teams operating across multiple markets. Field Operations must deliver safe, reliable, and consistent service while building the leadership, capacity, and operating practices needed to grow.

As Head of Field Operations, you will own Zipline’s national Field Operations strategy and performance, while leading the organization through regional leaders. You will translate company priorities into operating plans, resource decisions, and standards that work across each/all the regions. You must be able to align leaders around a clear direction, develop strong teams, and stay close enough to the field to resolve the most consequential problems.

What You'll Do

• Hire and develop regional leaders; own organizational design, staffing, coverage, succession, and Field Operations budget planning, allocating resources against demand and growth priorities.

• Set national and regional targets for safety, reliability, delivery performance, and efficiency; lead performance reviews and hold regional leaders accountable for sustained results.

• Establish common safety practices, site routines, training expectations, escalation paths, and readiness standards with functional owners; ensure adoption and prompt action when conditions are unsafe.

• Sequence new sites and markets with Launch and Commercial teams, align staffing and operating readiness with site and technical dependencies, and establish clear handoffs into stable daily operations.

• Align Field Operations with Flight Operations, Customer Operations, Maintenance, Service Engineering, Launch, and partner teams; clarify decision rights and resolve ownership gaps while respecting functional safety and technical authority.

• Use site performance and field feedback to address recurring issues, simplify work, and improve consistency; prioritize corrective actions with functional owners and verify that improvements hold across regions.

• Hire and develop regional leaders; own organizational design, staffing, coverage, succession, and Field Operations budget planning, allocating resources against demand and growth priorities.

• Align Field Operations with Flight Operations, Customer Operations, Maintenance, Service Engineering, Launch, and partner teams; clarify decision rights and resolve ownership gaps while respecting functional safety and technical authority.

• Use site performance and field feedback to address recurring issues, simplify work, and improve consistency; prioritize corrective actions with functional owners and verify that improvements hold across regions.

What You'll Bring

• Experience leading senior managers or regional leaders, developing successors, and building accountability through multiple management layers.

• Judgment balancing safety, service reliability, growth, and cost, including during disruptions and decisions under pressure.

• Strong workforce and financial planning skills, including headcount, operating budgets, capacity, and resource allocation.

• Experience establishing operating standards and helping distributed teams adopt new tools and ways of working.

• The ability to connect technical capabilities with daily operations, coordinate complex programs across functions, and turn field insight into lasting improvements.

• Willingness to travel frequently across U.S. regions and work directly with frontline teams, particularly during launches and major operating issues.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $200,000 - $250,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

jobs.title: Field Operations Supervisor | Atlanta, GA
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

Zipline is looking for a Field Operations Supervisor to lead daily execution across 3–5 Drone Charging Sites in the greater Atlanta area. These sites support aircraft readiness and delivery operations.

You will directly lead local field teams and help ensure each site is staffed, safe, organized, and ready to operate throughout the seven-day operating week. You will coach employees, coordinate schedules and training, reinforce standard operating procedures, and address performance or readiness gaps.

You will report to the Business Field Operations Lead,  and work closely with Flight Operations, Customer Operations, Maintenance, and other teams. The Business Operations Lead sets market priorities and operating systems; you will translate those priorities into consistent execution across your assigned sites.

This is an onsite, field-based role requiring regular travel between locations. The operating schedule spans seven days, so the role may require early mornings, evenings, weekends, or holidays to support team and site needs.

What You'll Do

• Lead daily site execution. Ensure assigned sites are staffed, organized, and ready to support the operating schedule.

• Manage and develop frontline teams. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, coach performance, and address issues promptly and consistently.

• Support hiring and onboarding. Partner with the Business Operations Lead on staffing needs, participate in hiring, and help new employees complete onboarding and role training.

• Coordinate schedules and coverage. Build and adjust staffing plans for assigned sites based on operating hours and business needs. Identify coverage risks early and communicate gaps.

• Train teams and reinforce standards. Deliver or coordinate training, confirm employees understand their responsibilities, and coach teams on approved procedures.

• Implement and improve SOPs. Ensure teams follow current operating procedures and site checklists. Identify unclear or outdated instructions and recommend updates to the Business Operations Lead.

• Maintain site readiness. Monitor charging equipment, supplies, inventory, and site conditions. Coordinate with Maintenance or other teams when equipment or facility issues need attention.

• Monitor performance and take action. Review measures such as fulfillment speed, site readiness, quality, and customer experience. Use data and direct observation to identify problems, assign follow-up, and track progress.

• Conduct site visits and audits. Check operating standards across shifts and locations, document gaps, and follow through on corrective actions.

• Coordinate issue response. Work with Flight Operations, Customer Operations, Maintenance, and the Business Operations Lead to resolve operational issues and escalate risks promptly.

• Support launches and operational changes. Help prepare teams and sites for new launches, updated procedures, and changes to local operations.

• Communicate field conditions. Provide timely updates on staffing, site readiness, team performance, risks, and improvement opportunities.

• Build future leaders. Identify employees with leadership potential and provide coaching and development opportunities.

What Success Looks Like

• Assigned sites have reliable staffing and are prepared for the seven-day operating schedule.

• Employees understand their roles, training requirements, and operating procedures.

• Site readiness issues are identified early, assigned to the right teams, and followed through to resolution.

• Teams consistently follow safety and quality standards across locations and shifts.

• Performance gaps are addressed with clear coaching and documented follow-up.

• Site conditions and operating practices are consistent across the supervisor’s assigned locations.

• The Business Operations Lead has timely, accurate information about field performance, staffing, risks, and support needs.

What You'll Bring

• At least 3 years of experience in field operations, fulfillment, logistics, warehouse operations, retail management, or a related field.

• At least 1 year of direct experience supervising or coaching frontline employees.

• Experience coordinating schedules, staffing coverage, training, and performance expectations.

• Ability to use operational data and direct observation to identify issues and make practical improvements.

• Strong communication and coaching skills, including the ability to set expectations and address performance concerns.

• Strong organization and follow-through across multiple sites, teams, and priorities.

• Ability to work independently in the field and travel regularly between assigned sites.

• A hands-on leadership style and willingness to assist with physical operations when needed.

• Availability to support a seven-day operation, including early mornings, evenings, occasional weekends, and holidays based on business needs.

• A valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

• Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Ability to complete required pre-employment screening and employment eligibility verification.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $75,000-$90,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!
