jobs.title: Shift Lead (Fort Shafter)
jobs.description:
JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 18 years of age or older.

Prior QSR management experience highly desired.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 4".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24"- 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Good standing License with a minimum of one year driving history and a safe, reliable vehicle.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

Assistant managers are responsible for everything that happens during the shift. This includes cost control, inventory control, cash control and customer relations. You set the tone and the example for the store and you have to be on your game 100% of the time!

Your job responsibilities would include (but are not limited to):

• Perform all the duties of the Customer Services Representatives and Delivery Drivers.

• Maintain a professional appearance at all times in compliance within the Domino's Pizza Grooming Standards.

The good news is we can teach you how to answer the phone and make a perfect pizza. But here are a few skills you should have to be a successful Assistant Manager:

• Experience leading a team; during your shift, you will manage a staff of anywhere from 3 to 30 people. You will need to use your stellar attitude and motivational skills to get them in the right place, at the right time and doing the right thing all while creating a great place to work.

• A great role model - you're the person everyone will look to. From being on time for your shift, to having a great attitude to customers and co-workers and even how you dress - you have to have high standards for yourself and the rest of the team.

jobs.description:
General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be at least 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

You’re the boss, the big cheese, top dog. You’re a natural born leader, so maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the head honcho? You got game? You got spring in your step? You want the best job in the world! And schedules that work with you, not against you? That's right, we live to beat the rush and make it possible to make, bake or take pizzas during the hungry hours of the day and night, part or full time. Even if you just need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, drop us a line. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From customer service representative to management, General Manager to Manager Corporate Operations or Franchisee, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 16 years of age or older for in store work. You must be 18 years of age or older for Delivery work.

General job duties for all store team members

• Operate all equipment.
• Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
• Prepare product.
• Receive and process telephone orders.
• Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
• Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions. Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

• Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
• Must be able to make correct monetary change.
• Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
• Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
• Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to:

• Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks. In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
• Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside. Fumes from food odors. Exposure to cornmeal dust.
• Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
• Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
• Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

• Talking and hearing on telephone.
• Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
• Depth perception.
• Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following :

Standing: Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking: Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

• Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
• Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
• Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

• Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
• Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
• Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

• To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
• Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

STOOPING/BENDING

• Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
• Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
• Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
• Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

CROUCHING/SQUATTING

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

REACHING

• Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
• Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
• Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
• Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

HAND TASKS

• Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
• Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
• Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
• Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
• Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
• Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

MACHINES, TOOLS, EQUIPMENT, WORK AIDS

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

In addition to the above listed descriptions. Delivery drivers will also need to be able to perform the following:

Driving Specific Job Duties

• Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.
• Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

• Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.
• Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Essential Skills

• Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.
• Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Physical Demands

CARRYING: During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

DRIVING: Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

WALKING: Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

CLIMBING: During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Work Conditions

Exposure to:

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

Sensing: Far vision and night vision for driving.

jobs.title: General Manager(05151) - 15634 NW Us Hwy 441
jobs.description:
Our Domino's Pizza Assistant Managers are the backbone of our business! Assistant Managers handle all aspects of running a Domino's Pizza store, including leading their team, setting high standards for customer service and maintaining exceptional product quality standards.

Paid Training!

We offer a chance for professional growth by requiring all our Assistant Managers to be trained and certified through our unique Management Development Program. If you have limited experience, this program will teach you everything you need to learn to become a successful manager. If you have previous experience, the program allows for self-paced learning and fast tracking to help you advance.

Opportunities!

Our Management Development Program allows only our own store managers to apply for franchising opportunities - which sets us apart from our competition. For many of our General Managers, the ultimate goal is to own their own business. Only individuals who have successfully managed a Domino's Pizza store for at least a year, are eligible to apply for a franchise. Join our team and learn how business ownership may be within your grasp!

Great Pay!

Our assistant managers are paid a a industry competitive salary. In addition, assistant managers are eligible to earn performance based wage increases and sometimes incentives based on the profitability of their stores, as well as the store's overall performance.

Qualified management applicants must be at least 18 years old, have a valid driver's license and a good driving record. Some management experience is a plus. The ability to work in a fast-paced, high volume environment and be able to handle multiple tasks at once is required.

ABOUT THE JOB

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. Then you go to work and you make sure that everyone there is doing what they need to do, even your boss. You just do that because you've always done it. Well maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance - Domino's Pizza is hiring bosses - more specifically assistant managers. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills - judgement, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance& punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Ready to hit the road and make deliveries happen? Here's what your day will look like:

• **Master the open road** – Safely operate your delivery vehicle like a pro, following all traffic laws and company safety guidelines while navigating Denver's streets with confidence

• **Keep it clean and organized** – Maintain a neat, well-organized delivery vehicle that's ready for action
• **Follow the playbook** – Stick to company protocols for package handling and customer interactions to ensure everything runs smoothly

• Valid driver's license with a clean driving record
• Proven experience operating delivery or commercial vehicles
• Strong knowledge of vehicle operation, maintenance, and safety procedures
• Excellent time management and organizational skills
• Proficiency with GPS navigation systems and route planning tools
• Ability to lift, carry, and transport packages weighing up to 50 pounds regularly
• Strong customer service and interpersonal skills
• Ability to work independently and meet strict delivery schedules
• Familiarity with Denver area geography and local traffic patterns (preferred)
• Basic computer skills for electronic delivery confirmation systems
• Physical capability to perform repetitive loading and unloading tasks
• Reliable attendance and punctuality

jobs.description:
Pay range is $14-$20 depending on experience.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

EXPOSURE TO

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Additional Job Details Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. Maintian all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability. jobs.title: Program Manager, Customer Education
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey's Customer Education team delivers education at scale to professionals at law firms and in-house legal teams around the world. As Customer Education Program Manager, you will run a global series of product and legal AI education webinars, develop out-of-the-box Harvey workshops, and support colleagues across Harvey, such as the law schools team, with curriculum and consistent, high-quality content for their programs. You’ll turn objectives to polished sessions, and will monitor adoption data that shows what worked and how our programs can be improved. We need a versatile builder who moves easily among instructional design, visual design, and program management and who brings structure and calm to a fast-moving product.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


PROGRAM DESIGN AND CURRICULUM

 - Design role-based programs that move law firm and in-house professionals from onboarding to daily use of Harvey

 - Apply adult learning principles and instructional design models to set objectives and build and sequence content

 - Translate product releases and expert workflows into practical lessons for legal professionals

 - Adapt content for regional audiences, practice areas, and varying levels of experience with Harvey

 - Partner with Product and Customer Success to keep curriculum current as the platform evolves


GLOBAL WEBINAR PROGRAM

 - Own a global program of product and legal AI education webinars, from calendar and topic selection through registration, delivery, and follow-up, with sessions that serve AMER, EMEA, and APAC

 - Recruit and prepare presenters and subject-matter experts, write run-of-show documents, and produce polished slides

 - Facilitate and moderate sessions for audiences of all sizes

 - Tailor sessions for law firm, in-house, and practice-area audiences, and coordinate regional presenters

 - Track attendance, engagement, and post-session product usage, and use the results to refine topics and formats

 - Test new formats, such as office hours, workshop series, and on-demand recordings, to extend reach across regions and audiences


WORKSHOPS AND PROGRAM SUPPORT

 - Develop out-of-the-box Harvey workshops, complete with slides, exercises, and facilitator guides, that colleagues and customers can run on their own

 - Partner with colleagues who run their own programs, such as the law schools team, and support them with curriculum, materials, and instructional design

 - Set shared standards that keep education content consistent in quality, voice, and brand across Harvey's programs

 - Update workshops and shared materials as Harvey releases new products and features

 - Track how colleagues and customers use workshops and shared materials, and refine them based on feedback


PROGRAM MATERIALS

 - Create one-pagers, quick-reference guides, and PDFs that customers use without a trainer in the room

 - Apply Harvey brand standards and strong visual design to every asset

 - Maintain an organized, current library of customer-facing learning resources

 - Partner with Customer Success to embed resources in onboarding and renewal programs across customer segments


LEARNING PLATFORM OPERATIONS

 - Publish and maintain content in Harvey Academy LMS

 - Configure courses, enrollments, and learning paths by audience and region

 - Report on completion, engagement, and adoption metrics




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Four or more years of experience managing customer education, enablement, or training programs, preferably at a B2B technology company

 - Experience supporting cross-functional colleagues with curriculum and content for their programs

 - A portfolio that shows your program and visual design work

 - Experience running live training programs, such as a global webinar series

 - Command of instructional design methods and adult learning theory

 - Strong visual design skills in Figma, Claude, Google Slides, or similar tools

 - Hands-on experience with at least one LMS or customer academy platform

 - Clear, precise writing for professional audiences

 - Working knowledge of generative AI and how legal professionals use it

 - Confident facilitation for large virtual audiences

 - Strong organization and sound judgment in prioritizing competing requests


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience teaching legal, tax, financial services, or other professional services audiences

 - Experience with webinar platforms such as Zoom Webinars

 - Familiarity with learning analytics that connect education to product adoption

 - Experience using AI tools to speed content development




COMPENSATION

$120,900 - $166,200 USD

jobs.title: Corporate Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
At Rula, we are a remote-first company that believes mental health is just as important as physical health. We recognize that mental health issues can be complex and multifaceted, and we are dedicated to treating the whole person, not just the symptoms.

We aim to create a world where mental health is no longer stigmatized or marginalized, but rather is embraced as an integral part of one's overall well-being. 

We believe that by providing quality care that is both evidence-based and compassionate, we can empower individuals to take charge of their mental health and achieve their full potential. We are passionate about making a positive impact on the lives of those struggling with mental health issues and we strive to be a force for positive change in the field of mental healthcare.

About the Role

We are seeking a Corporate Accounting Manager to strengthen Rula's Accounting team by taking on our more complex journal entries, including payroll, and helping make our monthly close faster, simpler, and easier to repeat as the business scales. In this role, you will support the month-end close, review colleagues' work where needed, and document and improve the processes behind our financials as we grow. You will work closely with the Sr. Corporate & Technical Accounting Manager and a small, collaborative team, with real room to shape how we work, including using automation and AI to cut down manual effort. If you enjoy bringing order to a fast-moving environment, this is a visible role where your ideas will be put to use.

Required Qualifications

 - 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 2+ years in public accounting (audit or assurance)

 - Hands-on experience contributing to the monthly close in an industry setting, including preparing complex journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis

 - Demonstrated experience designing, documenting, and improving accounting processes (for example shortening the close, reducing manual work, or strengthening controls)

 - Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and the ability to apply it to non-routine transactions

 - Experience working in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities, balancing recurring close deadlines with improvement projects, and the flexibility to move across areas of the team as needs change

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications

While having the preferred qualifications enhances your candidacy, having all of them is not mandatory. We encourage all interested applicants to apply, even those who may not meet every preferred requirement.

 - Active CPA license

 - Experience at a high-growth, venture-backed, or pre-IPO company

 - Experience reviewing the work of other accountants and sharing knowledge with the team

 - Experience with close management, ERP, and spend tools (for example NetSuite, FloQast, Zip, Ramp, or similar), including automating manual work

 - Exposure to internal controls over financial reporting (SOX), audit coordination, or public company readiness

 - Experience preparing payroll journal entries across multiple entities, or with equity (stock-based compensation) or capitalized software accounting

We're serious about your well-being! As part of our team, full-time employees receive:

 - 100% remote work environment: Working hours to support a healthy work-life balance, ensuring you can meet both professional and personal commitments (must be based in United States, currently not hiring in Hawaii)

 - Attractive pay and benefits: Full transparency of pay ranges regardless of where you live in the United States

 - Comprehensive health benefits: Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and FSA/HSA

 - 401(k) plan access: Start saving for your future

 - Generous time-off policies: Including 2 company-wide shutdown weeks each year for self-care (for most employees)

 - Paid parental leave: Available for all parents, including birthing, non-birthing, adopting, and fostering

 - Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Supporting your mental and physical health

 - Quarterly department stipend: Fun team-building activities or in-person gatherings

 - Community and employee resource groups: Participate in groups that celebrate employee identity and lived experiences, fostering a sense of community and belonging for all

 - Home office stipend: New hire home office stipend & $50 monthly stipend to help cover internet or cell phone expenses

 - Wellness at Rula program: Year-round wellness initiatives and a $50/month wellness stipend

Our team

We believe that diversity, equity, and inclusion are fundamental to our mission of making mental healthcare work for everyone.  We are dedicated to having a culture of inclusion that will support our employees in feeling safe, seen, heard, and valued.

4DMT is a leading late-stage biotechnology company advancing durable and disease-targeted therapeutics with potential to transform treatment paradigms and provide unprecedented benefits to patients. The Company’s lead product candidate 4D-150 is designed to be a backbone therapy forming the foundation of treatment of blinding retinal vascular diseases by providing multi-year sustained delivery of anti-VEGF biologics (aflibercept and anti-VEGF-C) with a single intravitreal injection, which substantially reduces the treatment burden associated with current bolus injections. About Us:

BlackSky is a real-time intelligence company. We own and operate the world's most advanced space-based intelligence platform and provide customers satellite imagery, automated analytics and high-frequency monitoring of strategic locations, economic assets and events from around the globe. BlackSky is trusted by the most demanding allied military and intelligence organizations and commercial companies to deliver foresight into critical matters that affect national security and the economy. This includes high-speed tasking, ground and space telemetry, health monitoring, and low-latency communication with ground stations worldwide. In this role, you’ll develop software that bridges the gap between hardware-level interfaces and cloud-deployed microservices. You’ll contribute to mission-critical systems that keep our satellites safe, responsive, and efficient; operating 24/7 with minimal human intervention.

Success in this role means having a strong sense of initiative and ownership, a deep curiosity for how complex systems work, and the discipline to trace and validate requirements while thoughtfully challenging them when needed. jobs.title: Staff Technical Project Manager, Global Physical Security
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

We're hiring a Staff Technical Project Manager to own delivery of Crusoe's Global Physical Security (GPS) portfolio. Your deliverable is the outcome, not the schedule: every site moved onto our new platforms, a working GSOC, and site findings closed.


You'll run several related workstreams at once across Construction, Facilities, IT, site operations, integrators and vendors. None of them report to you. You'll turn loose commitments into dated, owned, checkable deliverables, hold people to them, and force decisions when work stalls.

This is a program role, not a project role. You'll be the person who sees a slip coming weeks out and raises it with options, rather than reporting the miss after it lands.

Level: Staff. 
Reports to: Lead, IT & Security Program Management Office. 
Location: San Francisco, CA; Denver, CO; or Dallas, TX.



What You'll Be Working on:

 - System Lifecycle & Deployment: Manage end-to-end delivery of physical security assets—including access control, video surveillance (CCTV), intrusion detection, and Security Operations Centers (SOC)—from design and installation to testing and commissioning.

 - Standards & Governance: Own and adapt global physical security standards, master specifications (e.g., Division 28), and reference design templates across regions.

 - Cross-Functional Integration: Partner with IT, network engineering, legal, privacy, and facilities teams to integrate physical security systems with enterprise networks and digital tracking tools (CAD/BIM validation, dashboards).

 - Vendor & Contractor Management: Direct external security system integrators, author technical scopes of work, evaluate RFPs, manage bids, and oversee site quality assurance (QA/QC).

 - Risk & Change Management: Conduct site risk assessments, handle design-exception governance, and manage brownfield/retrofit upgrades with zero or minimal operational downtime.

You'll own six workstreams that together make up the GPS program.

 1. Access control and video platform migration. Move every site off the legacy Meraki estate onto our selected cloud-based access control and video platforms, and onboard new sites as they come online. Waves run Q2 through Q4.

 - Wave planning and site sequencing

 - Per-site readiness criteria and tracking

 - Cutover runbooks and rollback plans

 - Acceptance testing and sign-off

 2. GSOC buildout. Bring our Global Security Operations Center to go-live. Coordinate facility readiness, technology cutover, staff onboarding and the go-live checklist across Construction, IT and our staffing vendor.

 3. Site remediation. Our security assessments produce a findings register, and most fixes belong to Facilities, Construction or site ops. You'll get each finding an owner and a date, drive it to close, and keep the register visible to leadership.

 4. Integrator delivery. Manage multiple integrators across geographies.

 - Scope-of-work templates

 - Submittal review cycles

 - Acceptance testing and defect closeout

 - Integrator performance scorecards

 5. Vendor and procurement lifecycle. Run RFPs, contract timelines and onboarding for staffing, platform and monitoring vendors. Several of these land this quarter and next.

 6. Intake and triage. Stand up a front door for new GPS requests so each one is scoped, prioritized and sequenced against the roadmap instead of quietly absorbed.



How You'll Work:

 - Make commitments real. Turn "we'll get to it" into a named owner, a date and a clear definition of done.

 - Hold the line on dates. Hold peers, vendors and people senior to you to what they committed, directly and respectfully.

 - Lead without authority. Drive work across orgs you don't control, and escalate only when escalation is the right tool.

 - Call slippage early. Read leading indicators such as late submittals, long-lead equipment and unstaffed shifts. Raise risk while there's still time to act.

 - Force decisions. Know the difference between work that needs chasing and work that needs someone to decide. Get the decision framed, put it in front of the right person, and get it made.

 - Set the standard. Define how GPS runs programs, including planning templates, readiness criteria, status cadence and scorecards that other teams adopt.

 - Exercise discretion. You'll handle site layouts, vulnerabilities and incident details. You know what to share, with whom and when.
   
   

What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 10+ years in technical program or project management, including at least 5 years owning a multi-workstream program end to end

 - Delivery experience in the built environment, including construction schedules, integrators, submittals, commissioning and turnover

 - A track record of multi-site rollouts across a geographically distributed portfolio

 - Enough technical fluency in access control, video surveillance, networking and low-voltage systems to challenge an integrator's plan and spot when you're being talked in circles

 - Experience running vendor work end to end: RFPs, SOWs, contract milestones, acceptance and performance management

 - Comfort holding senior stakeholders and vendors accountable, and forcing decisions without leaning on escalation

 - Clear, concise written status reporting that leads with risk and the ask

 - Sound judgment and discretion with sensitive security information

 - Experience standing up a GSOC, SOC or other 24/7 operations center

 - Background in data center, critical facilities or mission-critical construction

 - Experience managing contract security staffing or remote monitoring vendors

 - PMP, PgMP, PSP or CPP certification

 - Familiarity with security frameworks and audits that touch physical controls, such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001
   
   

Bonus Points

 - Hands-on experience with cloud-managed access control and VMS platforms, or with migrating from one to another
   
   

Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $230,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Lead Design CNC Programmer/Operator
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Role Overview

The Lead Design CNC Programmer/Operator is responsible for programming, setting up, and operating CNC equipment in support of Design Studio vehicle properties, prototype models, and development programs.

Working closely with Design, Engineering, Modelers, and Fabrication teams, this role supports the manufacture of a diverse range of prototype components, from small development parts to full-scale vehicle bucks, aerodynamic models, composite tooling, fabricated structures, and show car assets.

The ideal candidate combines strong CNC programming and machining expertise with exceptional organization, problem-solving ability, and adaptability. Success in this position requires the ability to work across a broad range of materials, project types, and component scales while consistently delivering high-quality work in a fast-paced prototype environment.

Key Responsibilities

CNC Programming & Machining

• Develop, optimize, and verify CNC programs for complex 3-axis and 5-axis machining applications.

• Setup, operate, and troubleshoot large-format CNC routers and gantry mills.

• Select and implement machining strategies, tooling, and work holding solutions that deliver high-quality prototype parts and properties.

• Evaluate CAD data and identify potential manufacturing concerns before machining begins.

• Maintain organized PowerMill projects, CNC programs, fixture models, and related manufacturing data.

Prototype Manufacturing Support

• Manufacture prototype components supporting vehicle development programs, including design bucks, ergonomic properties, aerodynamic models, composite tooling, fabricated structures, clay studio assets, and show car components.

• Interpret CAD models, design data, and engineering information to develop practical manufacturing solutions.

• Modify CAD geometry and create fixtures, support structures, and work holding solutions when required.

• Collaborate closely with Design, Engineering, Modeling, and Fabrication teams to support successful project execution.

Technical Excellence & Support

• Serve as a technical resource for CNC programmers and operators.

• Provide guidance on machining strategies, tooling, fixturing, and manufacturing processes.

• Take ownership of the department's most technically challenging machining projects.

• Support troubleshooting efforts across programming, machine operation, tooling, and manufacturing methods.

• Lead by example through technical excellence, craftsmanship, organization, and accountability.

Equipment & Shop Support

• Monitor machine performance and operating conditions to ensure reliable operation.

• Perform routine maintenance and support preventative maintenance activities.

• Identify opportunities to improve machine performance, tooling, machining processes, and overall shop capability.

• Support a safe, clean, and organized working environment.

Minimum Qualifications

• 5+ years of CNC programming and machining experience.

• Strong experience programming and operating both 3-axis and 5-axis CNC equipment.

• Proficiency with Autodesk PowerMill and working knowledge of CATIA and/or Fusion 360.

• Experience working directly from CAD models and digital design data.

• Strong understanding of machining principles, tooling selection, work holding, and manufacturing processes.

• Proven problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Effective communication and collaboration skills.

• Ability to work independently within a fast-paced prototype environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience within an automotive design studio, prototype manufacturing environment, model shop, motorsports, aerospace, or similar low-volume manufacturing environment

• Experience programming and operating large-format CNC machinery.

• Experience machining large-format components and vehicle-scale properties.

• Familiarity with Heidenhain, Fagor, and Mitsubishi control systems.

• Experience designing fixtures, supports, and manufacturing aids.

• Experience machining polyurethane modeling board, aluminum, carbon fiber composites and mold tooling, plastics, and wood.

Success Measures

• Delivery of high-quality prototype components and vehicle properties.

• Successful execution of complex machining projects from programming through final completion.

• Safe and reliable operation of CNC equipment.

• Organization and maintainability of CNC programs, CAD/CAM data, and fixture files.

• Effective technical support provided to the team.

• Adaptability across a wide range of materials, project types, and manufacturing challenges

• Strong and effective collaboration with Design, Engineering, Modeling, and Fabrication teams.

Salary Range: The compensation range for this position is specific to the locations listed below and is the range Lucid reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including job-related knowledge; skillset; experience, education and training; certifications; and other relevant business and organizational factors.

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. jobs.title: VP of Operations
jobs.description:
The role

You own how work gets scoped, staffed, and run at Movers+Shakers. That means four things: resourcing, the PMO, how we build our scopes, and the workflow our content moves through.

Movers+Shakers is a social-first creative agency tracking to grow revenue more than 50% in 2027. The work we do is strong and demand is high. What we are missing is an operator with a bird's-eye view of capacity, staffing, and margin, who sees problems 90 days out instead of the week they land.

This is a hands-on seat. You will lead the project managers and the resourcing team, and you will also be deep in the work itself… building scopes, reworking staffing plans, and standing up new client teams. We are not looking for someone to design an operating model from scratch. The foundations exist: we run on EOS, we have a PM team, a resourcing function, and a finance practice. Your job is to connect these pieces as one system and tighten what is loose.

• Reports to: Our Integrator

• Team: You will sit on our executive leadership team

• Leads: the Director of Project Management and the PM team, and the Associate Director of Resourcing

• Peers: Business Partnership (aka Account), Integrated Production, Creative, Finance, People, AI Leadership

What you'll own

1. Resourcing and capacity

• Lead the resourcing team and own who is staffed on what, across full-time staff and freelancers.

• Maintain a rolling 90-day capacity view of the agency, tied to the revenue forecast and the new business pipeline.

• Turn our revenue goals and projections into hiring requests early enough that we can recruit ahead of need (3-6 month time horizon).

• Make the calls on full-time versus freelance, with the margin impact visible.

2. The PMO

• Lead and develop our project managers.

• Hold one standard for how projects are planned, tracked, and reported, so any leader can see the health of any workstream.

• PMs own the project from kickoff to close-out. Integrated Production owns the production; your team owns the plan, the timeline, the budget, and the contribution margin planning.

3. Delivery Economics

• Strong partner to Finance to manage and execute on contribution margin targets for each Pod

• Run the scope-to-actuals learning loop: what we sold, the hours we delivered, and how we scope differently next time.

• Call it early when a workstream is over-servicing or under-staffed, and work the fix with the pod lead.

• Interpret, communicate, and provide actionable insights on the agency-wide view of contribution margin, resource capacity and P&L supported hiring plans to the Integrator

4. Scoping & team building

• You are the owner of how we build scopes: the staffing model, and the hours behind every new and existing scope, renewal, and pitch.

• Finance is your counterpart. You build the scope; together you make sure it ties to the rate card, margin goals, and the revenue forecast.

• Give the capacity and margin read on each new business opportunity before we decide to pursue it.

• Stand up the team for a new client win quickly, without pulling the floor out from under existing clients.

5. Workflow, tools, and the content supply chain

• Lead and champion the rollout of our content supply chain and Workfront integration: the connected AI-enabled workflow that moves content from brief to approval to publish.

• Partner with our head of Innovation and Technology on every technology and AI rollout. They choose and build the tools; you make them part of how each team works day to day.

• Bring them the operational problems worth solving with AI, and report back on what is actually being used.

• Own adoption of agency-wide workflow and project tools, and retire duplicate tools and manual steps as the new workflow takes hold.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

• The rolling 90-day capacity view is live and leadership uses it to decide which new business to pursue.

• Every active workstream has a current staff plan, and every pod lead has a margin view they trust.

• The PMO works from one project standard.

In your first year

• No surprise hiring: roles are requested from the forecast, months ahead of need.

• Every scope is built one way, and we can explain every gap between what we scoped and what we delivered.

• The content supply chain runs across all retainer clients.

• A new client team goes from signed scope to staffed and running in weeks.

Who you are

• 12+ years in agency operations, project management, or resourcing, in creative, social, or content agencies.

• You have run a PMO and a resourcing function at the same time, at an agency of 50 to 200 people that was growing fast.

• You have helped client leads move workstream margin, and you can tell us the number before and after.

• You build scopes and staff plans yourself. You are fluent in rate cards, utilization, and the full-time versus freelance trade-off.

• You have rolled out a workflow or project platform across an agency and can show the adoption numbers.

• You manage managers and still are deep in the work. Senior enough to lead the function, not too senior to live & breathe the spreadsheets.

• You use AI tools extensively in your own daily work and have a view on how they change agency workflow.

• You say the hard thing early, with the data, and you bring the joy while doing it.

• EOS experience is a plus.
