About the job

As the Director of Finance at Go Nimbly, you’ll own the financial operations that let our team grow with discipline. Reporting to our Director of Operations, you’ll be the primary finance partner for the business, responsible for FP&A and accounting, while building the systems and data foundation that make both run well.

This role suits someone who can work as both strategist and operator. You’ll partner with leadership on where the business is headed, and you’ll also own the monthly close and the forecast, and tie revenue targets, headcount, compensation, and margin into one view of the business. You’ll be a strong technologist who sees finance as a data problem as much as an accounting one, and who builds systems that scale.

You’ll lead and develop our finance and accounting team and collaborate closely with Operations, HR, and the leadership team.

Remote: Location Requirements

We’re a fully remote company. At this time, we are only able to hire candidates who reside in the following locations due to payroll, tax, and compliance requirements:

U.S. states: California, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah.

The Director of Finance will:

 - Lead FP&A end to end, including the annual financial plan, rolling forecasts, and scenario planning, translating revenue targets, hiring, compensation, and margin goals into models leadership can steer by.

 - Partner with Operations to turn utilization targets, capacity, and staffing assumptions into the financial forecast, and track the metrics that matter for a services business, including utilization, billing realization, project margin, pipeline-to-revenue conversion, and cash flow.

 - Prepare board materials, and present financial performance and key operating metrics to leadership and the wider company.

 - Model and administer the financial side of compensation and incentive plans, working with Operations and HR to keep them financially sound and easy for employees to understand.

 - Oversee accounting operations, including month-end close, revenue recognition, AP/AR, payroll coordination, audit readiness, and tax and compliance obligations.

 - Build and maintain the finance tech stack, including billing, expense, and reporting tools, and connect them so data flows cleanly between systems.

 - Develop dashboards, models, and automated reporting that reduce manual work and give leaders reliable answers quickly.

 - Partner with leadership on pricing, staffing models, hiring plans, and investment decisions, translating financial analysis into clear recommendations.

 - Manage banking, vendor, and insurance relationships, along with cash management and financial controls.

 - Review and manage customer contract terms, including pricing, payment terms, and revenue recognition implications, in partnership with Operations and Legal.

 - Document finance processes and policies so the function runs on systems rather than institutional knowledge.

 - Make sound judgment calls independently, escalating to the Director of Operations when the stakes or ambiguity call for it.

What’s in it for you?

 - Flexible working environment: our entire team works remotely, and we have no plans to change this!

 - Tiered incentive program (in addition to base salary) to reward high performers.

 - Gain exposure to several high-growth companies looking to scale and invest in their revenue operations function.

 - Colleagues who are top practitioners. Many Go Nimbly alumni now lead RevOps and GTM teams at high-growth companies!

 - Annual camp: a yearly offsite to celebrate the year and plan the next one.

 - Dedicated to employee development and career paths aimed at fostering your growth and your career.

 - 100% paid premiums for US employees’ insurance coverage.

About you

 - 10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, with at least 5 in a leadership role.

 - Hands-on depth across FP&A, accounting, and financial operations. You’ve owned these areas, not just supported them.

 - Experience building annual plans and forecasts, including modeling variable compensation and incentive structures.

 - Strong technical fluency. You’re comfortable with SQL or similar tools, BI platforms, and modern finance systems, and you’ve built models, pipelines, or automations yourself.

 - Experience in the back office of a professional services firm, with a working knowledge of utilization, project accounting, and services revenue recognition.

 - Demonstrated ability to operate autonomously: you know when to decide, when to consult, and when to escalate.

 - Excellent communication skills. You can explain financial concepts to non-finance leaders and turn analysis into clear recommendations.

 - Self-directed and accountable: you work proactively, communicate clearly, and close loops.

 - Comfortable working in a fully remote environment.

Bonus points if you:

 - Have built or supported a finance function at a scaling company

 - Have experience with multi-entity or multi-currency accounting, including international operations in EMEA or LATAM

 - Hold a CPA or MBA

As a remote first team, we rely on video calls to stay connected, make decisions, and work directly with clients, so being comfortable on camera and engaged in that setting is part of how we operate day to day.

About Us

We are positive people who have a sense of urgency, creativity, and decisiveness coupled with the willingness to work hard and well under pressure

 - Be a Leader. Leadership at Go Nimbly isn't about title, it's showing up with a point of view, saying the hard thing clearly, and making sure what you started actually lands.

 - Show Your Work. We love a finished product, but how you got there matters too. Clear communication and proactive updates are part of the job.

 - Value Long-Term Over Short-Term. The fast answer and the right answer aren't always the same. We're committed to building things that scale, even when that means slowing down.

 - Take It to the Finish Line. We don't hand things off and hope for the best. When you own something here, you own it all the way through.

 - Customer-Obsessed. When our clients win, we win. We genuinely understand their business and show up as trusted advisors, as invested in their outcomes as they are.

 - Gotchu Energy. The best teammates make the people around them feel like they've got backup, leaning into hard moments instead of away from them.

What’s next?

Apply! A real person on our Talent team reads every application. If we'd like to talk, we'll reach out. If not, we'll let you know that too, with clear feedback. Nobody likes being ghosted.

On the first call, our Talent team will walk you through the interview process. It varies by role and usually includes three to four rounds. We want to use everyone's time well and figure out together whether this is a good fit.

The base salary range for this role is $170,000 to $190,000 USD. 

Initial placement within the range depends on geographic location, experience, and skillset, with most hires landing at or near the midpoint, leaving room for growth and future impact. The top of the range is generally reserved for those who are performing at a high level and impact here at Go Nimbly. Final offer amounts will vary based on leveling, and will be adjusted based on geographical location and the candidate's applicable experience and skillset.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer II, Inference
jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About the Team

Senior engineers are area owners who lead designs, raise engineering standards, and deliver measurable improvements to latency, throughput, and reliability across multiple services. You'll partner with product, orchestration, and hardware teams to evolve our Kubernetes-native inference platform and meet strict P99 SLAs at scale.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead design reviews and drive architecture within the team; decompose multi-service work into clear milestones.

• Define and own SLIs/SLOs; ensure post-incident actions land and reliability improves release-over-release.

• Implement advanced optimizations (e.g., micro-batch schedulers, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse) and quantify impact.

• Mentor IC1/IC2 engineers; review cross-team designs and elevate coding/testing standards.

• Strong coding in Python or Go (C++ a plus) and deep familiarity with networked systems and performance.

• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes at production scale, CI/CD, and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry).

• Practical knowledge of inference internals: batching, caching, mixed precision (BF16/FP8), streaming token delivery.

• Proven track record improving tail latency (P95/P99) and service reliability through metrics-driven work.

jobs.title: Director: Integrated Care
jobs.description:
ATI Advisory is a healthcare research and advisory services firm changing how businesses, communities, and public programs serve complex populations. We deliver insight backed by original research and provide practical solutions for our clients and the families they serve. Our team includes nationally recognized experts across Medicare, Medicaid, long-term care, and provider delivery, and we bring an influential voice to efforts transforming health care.

For more information, visit www.atiadvisory.com.

The Role

ATI Advisory’s Payer Strategy and Program Design Practice helps states and health plans design and run Medicaid and Medicare programs. Our state work serves Medicaid agencies, the partner agencies that serve older adults and people with disabilities, and healthcare foundations on Medicaid policy, Medicare-Medicaid integration, and other state health policy issues.

The Director serves as project lead on state technical assistance and advisory engagements and is the primary contact for the client’s project lead. They bring a systems-level view of how Medicare and Medicaid intersect, with recommendations that fit each state’s goals, fiscal pressures, and how its government works. The Director reports to a Managing Director and works under an executive sponsor on each engagement.

What You’ll Do

Project Delivery

• Lead state engagements. Serve as project lead on multi-year technical assistance and advisory engagements for state Medicaid agencies and their partner agencies, from assessing program options through design, implementation, and oversight. Manage scope, budget, timeline, and deliverable quality as state priorities shift.

• Bring Medicare-Medicaid expertise. Advise on how traditional Medicare, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid interact for dual eligible individuals, including dual eligible special needs plan (D-SNP) contracting, aligned enrollment, and Medicaid managed care procurements.

Client Services

• Be the client’s trusted lead. Turn state priorities into clear recommendations for senior officials, and bring needs outside the current scope to the executive sponsor.

• Build relationships across stakeholders. Work with state agencies, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), health plans, providers, and enrollees and their families. Help health plans and other clients understand state policy and respond to it.

Business Development

• Support new work. Partner with the executive sponsor on proposals and scopes for new and expanded state work.

• Contribute to thought leadership. Write and present on state approaches to integration and Medicaid program design at conferences, expert workgroups, and national forums.

People Development and Operations

• Grow policy experts. Lead project teams of policy experts and analysts, and coach them to become subject matter experts and client advisors.

• Uphold operating standards. Keep project budgets, project management tools, and client relationship management (CRM) records current, and improve processes through project retrospectives.

What We’re Looking For

• At least 10 years of experience in Medicaid or Medicare policy, including work on integrated care for dual eligible individuals. Experience leading or advising state Medicaid agencies or health plans is strongly preferred.

• Deep knowledge of how Medicare and Medicaid interact, including Medicare Advantage plan operations.

• Experience designing, implementing, or overseeing integrated care or Medicaid programs.

• An understanding of how state government works, including budgets, procurement, and federal approvals.

• Experience as project lead on multi-year engagements, including leading project teams.

jobs.title: Payload Integration Engineer
jobs.description:
Why the Stratosphere?

From first principles, it is the obvious place to build. Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites move rapidly hundreds of kilometers above Earth. Our vision is an autonomous solar-powered bird operating around 20 kilometers, or 65,000 ft, above most clouds and weather. Much closer to Earth. Persistent by flying in circles. Effectively a Cell Tower in the Sky. That persistence is priceless. That is the promise of Skylink.

Start small. Build upward.

The first product of Icarus is a small, affordable solar-powered Stratospheric bird. A platform designed to be light, simple, and built under constraints. Affordability is the foundation. More importantly, it solves a real use case now. A wedge into the market through intelligence and communications. A beachhead that proves the model, attracts customers who need it so badly they’ll use it even before it’s perfect, and opens the path to market disruption at scale.

The vision: Skylink

The vision goes further than building one plane or even one fleet. The goal is Skylink: a persistent Stratospheric grid delivering continuous intelligence, uninterrupted communications, and global connectivity. A new layer of infrastructure. The next backbone of how we see, sense, and connect the world.

Our mission at Icarus is to re-establish and maintain dominance in the Stratosphere. We asked ourselves: what is the fastest and best way to execute this? The answer was not to start with a massive, billion-dollar program. It was to start with affordable birds, scale endurance step by step, and build upward into Skylink.

The Payload Integration Engineer owns end-to-end integration of small payloads onto Icarus aircraft. You turn mission needs into clear requirements, determine which payloads belong on the aircraft, and take them from concept through installation, ground test, and flight test. Mission fit comes first. If a payload does not meet the requirements, you make that clear and recommend the right go/no-go decision.

Reports to: Avionics Lead

Mission

Re-establish and maintain dominance in the Stratosphere.

Levels

We are hiring at Level I, Level II, and Level III through this posting. Your level will be determined during the interview process based on your technical skills, relevant experience, and demonstrated scope of ownership.

What you’ll do

• Translate mission requirements into payload and interface requirements across mechanical, electrical, power, and data/comms systems.

• Evaluate and down-select candidate payloads for mission fit, and recommend go/no-go.

• Own integration from concept through design, installation, ground test, and flight test.

• Work closely with electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and product to define interfaces and resolve integration issues.

• Maintain interface control documents and integration plans, and verify that requirements are met.

What we’re looking for

• Evidence that you can translate a mission need into clear, testable requirements.

• Hands-on integration ability across mechanical, electrical, power, and data interfaces.

• Sound engineering judgment when evaluating payload tradeoffs and mission fit.

• Ability to own integration issues through design, installation, testing, and verification.

• Clear technical documentation and communication across engineering and product teams.

Why Icarus

• Meaningful equity

• Top market salary and bonuses

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Factory in El Segundo

• Real ownership, real hardware, real flight

• Small team, massive responsibility

• High signal (engineering) to noise (management) culture

• Dream desk setup

• Daily lunch

• Unlimited celsius

This is not a normal engineering job

We are pioneers, not corporate managers. Engineering, flight, and execution matter more than process, politics, or management overhead. You will own your work end to end: define it, build it, test it, fix it, and prove it in flight. We expect extreme ownership, clear judgment, and an obsession with quality and speed.

No tourists. No bystanders. Only builders.

Hiring process

• Phone screen with the hiring manager via Microsoft Teams

• Onsite presentation and panel Q&A

US salary range

• Level I: $100,000 - $140,000 USD per year

• Level II: $140,000 - $180,000 USD per year

• Level III: $180,000 - $220,000 USD per year

These ranges reflect annual base salary. Final level and base salary will be determined individually based on relevant skills, experience, and the scope of responsibility. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are considered part of Icarus' total compensation package.

jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking to hire a highly skilled Mechanical Engineer for the Data Center and Mission Critical team for our east region. Although the position is primarily remote periodic travel may be required for client meetings, key project milestones, onsite collaboration sessions, or other business‑critical activities. Travel is expected to be occasional and scheduled in advance.

AECOM is a leader in the global data center consulting industry with robust teams in the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.  In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with our teams around the world on high-profile, fast-paced data center projects for global clients.  This is a hands-on, client-facing role with an opportunity for upward career mobility.

Responsibilities, required experience, and qualifications are summarized below:

Responsibilities:

• Data Center Heat Rejection and HVAC System Design: Developing and designing Heat Rejection and HVAC systems specifically tailored for data centers, considering factors such as type of cooling requirement as air cooled or direct fluid cooled, associated cooling loads, future flexibility of the system to accommodate variable heat distribution scenarios, phased construction and operation, airflow management, humidity control, system redundancy providing concurrent maintainability, energy efficiency, and compliance with industry standards and best practices.
• Cooling System Selection: Selecting appropriate air/water side cooling systems for data centers, including Fan wall units, computer room air handlers (CRAHs), chilled water systems, DX systems and CRAC units, in-row cooling, and containment solutions, based on the specific cooling requirements of the data center and the criticality of the equipment.
• Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) Analysis: Conducting internal CFD simulations to optimize airflow distribution, transient period analysis, identify hotspots, and ensure efficient cooling throughout the data center. Conducting external CFD on individual buildings and/or campus-wide to simulate effects of different electrical and mechanical components on each other and effects on design day selection criteria capacity of each component. For both types, prepare and/or direct preparation of models and analyse the results to recommend design modifications and optimize the Heat rejection and HVAC system performance. Coordinate the required changes and resulting effects with other trades on project.
• Redundancy and Fault Tolerance: Designing HVAC systems with redundancy and fault-tolerant features to ensure continuous operation of the data center in the event of equipment failure or maintenance activities. This includes the design of backup cooling systems, automatic switchover mechanisms, and monitoring systems.
• Heat Load Calculation and Capacity Planning: Performing heat load calculations for data centers to determine the cooling requirements based on the IT equipment, power density, anticipated growth, and phasing of the construction and operational steps. Conducting capacity planning to ensure the HVAC system can accommodate future expansions and upgrades. Performing HVAC loads for admin and common sections of the facility.
• Energy Efficiency and Sustainability: Implementing energy-efficient HVAC design strategies, such as utilizing economizers, variable speed drives, energy recovery systems, and optimizing airflow management techniques, to minimize energy consumption and support sustainability initiatives.
• Air Quality and Filtration: Ensuring the data center's air quality is maintained at optimal levels by designing appropriate filtration systems and implementing air quality monitoring mechanisms. Addressing concerns related to particulate matter, humidity control, and contaminant removal to protect sensitive IT equipment.
• Coordination with Electrical and Mechanical Systems: Collaborating with electrical engineers and mechanical engineers to integrate the heat rejection and HVAC system seamlessly with the electrical infrastructure, UPS systems, emergency power systems, fire suppression systems, and other critical infrastructure components.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's Degree with 6+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and or education.
• Experience in data center mechanical and electrical equipment installation and operation.
• P. E. registration is required

Preferred Qualifications:

• A bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, HVAC engineering, or a related field from an accredited university is typically required. Preference would be given to candidates with a master's degree or advanced coursework in HVAC systems or energy management.
• Knowledge of data center TER Standard Topology as per Uptime Institute, TIA 942, ANSI/BICSI 002
• Professional certifications related to HVAC engineering, such as Certified Energy Manager (CEM), Building Energy Modeling Professional (BEMP), or Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) accreditation, would be advantageous.

• Relocation is not available for this position
• Sponsorship for US Employment Authorization is not available for this role now or in the future.

At Rothy’s, building a sustainable future is at the heart of everything we do. We pride ourselves on fostering an inclusive environment at our HQ, retail stores and wholly-owned factory, and are growing our community every day.

Together, the members of our People & Workplace team make up the most well-versed employee directory you can imagine. From the moment a candidate is interested in working with us until the day they celebrate their first anniversary, and well beyond, this team is working behind the scenes to ensure everything is smooth sailing. From benefits questions to employee engagement and building community, these team members are true Rothy’s champions.

About the role:

As our Senior Manager, Total Rewards, you’ll shape how Rothy’s pays, recognizes and cares for our people across our HQ and growing retail fleet. You’ll own the strategy, design and delivery of our compensation, benefits and recognition programs; making sure they’re competitive, equitable, compliant and easy to understand. You’ll partner closely within the People Team and Finance, bringing market insights and clear, data-informed recommendations to evolve our practices as the company evolves.

What you’ll do:

Compensation & Benefits

 - Bring structure, consistency, and scalability to equity practices, support program administration, and help employees understand how equity fits within the broader total rewards picture

 - Lead the annual merit, promotion and bonus cycles end to end, from budget modeling with Finance to manager guidance, calibration support and employee communication

 - Own benefits strategy and plan design, including broker and carrier relationships, annual renewals and open enrollment, with a focus on value and a great employee experience

 - Manage our 401(k) plan in partnership with Finance and plan providers, including vendor management and annual compliance testing

 - Design and manage recognition and incentive programs

 - Ensure total rewards programs meet federal, state and local requirements across our multi-state footprint

 - Partner with Finance on compensation and benefits budgeting, forecasting and cost modeling

 - Partner with People Operations to ensure compensation and benefits data is accurate in our HRIS, and build reporting and dashboards that support decision making

 - Analyze compensation data and trends to assess program effectiveness, identify gaps and opportunities, and support business decisions

 - Translate complex compensation data and market trends into actionable recommendations for executive leadership

 - Develop tools, guidelines and resources that help managers make informed compensation decisions, and improve employee understanding of our compensation and total rewards programs



Leave of Absence Administration

 

 - Administer all leave and accommodation programs and policies, including but not limited to FMLA, ADA, and state specific leave and disability programs

 - Ensure all leave programs and policies are efficiently and accurately administered, ensuring compliance with all applicable federal and state laws

 - Serve as the point of contact for employees, managers, and HR inquiries regarding leaves of absence and workplace accommodations.

 - Develop tools and resources to help employees and managers understand and navigate leaves of absence and workplace accommodations.

 - Manage workers’ compensation claims



You are:

 - A strategic thinker who sees where market trends are heading and turns insight into clear recommendations and action plans

 - Highly analytical and detail oriented, able to bring together complex data to create new insights and levels of understanding

 - A trusted advisor who builds credibility with senior leaders and influences through data and thoughtful storytelling

 - A clear communicator who can make complex programs simple and approachable for any audience, from executives to store teams

 - Grounded in fairness and equity, with sound judgment and the discretion to handle highly confidential information

 - A builder who enjoys creating scalable programs, policies and frameworks from the ground up

 - Collaborative and solutions oriented, ready to roll up your sleeves in a fast-paced, growing company

 - Excited to embrace possibility and question the status quo to find better ways of doing things



You have:

 - Progressive experience in compensation and benefits, including ownership of total rewards programs in a high-growth, multi-state environment

 - Deep expertise in compensation design, job architecture, market pricing and pay equity analysis

 - Hands-on experience managing benefits programs, broker and carrier relationships, renewals and open enrollment

 - Strong working knowledge of total rewards compliance, including FLSA, ACA, ERISA, COBRA and state pay transparency laws (California experience a plus)

 - Advanced knowledge of leave of absence laws and regulations, including FMLA, ADA, and state specific leave laws

jobs.title: Temporary Senior Recruiter - Eataly Flatiron
jobs.description:
Temporary Senior Recruiter - Eataly Flatiron

3-Month Temporary Assignment

Job Overview

The Temporary Senior Recruiter - Eataly Flatiron will play a critical role in strengthening the store's leadership team by identifying, attracting, and securing exceptional talent across Eataly's dynamic retail and hospitality operations. This is a three-month temporary assignment focused on driving full-cycle recruitment for senior-level and management positions, supporting immediate hiring priorities, and ensuring the store has the leadership talent needed to maintain operational excellence and deliver exceptional guest experience.

Working closely with the Store Director, department leaders, and the Talent & Culture team, this role will take a hands-on, results-driven approach to managing recruitment efforts from initial sourcing through offer acceptance. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in hospitality and retail recruitment, the ability to quickly build relationships and understand business needs, and the ability to manage multiple searches in a fast-paced environment. Success in this role will be measured by the ability to accelerate hiring, build strong candidate pipelines, and deliver high-quality talent within the assignment period.

Responsibilities

• Leads full-cycle recruitment for senior-level and management positions, including operational leadership roles within Retail, Restaurants, Caffè, Culinary, and other store departments as needed.
• Partners closely with the Store Director, department leaders, and Talent & Culture to understand immediate business needs, establish hiring priorities, and execute targeted recruitment strategies.
• Manages all stages of the recruitment process, including job intake meetings, sourcing, candidate screening, interviewing, selection, offer negotiation, and closing.
• Proactively sources and engages qualified candidates through networking, referrals, industry connections, online platforms, and targeted outreach to generate strong candidate pipelines.
• Prioritizes critical and time-sensitive vacancies, maintaining momentum across multiple searches and driving recruitment processes forward to meet hiring objectives.
• Provides hiring managers with market insights, candidate availability, compensation expectations, and regular recruitment updates to support timely hiring decisions.
• Ensures a consistent, professional, and engaging candidate experience that reflects Eataly's employer brand, culture, and values.
• Builds and leverages relationships with external recruitment partners, hospitality networks, and industry organizations to support immediate hiring needs.
• Maintains accurate and timely candidate records, recruitment activity, and hiring documentation within the Applicant Tracking System, ensuring compliance with company standards and applicable employment laws.
• Tracks recruitment progress, hiring activity, and key metrics to provide visibility into open positions, identify potential roadblocks, and support effective hiring outcomes.
• Coordinates with store leadership and People Operations to support the onboarding and transition of newly hired leaders.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

Job Requirements

• This is a three-month temporary assignment based at Eataly Flatiron in New York City.
• Requires regular in-person presence within the store to build relationships with leadership teams, understand operational needs, and support recruitment activities.
• Must be able to manage a fast-paced recruitment workload and prioritize hiring needs throughout the assignment period.

Qualifications

• 6+ years of talent acquisition experience, preferably within hospitality, food service, retail, or other multi-department operational environments.
• Demonstrated experience recruiting senior-level, management, and leadership positions, ideally within a high-volume, multi-department organization.
• Strong understanding of hospitality and retail operations, organizational structures, and leadership hiring needs.
• Proven ability to quickly develop and execute effective sourcing strategies and identify qualified candidates for hard-to-fill positions.
• Experience managing multiple searches simultaneously while balancing competing priorities and tight deadlines.
• Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and advise hiring managers at all levels.
• Knowledge of Applicant Tracking Systems and modern recruitment technologies.
• Excellent communication, interviewing, negotiation, and candidate assessment skills.
• Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and follow-through.
• Ability to work independently with a high degree of accountability and adapt quickly to changing business needs.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Annual Salary Range: $85,000 – $95,000

Eataly is an equal employment opportunity employer. It is the Company’s policy to not unlawfully discriminate against any applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability or any other characteristic made unlawful to consider by applicable federal, state, or local laws. Eataly also prohibits harassment of applicants and employees based on any of these protected categories. It is also Eataly’s policy to comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws regarding consideration of unemployment status, salary history, credit/bankruptcy history and criminal background/conviction history in making hiring decisions.  If contacted for an employment opportunity, please advise Human Resources if you require accommodation.

Our Acute Behavioral Services (ABS) group homes support individuals with complex mental health and behavioral needs. Many of the people we serve have experienced frequent crises, hospital stays, or legal involvement. They may have a history of failed placements and need a highly structured environment to succeed.

Our homes are specially designed for safety, and our approach is consistent, person-centered, and focused on helping individuals reach their goals while maintaining safety for everyone. • Accurately document services, behavioral observations, health concerns, and program activities using electronic systems (T‑logs, Therap, health tracking).
• Monitor behavioral changes, identify escalation indicators, and communicate proactively with supervisors and team members during crisis or safety situations.
• Support family and personal contacts, assist with appointments, medication administration tasks (as allowed), and follow all medical and nutrition plans.
• Participate in team meetings, provide feedback on individuals’ needs, and assist in training new staff while modeling positive, professional behavior.

Required (Must-Have)

• High school diploma or GED
• 3 years minimum of experience working with individuals with chronic and severe mental illness OR a degree in a mental-health–related field
• Must be at least 18 years of age; some programs require employees to be 21 years of age or older
• Valid driver’s license and proof of auto insurance
• Basic computer skills and ability to use electronic documentation systems

Physical Requirements

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods
• Ability to safely manage physically demanding situations

Skills & Abilities

• Follow behavior support plans, treatment plans, functional assessments, and person-centered plans
• Use crisis prevention, de-escalation, redirection, and manual restraints as trained
• Communicate clearly and professionally in writing and verbally, including documentation
• Work effectively in crisis situations and exercise sound judgment

jobs.title: Head of Community Relations
jobs.description:
About Cantina:

Cantina Labs is a social AI company, developing a suite of advanced real-time models that push the boundaries of expression, personality, and realism. We bring characters to life, transforming how people tell stories, connect, and create. We build and power ecosystems. Cantina, our flagship social AI platform, is just the beginning.

If you're excited about the potential AI has to shape human creativity and social interactions, join us in building the future!



About the Role:

We’re hiring a Head of Community Relations to build Cantina’s relationships with the AI filmmakers, character builders and creators shaping this medium. Their work will be central to how Cantina is introduced to the world and to how people discover and learn to use it afterward. 

You’ll build a program that gives creators good reasons to keep making work here: access to the team, useful tools, paid opportunities and recognition. You’ll also hire and lead the five-person team needed to run it.



Three things are essential:

 - You love AI video. You have a current portfolio, understand the production workflow and can discuss the strengths and limits of the tools you use.

 - You already belong to this community. X is where this community gathers and where Cantina’s community work will be concentrated. You have an established presence in the AI video conversation on X and relationships with creators who trust you. You know whose work matters and can explain why.

 - You have built and scaled a creator program. You have managed budgets, incentives, payments and program rules, and led a program from dozens of participants to hundreds or thousands. You can show what the program produced and provide references from creators who took part.



What else you bring:

You have hired and managed people, organized creator events, run a Discord at scale, and handled contracts, payments and support. You follow through on commitments, communicate candidly when plans change and exercise sound judgment about paid promotion. Experience in a game-studio creator program, creator marketplace or revenue-sharing model is useful, as is another language spoken in a major AI video community.



What you will lead: 

 - Creator relationships. Help us build out the AI video and creator ecosystem around Cantina. Establish who are our Tier 1 creators and give them early access, credits and clear briefs while preserving their own voices. Establish a Creator Council and a direct working relationship with Product. The measure is simple: priority creators make their best work on Cantina, publish it first and in their own voices on X / YouTube, etc and keep doing so weekly. Earn that through the quality of the experience and the opportunities you deliver.

 - Community programs. X is the center of the program. Lead Cantina’s participation in the AI video conversation there: daily presence, substantive replies, surfacing creator work to the company account, regular Spaces and office hours, and the steady build of the company and executive accounts ahead of launch. Make Discord a useful home for support, learning and sharing work, with showcases and challenges that feed back onto X. Bring creators together at a launch gathering, meetups and relevant festivals. You should be comfortable hosting, appearing on camera and representing Cantina in person.

 - Creator incentives and opportunities. Design and run the Creator Fund, including payments based on eligible views after content review, a clear rate card, bonuses, credits, commissions and grants. Make recognition tangible through creator credit, spotlights and agreed distribution opportunities. You own the Fund and its budget, working with Growth on economics, Partnerships on talent agreements and Trust and Safety on review standards. Paid work must be disclosed, artificial engagement excluded, and payouts and promised opportunities delivered reliably.

 - Creator education. Build a useful library of tutorials and demonstrations with the education lead and commissioned creators. For meaningful releases, coordinate early creator access and aim to publish a demonstration and lesson within 24 hours. Show work that an ordinary user can reproduce in Cantina. Explain the process and disclose unusually involved workflows so viewers understand what the result requires.

 - Creator feedback. Bring Product a weekly, prioritized account of what creators need. Agree which improvements to pursue, explain decisions to the community and credit the people whose feedback shaped the work. Maintain a visible record of requests, decisions and delivery.



The team and your partners: 

 - You’ll recruit and lead a team covering X community relations; Discord and in-app community; creator education; creator-program operations; and program coordination. The team will handle daily relationships, education, reviews, payments and administration, with clear responsibilities and a shared calendar.

 - You’ll work closely with Social on publishing creator work and with Partnerships on talent and commercial relationships. Growth owns paid acquisition; Marketing owns brand, press and the company narrative; Trust and Safety sets policy. Your responsibility is to make the creator program work across those teams.



What success looks like:

We’ll agree your first-90-day milestones against your start date and the launch work already underway. The initial priorities are:

 - Community setup. Map the priority relationships, onboard the first forty creators, set up Discord and a reliable community calendar, convene the Council, and agree the incentive program’s rules and rate card.

 - Creator participation. Build toward one hundred onboarded creators, with launch goals of seventy publishing and thirty sharing a tutorial or completed piece. Establish the tutorial library, begin reviewed payouts and bring the first two community hires into the team.

 - Program growth. Work toward, weekly publishing by priority creators, a forty-lesson education library and the full team in place. Work with Product to deliver three agreed creator-requested improvements and credit the people whose feedback shaped them. Measure creator participation and retention, the quality and frequency of published work, creator posts on X mentioning Cantina each week, the share of launch-week attention coming from community accounts rather than company accounts, education output, Discord activity and referred registrations. Report program costs alongside results, including cost per creator-published piece and per referred registration.



Compensation:

The anticipated annual base salary range for this role is between $200,000-$250,000. When determining compensation, a number of factors will be considered, including skills, experience, job scope, location, and competitive compensation market data.



Benefits: 

 - Competitive salary and generous company equity

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance – 99.99% of premiums covered by Cantina

 - 42 days of paid time off, including:
   
   - 15 PTO days
   
   - 10 sick days
   
   - 15 company holidays
   
   - 2 floating holidays

 - Generous parental leave & fertility support

 - 401(k) retirement savings plan

 - Lifestyle spending account – $500/month to use however you’d like

 - Complimentary lunch and snacks for in-office employees

 - One Medical membership, and more!

jobs.title: Meteorologist
jobs.location: Chicago, Illinois, United States; London, United Kingdom; New York, NY, United States
jobs.description:
Hudson River Trading (HRT) is seeking a Meteorologist to help build our weather data and analytics capability from the ground up, supporting trading in U.S. the natural gas and power markets. As the team's primary weather expert, you will shape what datasets we build, how we measure forecast quality, and how weather insight becomes a trading signal.

You will partner directly with researchers to build commercially relevant weather forecasts for systematic and fundamental strategies, working alongside data engineers who own the pipelines and infrastructure.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the subject matter expert for meteorology, providing weather analysis and guidance to research and trading teams

• Define requirements for weather datasets and analytical tools, partnering with data engineers to prioritize development and validate outputs

• Develop and maintain climatology and anomaly products, ensuring consistent definitions and reliable data quality

• Establish and lead forecast verification, evaluating the accuracy and limitations of models and data providers across seasons and weather conditions

• Lead tropical weather analysis during hurricane season, communicating potential impacts on energy infrastructure, supply, and demand

• Evaluate new weather data sources, vendors, and emerging forecasting technologies, and contribute to the team's development roadmap

• Investigate significant weather events and provide timely analysis, clearly communicating forecast uncertainty to technical and nontechnical stakeholders

• Help recruit, onboard, and mentor additional meteorologists as the team grows

Qualifications

• An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in Meteorology or Atmospheric Science (or equivalent)

• 6+ years of forecasting experience in energy, commodities, utilities, or another weather-sensitive industry; strong candidates with 4–6 years and direct energy-market experience will be considered

• Deep knowledge of global and regional NWP and ensemble systems, including biases and forecast limitations

• Proficiency analyzing gridded data (GRIB/NetCDF) in Python (xarray, pandas, or similar technologies) and define requirements for engineers

• Ability to collaborate with quantitative teams and communicate meteorological insights, including explaining uncertainty and defending forecasts

• Experience leading forecast verification and evidence-based model evaluation

• Hands-on experience developing climatologies and anomaly products

• Familiarity with evaluating AI/ML weather models against traditional NWP

• A background in tropical forecasting or hurricane response

• Knowledge of U.S. power markets and natural gas fundamentals

• Exposure to systematic or fundamental trading strategies

• A history of mentoring or leading meteorologists

• Cloud data platform or SQL proficiency

• AMS Certified Consulting Meteorologist (CCM) or similar credential

The estimated base salary range for this position is 200,000 to 300,000 USD per year (or local equivalent). The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role will also be eligible for discretionary performance-based bonuses and a competitive benefits package.

Culture

Hudson River Trading (HRT) brings a scientific approach to trading financial products. We have built one of the world's most sophisticated computing environments for research and development. Our researchers are at the forefront of innovation in the world of algorithmic trading.

At HRT we welcome a variety of expertise: mathematics and computer science, physics and engineering, media and tech. We’re a community of self-starters who are motivated by the excitement of being at the cutting edge of automation in every part of our organization—from trading, to business operations, to recruiting and beyond. We value openness and transparency, and celebrate great ideas from HRT veterans and new hires alike. At HRT we’re friends and colleagues – whether we are sharing a meal, playing the latest board game, or writing elegant code. We embrace a culture of togetherness that extends far beyond the walls of our office.

Feel like you belong at HRT? Our goal is to find the best people and bring them together to do great work in a place where everyone is valued. HRT is proud of our diverse staff; we have offices all over the globe and benefit from our varied and unique perspectives. HRT is an equal opportunity employer; so whoever you are we’d love to get to know you.

We employ various methods to evaluate the authenticity of candidate responses. If we determine that AI assistance was used by an applicant during an interview or an assessment, we reserve the right to immediately end the interview or assessment, disqualify the applicant’s candidacy and/or rescind any job offers extended.

You can review our Global Applicant Privacy Notice, which explains how we process applicant information.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Lead (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, tech leads combine hands-on technical expertise with leadership across multiple teams. They set direction, guide engineering practices, and create the conditions for technical delivery that is secure, resilient, and scalable.

We’re building a modernized Team Awareness Kit (TAK) application for the U.S. Air Force that works in a decentralized communications environment. The first release centers on push-to-talk with auto-transcribed transmission logs, secure direct and group messaging, offline maps, and user registration and login. The work may expand into other projects in the same portfolio. It’s full end-to-end product delivery for a tactical user base.

You’ll set the technical direction for mapping and communication mobile apps that have to keep working when the network doesn’t, and you’ll stay hands-on in the code while you do it.

What to know going in

You’ll join an existing team that’s already building and shipping. The team relies on AI-assisted, spec-driven development, so you should be comfortable working that way and holding the output to a high bar. You’ll manage two software engineers to start.

In this role, you’ll also serve as a people manager. As a manager, you’ll keep growing in your craft and contributing to client work, while also taking on responsibility for the people you manage — their development, their performance, and the conditions that help them do their best work.

What you’ll do

• Lead technical delivery of mobile and backend software for tactical users, from architecture decisions through implementation and code review

• Build secure applications that stay useful on degraded or disconnected networks, including real-time voice, messaging, and offline maps

• Partner with product, design, and platform and security teams to resolve dependencies and explain technical tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Shape how the team uses AI-assisted development, pairing spec-driven practices with independent verification, automated testing, and security review

• Build strong working relationships with the people you manage and actively support their development

• Coach individuals through growth, feedback, and day-to-day challenges

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

• Hands-on technical leadership of complex software delivery, including architecture decisions, implementation, code reviews, and mentoring engineers

• Full-stack delivery across modern frontend or mobile applications, backend services, APIs, and relational databases, including becoming productive in unfamiliar languages and frameworks

• Experience with distributed systems, real-time or asynchronous communication, and integration with external systems

• Secure application development, including authentication, authorization, encryption, and secrets management, along with cloud or container deployment and CI/CD

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools with independent verification, testing, and security review

• Can produce high-quality code by adhering to good practices such as automated testing

• Understand the importance of always putting users at the center of your work, including thinking through the impact and implications of any code that you write

• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery

• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

• Experience with Flutter and Dart, Go, PostgreSQL, SQLite, WebSockets, or WebRTC

• Experience with geospatial applications, mapping, offline-first operation, or software for degraded or disconnected networks

• Experience with AWS, Kubernetes (EKS), Helm, Argo CD, Terraform, Crossplane, or GitHub Actions

• Experience delivering defense or regulated systems, including STIGs, RMF and ATO processes, CAC and PKI, or mTLS, plus familiarity with TAK and Cursor on Target (CoT) interoperability

• Experience improving AI-assisted engineering workflows, such as specification-driven development, agent orchestration, automated testing, or review automation

• Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

• Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.

• All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.

• This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment.

• You must be able to obtain and maintain a Common Access Card (CAC) and any special access the contract requires.

• You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role may require occasional travel to Montgomery, Alabama, and other U.S. Air Force bases.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Software Engineer at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

• Associate Software Engineer: $90,000–$125,000

• Software Engineer I: $120,000–$140,000

• Software Engineer II: $135,000–$160,000

• Senior Software Engineer: $150,000–$185,000

• Staff Software Engineer: $170,000–$203,000

• Principal Software Engineer: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

• Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance

• Short-term and long-term disability insurance

• Life and AD&D insurance

• Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account

• Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period

• Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays

• Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents

• Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options

• Business development / sales bonuses

• Referral bonuses

• Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development

• Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases

• Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)

• Flexible, remote-friendly work environment

• An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

• Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.

• Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.

• Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

jobs.title: Manager of Special Education Legal Compliance
jobs.description:
The Manager of Special Education Legal Compliance serves as a critical support to special education, faculty and school leaders, providing guidance in the areas of compliance and student data systems. This role collaborates closely with state-level staff, regional curriculum teams, and school-based personnel to ensure the delivery of high-quality, individualized educational programs for students with diverse learning needs. By supporting effective teaching practices, ensuring adherence to legal and instructional standards, and ensuring compliance with IDEA and Texas State Education Law & Regulations, Section 504 Law & Regulations,  the Special Education Manager of Legal Compliance helps advance the mission of KIPP Texas Public Schools—ensuring that every student has the tools and supportive environment necessary to thrive.

The Manager of Special Education Legal Compliance is responsible for leading and coordinating statewide systems that ensure legal and regulatory compliance, operational excellence, and equitable access to services for students with disabilities across KIPP Texas. This role oversees special education enrollment and records transfer, PEIMS reporting, TEA Complaints, Critical Cases, State Performance Plan Indicators and audits.  This leader builds efficient processes to meet IDEA, Section 504, and state compliance requirements while promoting high-quality services and support for students, families, and campus teams.

• Strategy | Support the strategic vision to ensure that KTX school and regional teams implement the Special Education Strategic Plan and provide comprehensive improvement of school performance using a collaborative approach to clear and specific performance targets aligned to the Special Education Strategic Plan and execute, monitor, edit strategic plans, annual goals and quarterly benchmarking for departmental improvement.

• Communication | Assists the Senior Director of compliance in ensuring KTX special populations teams are provided excellent communication, customer service and well-coordinated support.

• Legal Framework & Compliance | Possess experience and knowledge of IDEA and Texas State Education Law & Regulations, Section 504 Law & Regulations and understanding of the essential elements of high performing MTSS systems and structures.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Special Education Enrollment & Records Compliance

• Lead and manage standardized procedures for identifying, enrolling, and tracking students with disabilities, ensuring adherence to IDEA and TEA timelines.
• Oversee transfer of special education records and coordinate timelines for ARD/IEP implementation and evaluation.
• Ensure accurate and timely communication with campus, regional, and network stakeholders to guarantee continuity of FAPE. Support placement decisions in collaboration with regional teams for students requiring self-contained or low-incidence programming.

Data Analysis and Improvement

• Analyze school data including MTSS, 504, and ARD compliance to inform school based support and assistance.
• Analyze student data, to inform compliance decisions and interventions.
• Recognize patterns in student performance data and make recommendations for professional development and instructional improvements.
• Use data to identify and support the academic needs of special education students.

Stakeholder Engagement

Professional Development

PEIMS & Data Compliance

• Implement data validation and monitoring systems to prevent compliance risks and funding loss.

COMPETENCY AND SKILLS:

jobs.description:

The IT Technician is responsible for routine diagnostic and maintenance tasks and for early identification of problems. This position works from Magnolia Headquarters in Waco, Texas. It reports to the IT Operations Manager and has no supervisory responsibilities.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provide customer service over the phone and by email to assist end-users in resolving computer hardware and software problems*
