jobs.title: Compliance Engineer
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey's Compliance Engineering team is the compliance professionals counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: compliance professionals who bring real compliance and risk management experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Compliance Engineers understand how compliance teams think and work, and they use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live, in-practice pressure. They also shape Harvey’s product roadmap, so every release is grounded in what compliance teams need. They serve as the subject matter layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

This Compliance Engineer will be the founding member of this team, working directly with the leader of Legal Engineering to define the role and, as the function grows, build it out.

You may be asked to travel around 2-3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1-3 days at a time.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

Compliance Engineers are compliance professionals who want to help build the future of how compliance work gets done. Working closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, you will engage with compliance, risk, and regulatory teams across the customer lifecycle, from the first conversation to a complex workflow and ongoing use. You will:

 - Partner with Account Executives to lead discovery to understand how compliance processes run today and where the time and risk sit.

 - Demonstrate Harvey on real compliance use cases and run collaborative pilots that show meaningful value.

 - Train compliance teams and help them configure and build agents and workflows they can put into practice.

 - Bring customer and prospect feedback back to Product and Engineering to help shape the roadmap.

 - Help define the Compliance Engineer role and build the playbook, including demo assets, use cases, and engagement models.

 - As the function grows, help hire and develop the team.

The scope of this role is intentionally open. You will help shape it.





WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience as a compliance practitioner in-house, at a regulated company, in consulting or advisory, or advising a sophisticated compliance team.

 - Strong understanding of the workflows, challenges, and demands of compliance teams, including balancing regulatory risk with business priorities.

 - Comfort with technology and operations, and a builder’s instinct for turning a repeated manual process into something repeatable.

 - A commercial mindset, with the ability to understand customer value and make the case for change.

 - Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility with compliance leaders and business stakeholders at all levels.

 - Outstanding communication and presentation skills. You’re comfortable leading a live demo, facilitating a workshop, or engaging in strategic customer conversations.

 - Deep curiosity about AI’s potential to transform compliance work, paired with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset and bias toward action.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and excitement about helping define a new role and function.

 - Experience at a technology or SaaS company, sales or customer-facing experience (solutions consulting, pre-sales, advisory), and/or hands-on experience using AI tools in compliance work are all pluses.

$218,400 - $327,600 USD (75/25) OTE

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT OUTTAKE

Outtake exists to empower and facilitate trust for a digital-first world. Today, impersonation, fraud, AI-driven scams, and identity abuse spread faster than any security team can respond to. So we built something different: an agentic AI platform that proactively detects, monitors, and takes down impersonators, automating protection in hours, not weeks.

 

Built by ex-Palantir, ex-CTO/founders, and ex-Notion engineers, Outtake is designed for clarity, autonomy, and velocity. Our goal is ambitious: become the trust layer of the modern internet. And we intend to do it with a lean, dense, exceptionally talented team.

 

Outtake is backed by top-tier investors and operators who believe in our mission and our model. With strong financial footing and a long runway, we prioritize creating an environment where people can do the best work of their careers.


THE ROLE

This is a platform engineering role. You will own the foundations that product engineers rely on every day, designing and maintaining the systems, tools, and primitives that determine how fast, safely, and confidently the team can ship. Your work directly influences developer workflows, reliability, and day-to-day engineering velocity.

You will prioritize work that multiplies impact across the engineering org, turning patterns into platforms and one-off fixes into systems rather than solving the same problem repeatedly. The goal is to make it easier for engineers to move quickly and do the right thing by default.

This is a role that expects you to build durable foundations. You will develop and evolve a point of view on how engineers should work, then translate that vision into code and systems — operating comfortably in messy, fast-moving environments and steadily turning them into something more solid without slowing the team down. You'll balance long-term thinking with practical execution.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the foundations that product engineers rely on every day, including the systems, tools, and primitives that shape developer workflows, reliability, and velocity

 - Prioritize work that multiplies impact across the engineering org, turning repeated patterns into platforms and one-off fixes into systems

 - Develop and evolve a point of view on how engineers should work, then translate that vision into code and durable systems

 - Operate in messy, fast-moving environments and steadily turn them into something more solid without slowing the team down

 - Build or own internal platforms, developer tooling, or shared infrastructure that engineers default to

 - Remove entire classes of errors through better abstractions rather than one-off fixes

 - Build infrastructure that quietly unlocks faster product work across teams

 - Become the person other engineers rely on when systems get weird or unclear, and the person leadership turns to when deciding how the platform should evolve next




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A track record of building and owning foundational systems that other engineers depended on, along with experience living with the consequences of those decisions

 - The ability to ramp quickly, operate in ambiguity, and make progress without needing problems fully specified up front

 - An understanding of the tension between ideal solutions and velocity, and the judgment to know when to pursue one over the other

 - An instinct for leverage, with a preference for systemic fixes over one-off solutions

 - A clear point of view on how engineers should work, and the drive to turn that into code, tooling, and defaults

 - Experience working closely with other engineers or teams as an enabler, not just as an implementer

 - A desire to help define and build the platform's direction, rather than execute against a tightly defined scope and fixed roadmap

 - Nice to have: experience building or owning internal platforms, developer tooling, or shared infrastructure

 - Nice to have: experience working on agentic systems, LLM platforms, or large-scale data ingestion pipelines

 - Nice to have: a track record of being the person people go to when systems get weird or unclear






LIFE AT OUTTAKE

 - Office: For those in NY, we are an in-person team (5 days a week, with flexibility as needed) working out of a stunning waterfront office in Brooklyn. Collaboration, speed, and clarity matter.

 - Health: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for employees.

 - Time Away: Flexible PTO. We trust adults to manage energy, not clock time. 

 - Culture & Team: Annual company retreats and regular in-person events.

Outtake is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team.

jobs.title: Supervisor Clinical Lab
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Supervisor of the clinical laboratory is a member of the Operations Department whose role is to oversee employees' performance and serve as a liaison between employees and senior management to meet company goals and quality objectives. The supervisor is responsible for daily supervision of lab staff performing duties such as laboratory testing and data review. Duties include but are not limited to coaching, motivating, staffing, evaluating,
and training staff. The supervisor works closely with the manager to ensure company and team goals are met while adhering to good manufacturing practices and CLIA/CAP guidelines.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provides direct supervision to professional individual contributors and/or skilled, support individual contributors

• Ensures production work is consistently completed according to department goals.

• Administers company policies that directly affect subordinate employees.

• Monitors team members to ensure adherence to SOPs and safety procedures

• Oversees training and development of all staff members

• Document nonconformances and all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from the established performance specifications as needed. Escalates protocol deviation to lead/supervisor.

• Handles employee issues in collaboration with the department manager and Human Resources.

• Ensures alignment with team for reasoning behind instructions/processes and changes

• Plans and leads shift meetings. Meets regularly with individual team members to discuss goals and progress

• Go-to person when manager is not present.

• May assist lab team in day-to-day tasks

• Keeps team morale up and maintains professionalism of team members, including by acting as role model.

• Identifies trends and issues and effectively executes solutions

• Actively interacts with interdepartmental teams such as OPS, Accessioning, Engineering, Stats, R&D, and Support.

• Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

New York City, NY - Fifth Avenue

At Rothy’s, we believe there’s a better way to do business—one that puts the planet and its people first. That’s why we’ve transformed millions of plastic bottles into stylish, sustainable shoes and bags, creating wardrobe staples that look just as good as they feel.

In our retail stores, clienteling, and genuine connection are at the heart of everything we do. We take pride in building lasting relationships with our customers—getting to know their style, anticipating their needs, and creating personalized experiences that make them feel truly seen and supported. Whether it’s helping someone find their perfect fit or sharing the story behind our sustainable designs, every interaction is an opportunity to deepen that connection.

As we grow, we’re cultivating not just a workplace, but a community. It’s a place where careers can grow, ideas are shared, and people feel a true sense of belonging. Every day brings new opportunities to learn, lead, and make an impact—together, as part of a welcoming, inclusive team that celebrates each other’s contributions.

Shopping at Rothy’s IRL is not your ordinary retail experience—so naturally, our Stores team is extraordinary, too. Experts in the fit, wear and sizing of our shoes, these team members provide deep knowledge of every Rothy’s style and out-of-this-world customer service—creating long-lasting brand loyalty. Customers love shopping in our stores due to these exceptional interactions.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Keyholder, you will help bring our company values to life by creating a service-first culture on the sales floor and supporting smooth store operations. You’ll act as a role model for your peers, delivering exceptional customer experiences, coaching in the moment, and upholding operational excellence. As part of the leadership team, you may serve as Manager on Duty, ensuring the store reflects our brand standards and values in every interaction.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Customer Experience (80%)

 - Lead and model Rothy’s Experience through exceptional service and selling on the sales floor by coaching and guiding team members to consistently uphold brand standards

 - Drive personal and team sales results, by delivering the Rothy’s Experience to all customers and supporting your teammates through coaching and team selling

 - Create lasting relationships with our customers by engaging in strong clienteling practices

 - Assist with the execution of in store events and activations that engage the local community, support brand awareness, and drive sales

 - Support with onboarding and training by reinforcing store standards, SOPs, service expectations, selling behaviors, and product knowledge on the sales floor

Team Leadership & Operational Excellence (20%)

 - Act as Manager on Duty when assigned ensuring daily operations, visual merchandising tasks, and service expectations are being met by all team members

 - Own assigned areas of responsibility as part of the Division of Responsibility (DOR) program and communicate progress, opportunities, and feedback to store leadership




YOU ARE:

 - Guided by Rothy’s values and committed to fostering a welcoming, service driven environment:
   
   - Embrace Possibility.  We dream BIG, really big
   
   - Obsess Over Innovation: We never accept the status quo
   
   - Make the Planet Proud.  We make the right choice, not the easy one
   
   - Collaboration is Key.  We’re laser focused on driving results

 - 18 years of age or older




YOU HAVE:

 - 1–2 years of retail or customer service experience, ideally with some leadership responsibility

 - A proven ability to connect with customers and deliver exceptional service

 - Experience supporting operational tasks such as merchandising, shipment, or stockroom leadership

 - A desire to grow your leadership skills

 - Ability to stand/walk an entire shift

 - Ability to lift, push carry or otherwise move up to 25 lbs

 - Ability to frequently bending, reaching, stretching, and safely use ladders and step stools

 - Ability to uphold Rothy’s Experience by following our dress code, including wearing Rothy’s shoes during every shift

 - Availability to work a minimum of 40 hours/week, including peak business days (Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays), holidays, and evening and opening shifts





OUR BENEFITS:

 - Generous paid time off

 - 401k matching

 - Comprehensive health plans for you and your family

 - Supplemental mental health benefits

 - Monthly wellness reimbursement

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

About Amperesand

[Standard company overview – maintained by Talent Acquisition / Marketing]

Amperesand is building next-generation power infrastructure systems for Data Centers, EV charging platforms, and future energy applications. Our systems combine advanced power electronics, embedded controls, and scalable energy architectures to rethink how power is converted, controlled, and deployed.

About the Role

Role Summary

Amperesand is looking for a Senior or Staff level Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer to develop an advanced liquid-cooling system for its next-generation medium-voltage solid-state power conversion platform. This is a hands-on role where you’ll develop the thermal system through architecture and concept selection, system sizing and modeling, CAD and detailed design, thermal CFD simulation, coolant and airflow routing, design for manufacturing and assembly, thermal system validation, and troubleshooting.

You’ll work closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, quality, suppliers, and factory teams to design, develop, and build the best system for a novel application, solve problems that don’t have established answers, with the opportunity to own thermal design.  Thermal performance is critical to the overall performance of our solid-state power converter and a key differentiator for Amperesand.  We are looking for someone with deep expertise in thermals, system modeling and simulation, detailed design experience, and a track record of complex technical work and solving novel problems.  We are not looking for someone who simply executes to a defined specification. The role can be based in Reno, San Francisco, or the South Bay.

What You’ll Do

• Develop the thermal system for Amperesand’s solid-state power conversion platform from architecture into mass-production.

• Work on architecture and concept selection.

• Model the thermal system performance across our operating conditions and mission profiles.

• Detailed design of the thermal system components, including 3D and 2D CAD of structures, coolant routing, interconnections, and thermal CFD.

• Partner with the manufacturing and quality teams on DFM/DFA activities to ensure the thermal system design is manufacturable.

• Prototyping and validation of the thermal system.

• Problem solving anywhere and everywhere between architecture and start of production.

• Years of experience: 3+ for Senior level, 6+ for Staff level

• BS in mechanical engineering or a closely related field, Masters or PhD are a plus

• Liquid-cooling thermal system and mechanical design experience, CAE expertise

• Compressor-loop refrigeration system experience

• Demonstrated ability to deliver a thermal system and solve novel engineering problems

• Hands-on testing and validation experience

• Experience with Catia 3DX

• Experience with Siemens Amesim or similar

• Familiarity with high-voltage design

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

One of our company values is "Embrace Differences" and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging are the principles guiding how we build our business and teams. We encourage interested candidates from all backgrounds to apply even if they don't think they meet every expectation of the role.

About the role:

We are seeking an inspiring and adaptable Psychiatric Nurse Manager to lead and empower a growing remote team of 30-40 part-time and full-time psychiatric providers delivering care to adult clients. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Clinical Care, you will champion clinical excellence, support professional growth, and help shape the future of our psychiatric services.

Core Areas of Responsibility:

Team Leadership & Mentorship:

• Directly manage and develop 30-40 remote psychiatric providers. Provide clinical consultation, crisis support, performance coaching, and foster an engaging, high-performing team culture.

• Establish team priorities, workflows, performance expectations, and operational goals.

• Implement and support company roll-outs of clinical policies and procedures while working collaboratively with cross-functional stakeholders across the company.

• Use team-level performance data, engagement scores, attended sessions, documentation timeliness, to guide coaching and catch problems early.

Clinical Practice:

• Maintain a small caseload (~10 client hours/week depending on business need) and cover for urgent appointments and refill requests as needed.

• Thoughtfully integrate technology into your practice and provide data-driven care.

• Actively engage in our community and professional growth through case consultation.

• Conduct audits and reviews of provider activity and clinical documentation as needed.

• Identify trends impacting psychiatric providers and recommend operational improvements.

Operational Excellence:

• Establish team workflows, track key performance indicators, conduct documentation audits, and collaborate cross-functionally with Quality, Legal, and Compliance teams.

• Use data-driven decision making to optimize provider experience, client outcomes, and operational efficiency.

• Help develop scalable operational processes to support future growth and expansion of psychiatric offerings.

Innovation & Product Collaboration:

• Serve as a subject matter expert for practitioner workflows. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Ops teams to refine digital tools and scale care delivery.

We're looking for someone with:

• Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) from an accredited institution and board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) license.

• Active PMHNP license in CA, WA, FL, or TX held for 2+ years

• Active DEA and state prescriptive authority registrations.

• Willingness to obtain cross-licensure in additional states. We’ll cover the entire cost.

• 2+ years of experience managing a team of licensed psychiatric practitioners, including 6+ months of remote management experience. Strong preference for experience managing a large team (20+ direct reports) of part-time providers.

• Strong grounding in psychiatric prescribing regulations, measurement-based care (e.g., PHQ-9), and HIPAA standards.

• Experience investigating or resolving complex clinical, quality, compliance, or provider performance concerns.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make data-informed decisions.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

• Experience working in a fast-paced, high-growth technology environment.

• Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive projects to completion.

• Install, replace, and repair residential plumbing systems and equipment, including water heaters, boilers, water supply lines, drain and sewer lines, gas lines, and related components..

• Working knowledge of boiler piping, circulator pumps, expansion tanks, and zone valves preferred.

jobs.title: Assistant Teacher (Float): Boca Raton, FL
jobs.description:
As a full time Assistant Teacher (Float) at Bezos Academy (internally titled Assistant Teacher I), you share our passion for early childhood education and commitment to creating nurturing, high-quality learning environments for all children. While exact responsibilities will vary from school to school, you may assist in classrooms, serve and supervise mealtimes, and support the overall operations of the school. Drawing on your organizational skills, professionalism, and commitment to children, you will support a multi-state network of schools in under-resourced communities, offering quality Montessori-inspired preschool at no cost to families.

LOCATION

We are actively hiring for an Assistant Teacher (Float) to support our preschool in Boca Raton (777 Glades Rd, Boca Raton, FL 33431).

SCHEDULES, BENEFITS, AND COMPENSATION

• School schedules vary depending on community needs but generally range from 8am-5:30pm, with teachers staggered across these hours with varying start and end times totaling no more than 8 hours per day. Your specific schedule will be determined with your school leader when considering all staff, classroom, and community needs.

• This is a full time (40 hours per week), non-exempt/hourly position.

• This role includes 32 days of scheduled breaks, 3 days of paid personal time off, 9 paid days of care (sick) time, 10 paid holidays, and additional time off if required by applicable law. Benefits for this role include medical, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, a 401(k) plan with a 4% employer contribution match, an employer-matched flexible spending account for dependent care, and more. Please see here for details.

• The full compensation range for this position is $19-$22 per hour. The starting pay for all new employees is $19 per hour.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

• Age 18 with high school diploma or GED

• Ability to pass background checks, clear tuberculosis screenings, and (upon hire) successfully complete trainings required by the state of Florida to supervise children independently

• Ability to independently supervise, communicate effectively with, and care for young children safely, including ability to lift a minimum of 40 lbs

• Access to reliable transportation to and from work and ability to consistently attend work as scheduled to ensure proper staff-to-child classroom ratios and support smooth school operations

• Must have a valid Food Handler’s Permit or be willing to obtain one upon hire

• Ability to complete 20 hours of onboarding by your seventh day of employment

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Prior experience supporting or teaching children ages 3–5 in a Montessori or early childhood classroom setting

• Experience working effectively across lines of difference and fostering an inclusive, welcoming environment for all children and families

• Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to manage daily operational tasks such as classroom setup, safety checks, and basic clerical responsibilities

• Demonstrated reliability and flexibility in supporting school operations, including meal service, playground supervision, assisting with classroom coverage as needed, and lead after-school activities

RESPONSIBILITIES

*NOTE: The combination of responsibilities may vary based on the needs of the school site, students, and prior experiences of the Assistant Teacher.

Instructional

• Serve as a floating assistant teacher, providing support wherever and however the school most needs it each day

• As needed, independently supervise children throughout the day in classrooms and a variety of other situations, including but not limited to arrival/departure, transitions, outside time, rest/nap time, and (if offered) extended hours

• Assist in maintaining accurate child and family records

• Complete Montessori basics training and credentialing/licensing requirements within seven days of hire

Operational

• Support Bezos Academy classrooms by following regulations and guidelines in the day-to-day operation of the classroom and school (e.g. cleaning/preparing materials, meal prep and cleanup, nap time transitions, laundry, bathroom supervision, etc.)

• Support school leadership and teachers to foster a nurturing, safe, and stimulating, non-competitive school environment

• Support children’s increasing independence with daily living skills (i.e., washing hands, using the bathroom, eating meals and snacks, cleaning up, etc.)

• Maintain licensing and credentialing requirements and complete required ongoing professional development trainings in a timely manner

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

• Assume postures at low levels (e.g., kneeling, stooping, bending, and sitting on the floor) as needed to communicate effectively with children

• Provide support to nearby Bezos Academy schools, as needed, at the direction of your Head of School or District School Leader

Other

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

Bezos Academy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Bezos Academy participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with employee Form I-9 Information to confirm authorization to work in the U.S. Bezos Academy only uses E-Verify once a candidate has accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. If E-Verify cannot confirm that an employee is authorized to work, Bezos Academy will give the employee written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so the employee can begin to resolve the issue before any adverse employment action is taken. For more information about your right to work, please see the Notice of Right to Work.

We will work with you to ensure you have a fair opportunity to apply for our open positions.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager: Developer Experience
jobs.description:
About Us

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Our HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant platform bridges the “last mile” of AI adoption, empowering sectors like healthcare and national security to run trustworthy, predictable AI agents across any model or environment—whether in the cloud, on-prem, or at the edge—with unified policy enforcement, continuous monitoring, and fully immutable audit trails.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. The company has repeatedly topped Hugging Face’s GAIA Leaderboard for Generalized AI Assistants, placing it firmly at the forefront of AI-agent innovation.

The role: Senior Product Manager, Developer Experience

You'll own the experience of developers who build, test, and deploy AI agents with Trase. Your job is to help a new developer get to a working agent quickly and give experienced teams tools they can trust in production. As teams move from experimental agent demos to mission-critical production systems, you will define the standard for how serious developers build, evaluate, and ship AI agents.

You’ll be the product manager for Trase Arena, our SDK and tools for building AI agents. Your scope covers a developer’s work from the first build through deployment, observability and improvement on Origin. You'll work directly with developers, engineering, design, and product marketing to build an experience that earns adoption through the product itself.

What You Will Do

• Know the developer: Work directly with developers to understand what they're trying to build. Observe where they get stuck, test assumptions, and use what you learn to set priorities.

• Set a high bar for the tools: Own the developer experience across the SDK, APIs, and CLI. Make them consistent, predictable, well documented, and useful for real development work.

• Make the whole journey work: Connect building, testing, evaluation, packaging, and deployment into a coherent experience. Partner with the enterprise platform PM to make the path through production approval clear for builders and operators.

• Own documentation and onboarding: Treat these as core parts of the product. Help developers understand the concepts, complete their first deployment, and solve problems independently.

• Build ecosystem foundations: Prioritize examples, templates, and reference integrations that help developers build useful agents. Shape how developers discover, reuse, and share what others have built.

• Earn developer trust: Establish clear expectations for compatibility, API versioning, and deprecation. Work with engineering to make changes understandable and manageable for developers.

• Drive product-led growth: Reduce friction from first use through repeat adoption. Partner with product marketing on getting-started content and developer adoption, grounding that work in the actual product experience.

• Measure and deliver: Own priorities and follow through from discovery to release. Track monthly active developers, time to first deployment, onboarding time, developer satisfaction, and the number of agents built with Arena and running on Origin.

About You

• You've owned and shipped developer products such as SDKs, APIs, CLIs, or development platforms.

• You have strong product taste in developer tooling: You have an opinionated point of view on what makes an API intuitive, an error message actionable, and a CLI joyful to use—and you can defend those opinions with engineers and designers.

• You care about the details developers notice: clear abstractions, useful errors, accurate examples, dependable behavior, and documentation that answers the question.

• You think like an entrepreneur. You identify useful opportunities, test them with developers, and turn what you learn into product decisions.

• You take ownership without waiting for direction. You understand how to keep individual developers moving fast without creating dead-ends, allowing us to scale into production.

• You learn quickly and exercise sound judgment. You can explain a complex problem clearly and choose a practical path through it.

• You ship and measure what happens next. Your standard is whether developers can successfully build and deploy something useful.

Nice to have (not required)

• Experience building AI agents or working with evaluation and testing tools.

• Experience growing a developer ecosystem, marketplace, or integration platform.

• Experience improving self-service activation and developer retention.

• Experience connecting developer workflows with enterprise production requirements.

Our Trase Benefits:

For full-time roles only

• Career track opportunity with potential for rapid advancement with strong performance as the firm grows

• 100% employer paid, comprehensive health care including medical, dental, and vision for you and your family.

• Paid maternity and paternity for 14 weeks at employees' normal pay.

• Unlimited PTO, with management approval.

• Opportunities for professional development and continued learning.

• Optional 401K, FSA, and equity incentives available.

• Mental health benefits are available through Tara Mind.

We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer: You’ll receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.

Applicant Data Disclosure

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that Red Cell Partners, LLC ("Red Cell") uses third-party service providers to facilitate its recruitment and hiring processes. These providers include applicant tracking systems, candidate verification platforms, and fraud detection tools (collectively, "Hiring Platforms"). Your application materials, including your résumé, cover letter, work samples, responses to application questions, and any other information you submit, may be transmitted to and processed by these Hiring Platforms for the following purposes:

• Managing and administering your application throughout the hiring process;

• Verifying the accuracy and authenticity of application materials, including by cross-referencing information you provide against publicly available sources and proprietary databases;

• Identifying indicators of potentially fraudulent, fabricated, or materially misleading application content, including but not limited to discrepancies between submitted materials and publicly available professional profiles, geographic anomalies, and fabricated work histories.

Applications that are flagged through this process as containing indicators of fraud or material misrepresentation may be declined from further consideration. If you have questions about the status of your application or the evaluation process, please contact talent@redcellpartners.com.

Red Cell requires its Hiring Platform providers to process your information solely for the purposes described above and in accordance with applicable law. Your information will be retained only for as long as necessary to fulfill these purposes and any applicable legal obligations, after which it will be deleted in accordance with Red Cell's data retention policies.

For more information about how your data is used, please refer to our Privacy Policy and Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive - State Government
jobs.description:
At Submittable, we are transforming how organizations create social impact. Our platform empowers thousands of mission-driven organizations, from nonprofits to government entities, to make a difference in their communities and beyond. In 2024, our innovative software helped organizations worldwide run 30,000 programs, welcomed 1.2 million applicants, and facilitated the distribution of more than $10 billion in funding through our products on behalf of our clients.

We are on a mission to help organizations accelerate their impact, so we are proud to partner with organizations focused on Equity & Social Justice, Children & Education, Creative & Arts, Health & Wellness, Economic Justice & Opportunity, and Environment & Climate. At Submittable, technology and purpose converge, offering a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful change.

About the role

The Enterprise Account Executive, State Government, leads new business sales of Submittable's grants management and application software to state agencies and large local government organizations. The role owns a sales quota and a pipeline of complex opportunities, carrying each one from discovery through contract signature within public sector procurement processes, and grows revenue within assigned strategic government accounts.

The role partners with Government Sales Development, Solutions Engineering, Proposal, Legal, Implementation, and Customer Success teams to deliver solutions that fit each agency's program requirements, helping agencies run funding programs that reach the residents and communities they serve.

Key responsibilities

• Own a quota for new government business and expansion within assigned strategic accounts, building and managing a pipeline that meets monthly, quarterly, and annual targets.

• Lead consultative sales cycles with state and local government agencies, including discovery, tailored product demonstrations, and pricing proposals for program leaders, IT, procurement, and executive stakeholders.

• Manage public sector procurement requirements for each opportunity, partnering with the Proposal team on RFP, RFI, and other solicitation responses and with Legal on MSAs, SOWs, and agency contract terms through signature.

• Partner with Government Sales Development Representatives, Solutions Engineering, and Implementation to qualify opportunities, shape solutions, and hand off signed agencies smoothly to Customer Success.

• Maintain an accurate forecast and clean, current account, opportunity, and activity data in Salesforce, applying Submittable's opportunity management practices to deal strategy.

• Respond promptly and accurately to agency questions throughout the sales cycle, and share what is learned about agency needs, funding trends, and competitors with Marketing, Product, and Sales leadership.

• Build working knowledge of government grantmaking and funding programs and of Submittable's products, and recommend improvements to government sales plays, messaging, and processes.

• Maintain current Submittable Sales certifications and complete required training.

Skills & Competencies

• 5+ years of B2B SaaS or enterprise software sales experience, with a track record of meeting quota and closing new business deals of $100K or more in annual recurring revenue (ARR).

• Experience creating and responding to RFPs or similar formal solicitations.

• Experience drafting MSAs and SOWs and coordinating contract and legal review through signature.

• Experience delivering software demonstrations tailored to different audiences in a complex sale with multiple decision makers and partners.

• Experience using a CRM, such as Salesforce, to document deal progress and forecast accurately; experience with Salesloft and Gong preferred.

• Experience selling to state or local government agencies, or working in or with government grant programs, preferred.

• Builds account plans that map stakeholders, procurement steps, and decision criteria, and updates them as deals progress.

• Works across teams to reach shared deal decisions, shares information openly, raises risks early, and follows through on commitments to agencies and colleagues.

• Seeks to understand each agency's program goals and constraints and uses that understanding to shape proposals and solutions.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Compensation: The On-Target Earnings (OTE) range for this role is $170,000–$240,000, which includes base salary plus variable compensation tied to performance. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and qualifications. This role is also eligible for equity and Submittable’s benefits package.

We are interested in every qualified candidate eligible to work in the United States; however, we cannot accommodate scholastic or employment visas at this time. In addition, we are not able to consider applicants who reside in the following states: Alaska, Delaware, Hawaii, Louisiana, Maine, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, West Virginia, and Wyoming.

Fraudulent Recruitment Advisory: Submittable will NEVER request bank details, payment, or personal information during the hiring process, nor extend offers without an interview. All legitimate communications come from official submittable.com email addresses. If you receive suspicious outreach, please report it to people@submittable.com. (Please do not submit applications, resumes, cover letters, or other candidacy materials to this email address. Emails of this nature will not be reviewed or considered.)

Why Submittable?

Joining Submittable means becoming part of a forward-thinking, mission-driven company that values innovation, collaboration, and growth. We empower organizations working for social good with technology that accelerates their work, amplifies their impact, and drives meaningful change.

At Submittable, you’ll find a supportive, dynamic work environment where your contributions directly influence our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment and are excited to be part of a company dedicated to social impact, we invite you to apply!

Benefits: We are proud to offer highly competitive benefits to our full-time employees, including:

• Comprehensive health and life insurance with optional HSA, FSA, and DCA accounts

• 401(k) plan with employer match starting day one

• Equity stock options to share in our success

• Flexible hours, remote work options, and generous vacation and sick leave

• Paid parental leave for mothers, fathers, and adoptive parents

• Professional development stipends to support your career growth

• Opportunities to participate in community outreach and volunteer programs

• Monthly company-sponsored happy hours and gatherings to connect and unwind

Our Commitment to Inclusion & Belonging

At Submittable, we believe technology is a force for good, driving social impact and enabling corporate social responsibility on a global scale. To achieve this, we are committed to fostering a workplace that values inclusion and belonging as central pillars of our culture.

We embrace the strength of our diverse community by creating a safe space where employees feel empowered to share ideas, celebrate unique experiences, and learn from one another. By prioritizing inclusion, we aim to build an environment where everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and make innovative contributions that enable our customers to tackle complex challenges and spread more good.

jobs.location: Hybrid - Austin, Texas; United States - Austin, Texas
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About the Role:

You've made the calls, booked the meetings, and know what separates a good SDR from a great one. Now own SDR performance at Motive, side by side with the VP of Sales Development in Austin, and turn early-career reps into a pipeline engine and the next AE bench.

As Sr Manager, SDR Enablement Business Partner, you'll report to the VP, Sales Enablement and partner with the VP of Sales Development. You'll own SDR skills after ramp, SDR accreditation paths, and SDR activations, and lead a team of three in Pakistan (two SDR Enablement specialists and an SDR Accreditation PM). This is a hands-on role: you set the strategy, then run sessions, review calls, and build training yourself. It is based in Austin and works in the office with SDR leadership.

What You'll Do:

• Measure enablement by business outcomes shared with the VP of Sales Development (meetings set, pipeline quality, conversion to opportunity), backed by % of SDRs accredited in launched paths and % completing and passing each activation.

• Diagnose gaps from MORs, conversation intelligence, performance data, and leader interviews, and partner with Sales Ops to link accreditation to results.

• Bring the SDR view into quarterly enablement planning, set the quarter's priorities with the VP of Sales Development, and run the operating rhythm with SDR leadership, operating as a fully consultative partner by Q2.

• Build the SDR curriculum for prospecting into fleet and physical operations businesses: cold calling, messaging, objection handling, qualification, discovery, and handoff to AEs.

• Build and run SDR accreditation paths (6- or 12-month programs in quarterly skill cycles, with badges that mark progress) that bridge to the AE role.

• Coach on live calls and pipeline, and run drills, workshops, AI roleplays, and call reviews that turn practice into meetings.

• Add the Motive layer to the external early-career skills content SDRs use, aligned to the Motive Value Architecture, and keep the SDR Role Playbook current each quarter.

• Adapt and run SDR activations, plays, and tool refreshers, and serve as the intake point for plays from Sales Development leaders.

• Lead your team of three, with the SDR Accreditation PM running structure, badging, and reporting for SDR paths.

• Set the coaching standard for Sales Development managers so coaching stays consistent as the team grows.

• Partner with Role Readiness, which owns SDR onboarding, so new SDRs move from certified into your accreditation cadence, and with the senior Accreditation PM (under the Lead Enablement Business Partner, Enterprise Sales), who owns cross-segment accreditation standards. Connect SDR plans to the rest of GTM with the other EBPs, GTM Activation, Content & Academy, and Sales Ops.

What We're Looking For:

• 4 to 7 years in sales enablement, sales development leadership, or sales training at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company. Time as an SDR, BDR, or AE strongly preferred.

• You've enabled SDR or BDR teams in a high-volume outbound motion and can coach a cold call as well as you can design a program.

• You've built and run certification or accreditation programs, not just administered them, and can show measurable results.

• You read the data and the calls, find the gap, and fix it.

• Fluent in established sales methodologies (e.g., Sandler, Challenger, Command of the Message) and AI practice tools, and how they apply to prospecting.

• You've led a team, including offshore team members in another time zone, and influence leaders you don't manage.

• A strong facilitator and coach for early-career reps and experienced sellers alike.

• Able to work in the office in Austin, Texas with SDR leadership.

Pay Transparency

jobs.title: PEO HR Advisor
jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About the role

Our PEO Human Resources (“HR”) Advisory team provides HR consulting services to PEO, ASO, and US EOR customers. As a PEO HR Advisor, you will deliver effective and efficient HR consulting services to customers of Rippling PEO (“Professional Employer Organization”), ASO (Administrative Services Offering), and US EOR (Employer of Record). We’re looking for a self-driven, growth-minded “lover of all things employee management and risk mitigation.” You will serve as a trusted advisor to Rippling PEO customers, helping them navigate a variety of employee management scenarios while ensuring our customers remain compliant with relevant federal, state and local regulations. You’ll also work directly with Rippling’s product and engineering teams to improve Rippling’s compliance product offerings. It’s a highly cross-functional role with a significant impact on the success of multiple Rippling products.

What you will do

• Provide accurate, timely advice to help Rippling PEO, ASO, & US EOR customers implement best business practices and reduce employer risk for issues including: Leave of absence management, performance management, terminations, anti-harassment, policy development and other HR challenges that present legal or regulatory risk to their businesses
• Field customer inquiries as a trusted, highly knowledgeable HR expert; develop programs and processes with our sales, implementation, support and account management teams to meet our commitments to our customers
• Assist customers in managing employee claims related to unemployment benefits, state leave benefits, disability benefits, workers’ compensation, and employee grievances
• Establish processes to both professionalize our consulting offering and optimize our efficiency around these offerings
• Work closely with our product and engineering teams to develop a best-in-class HR Services offering that leans heavily on technology to ease the administrative burden of HR compliance
• Highly organized, self-motivated, and detail-oriented; great follow-through on projects/tasks big and small
• Have the courage to challenge the status quo when logic and reason require it. See something broken? Fix it.

What you will need

• Minimum 5 years of experience in customer/client-facing HR consulting services
• Deep understanding of HR compliance rules and regulations across federal, state, and local jurisdictions
• Experience managing employee claims related to unemployment benefits, state leave benefits, disability benefits, workers’ compensation, and employee grievances
• Excellent client-facing verbal and written communication skills
• Strong project management and organizational skills: high attention to detail with excellent work product, time management, and project execution
• Experience managing cases and/or processes in Salesforce
• Passion for technology, and a desire to work in an extremely fast-paced, high-growth company
• PHR or SHRM-CP certification, a plus
• Experience providing HR services to PEO customers, a plus
• Must be based on the West Coast, PST working hours

About the team

The PEO Human Resources (“HR”) Advisory team is a solution-focused team that's instrumental in helping clients manage their HR compliance issues and reducing the risk to the wider PEO organization. The team works closely with Product Engineering and Support teams, as well as sales, marketing and implementation teams to help build compliance initiatives and train internal teams on PEO issues.

Additional Information

Rippling is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other legally protected characteristics, Rippling is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities who need assistance during the hiring process. To request a reasonable accommodation, please email accommodations@rippling.com

Rippling highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture.  For office-based employees (employees who live within a defined radius of a Rippling office), Rippling considers working in the office, at least three days a week under current policy, to be an essential function of the employee's role.

This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. The salary for US-based employees will be aligned with one of the ranges below based on location; see which tier applies to your location here.

jobs.title: Director of Design & Creative Services
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Cresco Labs is one of the largest public, vertically integrated, multistate operators in the cannabis industry. Our portfolio of in-house cultivated and manufactured brands features some of the highest quality, most awarded and most popular cannabis products in America. With dozens of locations nationwide, our owned and operated Sunnyside® dispensaries provide a welcoming, positive, judgement-free place to shop for anyone at any point on their cannabis journey.

Founded in 2013, Cresco Labs’ mission is to normalize and professionalize cannabis through our passionate employees. As stewards of the cannabis industry, our teams are constantly focused on supporting the needs of our fellow colleagues, consumers, customers, and communities alike. With a focus on Social Equity and Educational Development, our SEEDTM initiative ensures that our company reflects the communities in which we serve, ensuring equal opportunity for all to have the knowledge and resources to work in and own businesses in cannabis.

At Cresco Labs, we aim to revolutionize and lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on quality and consistency of product, and to bring legitimacy to the industry with the highest level of integrity and professionalism.

If you’re interested in joining our mission, click the below links to join our team today!

MISSION STATEMENT

At Cresco, we aim to lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on regulatory compliance, product consistency, and customer satisfaction. Our operations bring legitimacy to the cannabis industry by acting with the highest level of integrity, strictly adhering to regulations, and promoting the clinical efficacy of cannabis. As Cresco grows, we will operate with the same level of professionalism and precision in each new market we move in to.

JOB SUMMARY

Cresco Labs is seeking a Director of Design & Creative Services to lead our in-house creative department, The HotBox, in Chicago, IL. HotBox is responsible for the execution of all omnichannel design, copywriting, and production work for the company, upholding the integrity of the Cresco Labs House of Brands as well as Sunnyside & SPS Retail Brands across multiple markets. Reporting to the Senior Director of Brand, Visual & Creative, this role sets and upholds the department’s overarching creative vision and standards ensuring cohesion, excellence, and brand consistency. The Director oversees a multidisciplinary team of Design Directors, Graphic Designers, Production Designers, Copywriters, and Project Managers.

CORE JOB DUTIES

• Set and uphold the creative vision, strategy, and standards for the department. Own the performance of the full creative lifecycle: concepting, design, copywriting, production, and project management with accountability for quality, efficiency, and alignment with business goals.

• Own cross-functional stakeholder relationships: communicating with clarity and precision in writing, presentations, and meetings, setting expectations on timelines and deliverables, and distilling complex information into clear takeaways and actionable next steps.

• Own capacity planning and project workflow across all creative workstreams—including intake, prioritization, and quick-turn projects through the Fast Lane—balancing business priorities, team capacity, and delivery timelines.

• Take initiative in proactively identifying and presenting strategic priorities, long-range creative plans, and forward-looking recommendations to senior leadership, ensuring the department is always thinking ahead of immediate deliverables.

• Develop and manage the department’s annual AOP creative budget and resource plan, including staffing, agency, freelance, production, photography, and technology needs. Participate in sourcing, onboarding, and oversight of external partners to ensure work meets internal brand standards.

• Understand complex regulatory & compliance frameworks, proposing creative solutions to meet the needs of multiple states markets efficiently.

• Drive creative innovation and operational improvement including application of AI within the department, motion graphics, data-driven design, inclusive design and selfservice platforms (e.g., Canva) that scale the team’s output while maintaining standards.

• Guide messaging strategy, brand voice, and copy quality across channels, ensuring strong alignment between written and visual communication.

• Direct in-house photoshoots end to end, ensuring alignment with brand strategy, budget, and production requirements.

• Establish creative governance from brief through final approval—clear objectives, defined audiences, stakeholder alignment, and structured feedback resolution.

• Champion continuous improvement across the department by identifying and applying relevant developments in design, copy, technology, production, and the broader industry.

• Develop, mentor, and retain talent. Conduct performance reviews, set clear expectations, and foster a collaborative, high-performing team culture.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND SKILLS

• 10+ years of professional experience in creative services, design, or marketing communications (in-house or agency)

• 5+ years in a leadership or director-level role, overseeing multidisciplinary creative teams including design, copy, and/or project management

• Strong understanding of creative workflows across design, copy, and production. Familiarity with Adobe Creative Suite and project management tools.

• Exceptional organizational and strategic planning skills, including creative budget development and agency/freelance spend management.

• Experience overseeing creative output across print and digital channels, including messaging strategy, user experience, and social content.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills—able to distill complex creative strategy into concise updates, clear recommendations, and defined next steps for both cross-functional partners and senior leadership.

• Genuine interest in and passion for the cannabis industry is required. Experience in regulated industries a plus.

In accordance with any local and state compensation laws, the compensation listed is the current estimated range for the position. Final offer details and future compensation may be determined by multiple factors including but not limited to, geographic location, market compensation data, skills, experience, and other relevant factors. For questions about this please discuss with your recruiter during the interview process.

Pay Range

$140,000—$150,000 USD

BENEFITS

Cresco Labs is proud to offer eligible employees a robust offering of benefits including, major medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(K)-match program, FSA/HSA programs, LTD/STD options, life insurance and AD&D.  We also offer eligible employees paid holidays and paid time off.  Other rewards may include annual discretionary bonuses, stock options as well as participation in our employee discount program. Benefits eligibility for permanent positions may vary.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Must be 21 years of age or older to apply

• Must comply with all legal or company regulations for working in the industry

• The company does not offer employment-based visa sponsorship for this role or any other position, now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis without the need for current or future sponsorship at any time.

Cresco Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all applicants will be considered without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) Notice to Applicants:

Please read the California Employee Privacy Notice (“CA Privacy Notice”) regarding Sunnyside* and its affiliate Cresco Labs’ policies pertaining to the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information. This CA Privacy Notice supplements the information contained in the Sunnyside* Privacy Policy and applies to California resident employees and job applicants. Applicants with disabilities may access this notice in an alternative format by contacting CCPAnotice@crescolabs.com

Reporting a Scam:

Cresco Labs is aware of fictitious employment offers being circulated from various sources. Many of these schemes consist of an alleged offer of employment with Cresco Labs with the intention of gaining personal information, including payment and/or banking information. Be aware that fraudulent job offers and correspondence may appear legitimate: they may feature a Cresco Labs logo, they may appear to originate from an official-looking email address or web site, or they may be sent by individuals purporting to represent Cresco Labs or an entity which includes the word Cresco Labs in its name.

Please note that Cresco Labs does not ask for payment or personal banking information as a condition of employment. Any personal information is requested for payroll or state badging purposes only. Applications can be securely submitted through our career’s pages.

We are working diligently to block this from happening. Beware if an offer of employment looks too good to be true. Never divulge personal and banking information or send money if you are unsure of the authenticity of an email or other communication in the name of Cresco Labs.

If you are in doubt, please contact us at Report-a-spam@crescolabs.com with questions.

jobs.title: Director Global Benefits
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is scaling fast across headcount, geographies, and the complexity that comes with both. Our benefits and leave programs are now the daily, tangible experience of working here for employees in a dozen countries, and they need an owner who can lead them at that scale.



We're looking for our first Director of Global Benefits to own Harvey's benefits and leave of absence strategy end to end, building on the foundations we have as we head into the next phase of our growth. You'll set the philosophy and stay close enough to the work to know whether a plan design holds up in practice.



This is a player/coach role for someone who has built and run a global benefits function before, ideally in a fast-scaling environment. You'll manage and grow our global benefits team, while engaging deeply in our highest-stakes workstreams: annual renewals, open enrollment, new-country launches, and the vendor relationships that underpin it all. You'll also own how benefits support feels day to day. Most employees meet this function through a single question at a stressful moment, and how that's handled matters as much as the plan design behind it.



You'll report to our Head of Total Rewards and partner closely with People Operations, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and Recruiting.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy and plan design

 - Define Harvey's global benefits and leave philosophy, including what "global consistency, local relevance" means as we enter new markets.

 - Lead plan design and redesign across the US and our international footprint (10+ markets and growing), balancing employee impact, competitiveness, and cost.

 - Build a program roadmap and business case for benefits, wellness, and leave, grounded in benchmarking and market analysis.

Team and service delivery

 - Grow and develop the global benefits team across the US and EMEA, setting priorities, raising the operating bar, and creating room for people to stretch.

 - Set and hold the standard for service delivery: response times, escalation, and follow-through on employee questions. Use AI and automation to take volume off the team without letting the experience get more distant.

 - Make our benefits legible, with clear, honest, localized communication so employees use what we offer and a partnership with Recruiting that makes our benefits a real differentiator in candidate conversations.

Programs, vendors, and spend

 - Oversee the annual cycle end to end: renewals, open enrollment, plan changes, carrier transitions, and new-country benefit launches.

 - Lead the global leave of absence program with consistency and care as volume scales.

 - Hold brokers, carriers, and third-party administrators to account globally, including RFPs, negotiations, contracting, and performance management.

 - Ensure compliance with local regulations in each market, partnering with Legal, Security, and Finance on vendor onboarding, data privacy, and risk review.

 - Manage the benefits budget with Finance and leverage utilization, cost, and sentiment data to decide what changes.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years in benefits, including 3+ years leading and developing a team, ideally in a high-growth technology company.

 - Deep US benefits expertise across health and welfare plan design, 401(k), leave, and the compliance landscape (ERISA, ACA, COBRA, HIPAA, FMLA and state equivalents).

 - Real international experience: you've designed or administered benefits in EMEA and/or APAC and understand that statutory minimums are a floor, not a program.

 - Strategic and hands-on: You can present a plan-design recommendation to executives in the morning and untangle a Workday eligibility rule in the afternoon.

 - Vendor and broker management: You've run RFPs, negotiated renewals, and held partners accountable across a fragmented global vendor landscape.

 - Financial fluency: You can build and defend a benefits budget, model cost scenarios, and explain the tradeoffs plainly.

jobs.title: Sr Outbound Product Manager Intern (MBA Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
Internship Program Overview

At ServiceNow, we’re looking for students who want to learn, grow, and take a giant step early in their careers, all while making a giant impact. We offer 12-week summer internship opportunities across various business functions.

Interns will participate in executive speaker series, career development workshops, philanthropic efforts, and team-building activities. Additionally, interns will have access to online learnings and a dedicated summer coach to further grow their careers with us.

If you want to make work, work better, we want you. To learn more, check out our Early Career Page!

Product Team Overview

We are looking for full-time MBA students to join our Product Management team at ServiceNow. As a Product Manager, you will work on complex high-tech problems by undertaking research, designing, and executing analysis, and helping frame and structure complex problems. You will work closely with other team members and stakeholders to accelerate our impact and directly contribute to our overall business strategy. This is an excellent opportunity if you are looking to get a taste of product management at a high-growth enterprise software company!

Product Management is a team sport at ServiceNow. We have a unique organization structure in which multiple Product Management roles work together to contribute to a product’s success.

We have two types of Product Managers within our teams: Inbound and Outbound

For the application: If you’re interested in both Inbound and Outbound Product Manager roles, please apply to your top choice only. Your application will automatically be considered for both roles. You are welcome to include your thoughts during the hiring manager notes.

For context: Inbound Product Managers plan for and develop new products and future releases of a product. They gather feedback to determine the problems we're trying to solve, then generate a product roadmap. They work with various teams such as release management, design, and engineering development.

For this role: Outbound Product Managers enable Go-To-Market teams on product innovation and evangelize the product with customers and partners. Considered the product experts, they generally serve as the bridge between the inbound PM and the product marketing team to ensure the product gets to our customers.

A few key responsibilities of Outbound PMs include:

• Enable our go to market partners

• Define pricing & packaging (in collaboration with our pricing team)

• Provide best practice content and guidance

• Package and deliver in-depth competitive analysis for go to market partners

• Drive customer usage and adoption programs

• Occasionally provide onboarding and renewal help

Additional possible responsibilities include:

• Support senior program managers and/or product managers across the entire project lifecycle to deliver critical programs for Service Now initiatives.

• Work and collaborate directly with Product Managers, Product Design, & Development Teams to build new features and improve adoption on existing features.

• Build familiarity with scrum process and willingness to contribute to team deliverables.

• Understand product strategy that sets us up for success as we look to grow to $15B+ in revenue.

• Research and collect product requirements from key buyer audiences and end-users to determine areas of opportunity for product enhancements.

• Oversee the product or project timeline, deadlines, milestones as it is being built by development/engineering and communicate with stakeholders to keep them updated.

• Contribute to the complete product lifecycle, from researching market needs and competition, analyzing customer data, writing product requirements, and delivering product features to market.

• Understand the technical and business impacts of product decisions that inform tradeoff decisions to optimize against product delivery and customer value.

Internship location may vary based on team growth strategies.

Required Qualifications

• Currently enrolled full-time at an accredited university pursuing an MBA in Engineering, Business Management, Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Applied Sciences, or a related field.
• Graduating May 2028 or later.
• Available to work full-time for a 12-week summer internship.
• 3–6 years of related experience.
• Experience using or evaluating AI to improve workflows, decision-making, problem-solving, automation, or data-driven insights.
• Experience defining product requirements and translating them into a product roadmap.
• Strategic mindset with the ability to balance customer desirability, business viability, and technical feasibility.
• Strong prioritization, problem-solving, and analytical skills, with a data-driven and hypothesis-led approach.
• Deep curiosity about customer needs and a passion for building relationships and delivering high-value solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with Agile methodologies and the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC).
• Experience collaborating with developers and designers to create compelling customer experiences.
• Demonstrated project management experience through internships, academic work, or personal projects.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $55.46 - $71.09, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.
