jobs.title: Safety Coordinator
jobs.description:
At Rent the Runway, our mission is to make women feel empowered and self-confident every single day by combining best in class technology, logistics, and customer service. Since our launch in 2009, we’ve developed proprietary technology, a one-of-a-kind reverse logistics operation, stores of the future, a viral brand, relationships with hundreds of fashion designers - and we are passionate about continuing to innovate our customer experience. We have pioneered the closet in the cloud and believe that every person globally will soon have a subscription to fashion. We are proud to be both a profitable and fast-growing business, with a loyal 10 million members who believe that rental is the future.

About the Job:

The Safety Coordinator serves as a designated safety representative of the assigned dream fulfillment center (DFC), coordinating and implementing all areas of the Rent the Runway’s (RTR) Safety Program as directed by the Sr. Manager of EHS. You will influence behavior and inspire commitment on the part of all personnel in complying with RTR’s safety standards and maintaining a safe work environment. This will include conducting training and coaching associates on observed work habits in support of this effort. A Safety Coordinator is a servant leader; dive in, roll up your sleeves to help in any situation, make tools available, remove obstacles for associates to excel in their roles, have empathy and compassion for associates, and the passion and leadership to stand up for them when the time arises.

Responsibilities:

• Identify and inform management of compliance issues, safety risks, and improvement opportunities through the process of doing daily, weekly, and monthly audits

• Facilitate incident investigation process

• Lead and participate in any investigations involving workplace incidents involving equipment and employees, along with investigations related to fleet safety.

• Conduct risk assessments related to jobs performed (Job Hazard Analysis) and new equipment introductions. Recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures to Management, including ergonomic considerations, in all such efforts.

• Ensure compliance with all RTR Safety Program expectations and applicable federal and state law.

• Maintain required paperwork to comply with RTR’s standards.

• Facilitate access to immediate aid for associates, visitors, vendors, or guests that need assistance or medical attention.

• Maintain accurate daily, weekly and monthly metrics to report to onsite management teams.

• Document safety incident information in RTR’s OSHA 300 log and 300a in a timely manner.

• Perform safety observations and audits.

• Train and assist the operations staff to comply with RTR’s safety responsibilities

• Perform specific safety training as required by the company.

• Conduct documented Monthly facility inspections and document findings

• Partner with the security team to ensure that the security team is aware of RTR’s safety policies.

Qualifications:

• Associates’ degree or Bachelor’s degree in safety, environmental, ergonomics or a related field required

• 2+ years of growing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, security or service operations.

• Experience maintaining confidentiality in all matters involving personnel issues in the workplace.

• Knowledge of OSHA regulations applicable in RTR’s industry.

• Calm demeanor in emergency situations.

• Must be flexible regarding shifts as safety incidents can happen at any time.

• Computer skills relevant to reviewing security footage and creating documents and incident logs.

• Proficient with Google Suite,Google Sheets, Looker, and Jira

• Strong written and verbal communication; bilingual in Spanish is highly preferred

• Enforce safety guidelines, cleanliness and security standards

• Ability to quickly recognize, diagnose and solve for challenges for associates in partnership with leadership

• Must operate with a sense of urgency and have attention to detail

• Align with the company's core values to ensure a world class customer experience

• Ability to lift a maximum of 50 lbs based on the needs of the role

• First Aid/ AED / CPR Certified

• Distribution Center or Manufacturing Safety experience at a site of at least 500 non exempt employees is a plus.

• OSHA Outreach Instructor (OSHA 30/10 ) is a plus

Benefits:

At Rent the Runway, we’re committed to the happiness and wellbeing of our employees, and aim to create a workplace that fosters both personal and professional growth. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Generous Paid Time Off including vacation, paid bereavement, and family sick leave - every employee needs time to take care of themselves and their family.

• Universal Paid Parental Leave for both parents + flexible return to work program - because we know your newest family member(s) deserve your undivided attention.

• Paid Sabbatical after 5 years of continuous service - Unplug, recharge, and have some fun!

• Exclusive employee subscription and rental discounts - to ensure you experience the magic of renting the runway (and give us valued feedback!).

• Comprehensive health, vision, dental, FSA and dependent care from day 1 of employment - Your health comes first and we’ve got you covered.

• Industry leading 401k match - an investment in your future.

• Company wide events and outings - our team spirit is no joke - we know how to have fun!

The anticipated base range for this position is $19.00 to $25.00. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Catering & Events
jobs.description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

The Catering & Events team owns one of Toast's most operationally important and fast-evolving products. Catering & Events helps restaurants take catering orders, manage private events, and get paid, all connected to the Toast platform. Operators use it for everything from daily office lunch orders to large weddings and buyouts, and it handles the details that make or break a high-stakes day.

Our vision is for Catering & Events to be the go-to solution for every Toast restaurant that caters or hosts events, and to serve a growing range of use cases across Toast's customer base. Getting there means three things: making the product easier to adopt and love, building the depth that sophisticated event operators expect, and applying AI to take work off operators' plates.

This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role at the intersection of restaurant operations, B2B software, and applied AI. You will shape how thousands of operators run their biggest revenue days, and you will help define where Catering & Events goes next.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

• Own and drive the Catering & Events product strategy, connecting investments to Toast's vision and near-term business outcomes such as revenue growth, customer retention, and support ticket reduction.

• Lead initiatives that help more customers get started and succeed with the product, from onboarding and setup to everyday workflows.

• Expand the product to serve more use cases and customer types across Toast's customer base, working directly with customers to translate complex, high-stakes workflow requirements into product decisions that serve the whole market.

• Define where AI creates real value for catering and event operators, and build the investment case to pursue the highest-leverage bets.

• Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success on packaging, positioning, and go-to-market to bring the product to the right customers in the right way.

• Shape and validate the business case for the next generation of Catering & Events, the long-horizon bets that drive future growth.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

• Proven experience defining and owning product strategy for a complex, operationally critical product, with bonus points for experience in food and beverage, hospitality, events, or payments.

• Creative and strategic instincts. You identify the next meaningful bet, make the case for it, and drive it from zero to conviction.

• Curiosity and a point of view on AI and agentic product opportunities in operational environments. You do not need to have shipped an agent, but you should have a clear perspective on where autonomous action creates real value and where it creates real risk.

• A track record of working directly with customers, translating nuanced workflow requirements into product decisions that scale well beyond a single logo.

• Strong instincts for the SMB operator: you understand what it means to run a restaurant without a data analyst, an IT team, or a change management budget, and you can build for that reality.

• Executive presence to drive alignment without authority across Engineering, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and product leadership in a high-stakes, cross-functional environment.

AI at Toast

At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it’s a core part of our culture.

Our Total Rewards Philosophy

We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters’ changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits.

The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. Zone A

$190,000—$304,000 USD

Zone B

Zone C

How Toast Uses AI in its Hiring Process

Throughout the hiring process, our goal is to get to know you. We use AI tools to support our recruiters and interviewers with tasks like note-taking, summarization, and documentation of interviews to ensure they can be fully focused on your conversation. All hiring decisions are made by people. We ask that you complete interviews and assessments on your own, without real-time AI tools, recording, or transcription bots, unless we tell you otherwise in advance. To learn more: https://careers.toasttab.com/ai-in-hiring

Our Approach to Hybrid Working

We embrace a hybrid work model that fosters in-person collaboration while valuing individual needs. Our goal is to build a strong culture of connection as we work together to empower the hospitality community, regardless of location. Please visit the Locations page on our career site to learn more about our in-office expectations by region: https://careers.toasttab.com/locations-toast

People Are the Secret Ingredient in Our Recipe for Success

jobs.title: Principal/Staff Product Manager, Platform
jobs.description:
About Us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world's largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We're based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, and Y Combinator.

We value diversity, in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide's team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

As a growth stage startup employee, you'll have the opportunity to build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners' lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.

 

About the Role

Fieldguide's platform is what every product is built on: documents, sheets, permissions, integrations and the agent infrastructure that runs through all of them. Our agents already support work across risk advisory frameworks and financial audit, and the platform is how we scale that to the whole engagement, to every firm's own methodology, and to the largest accounts' governance and security needs.

As Principal/Staff Product Manager for Platform, you'll be the senior product leader for the platform that agents and enterprise customers run on. Working closely with product leadership, you'll help shape platform strategy and own how it becomes a roadmap and shipped product. That includes giving firms the tools to build and publish their own agents, giving methodology owners and admins the right level of control, and connecting Fieldguide to the AI tools and systems firms already use. You'll partner with the Advisory and Financial Audit product teams, and with the cross-functional agent foundation teams, so every team builds on shared building blocks instead of rebuilding them.



What You'll Do

 - Shape the strategy for our agent platform, owning the roadmap and execution

 - Own the enterprise foundations our largest customers depend on: configurable roles and permissions, delegated template management, and governance and connectivity

 - Expand how customers and their AI tools work with Fieldguide through our API and MCP, so firms can run core engagement work from the tools they choose

 - Partner with the Advisory and Financial Audit PMs and with our agent foundation and AI quality teams to build shared components once and define the contract between the platform and the products built on it

 - Work with engineering and design on architecture trade-offs: what becomes a platform capability and what stays product-specific

 - Work directly with firm administrators, methodology owners and technical teams at our largest customers, including onsite, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap

 - Set the standard for platform thinking across the product organization
   

Who You Are

 - 10+ years of product management experience, including owning platform, infrastructure or developer-facing products at the staff level or equivalent

 - Experience building enterprise platform capabilities such as permissions and access control, APIs and integrations, or configurable workflows for large customers

 - Experience with AI agent infrastructure, or with building tools that let customers create and configure their own automation, is a strong plus

 - Strong technical fluency: you can go deep with engineers on architecture, APIs and AI agent design without needing to write code

 - Familiarity with audit, assurance or accounting software and workflows is preferred

 - Ability to communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, including recent AI developments

 - Able to hold a strategic position under sustained pressure from multiple product teams and large customers, and to change it when the argument is genuinely good

 - A senior individual contributor who leads through influence, comfortable shaping strategy alongside product leadership and then owning the execution

 - Degree in a technical or related field, or equivalent professional experience

 

More About Fieldguide

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

 - Fearless: Inspire and break down seemingly impossible walls.

 - Fast: Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

 - Lovable: Deliver happiness and 11 star experiences.

 - Owners: Execute and run the business with ownership.

 - Win-win: Create mutual value and earn trust for life.

 - Inclusive: Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.

 

Benefits

 - Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

 - Flexible PTO

 - 401k

 - Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions

 - Technology and Work from Home reimbursement

Now we’re taking the next step: agents that carry the whole advisory engagement, from scoping through sign-off, with practitioners stepping in only for exceptions and judgment calls.



As Principal/Staff Product Manager for Advisory, you will help shape the product strategy and roadmap that extends our agents from individual workflows to the full engagement lifecycle. You'll be building from a position of strength, with customers who already trust us and who are skeptical, expert and deeply invested in the quality of their work.



What You'll Do

 - Shape the strategy for the end-to-end agentic advisory engagement, and own the roadmap and execution that connect planning, testing and review into a single experience managed by agents

 - Define how practitioners supervise agents: what stays human, how exceptions surface, and how corrections make the agents better over time

 - Work with engineering, design and our AI quality teams to extend our agents across frameworks and engagement phases, with measurable evals and ground truth you help define

 - Work directly with partners, methodology owners and practitioners at top firms, including onsite, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap

 - Partner with customer success, sales and marketing to communicate the strategy and drive adoption of agentic workflows across our largest accounts



Who You Are

 - 10+ years of product management experience, including leading a major product line at the staff level or equivalent

 - Experience shipping AI agents in production for a B2B product, with evals and a clear approach to quality, not just AI features

 - Strong familiarity with advisory and assurance work (SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST, ISO or NIST), either as a practitioner or as a PM who built software for it.

 - Strong technical fluency: comfortable talking with engineers about LLM and agent architecture, evals, and trade-offs without needing to write code

 - Able to hold a strategic position under sustained pressure from commercial stakeholders and our largest customers, and to change it when the argument is genuinely good

 - Comfortable working with detail-oriented, skeptical audiences and translating their workflow into product requirements.

 

More About Fieldguide

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

 - Fearless: Inspire and break down seemingly impossible walls.

 - Fast: Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

 - Lovable: Deliver happiness and 11 star experiences.

 - Owners: Execute and run the business with ownership.

 - Win-win: Create mutual value and earn trust for life.

 - Inclusive: Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.

 

Benefits

 - Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

 - Flexible PTO

 - 401k

 - Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions

 - Technology and Work from Home reimbursement

jobs.title: Staff Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager, GTM Planning
jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 


ABOUT THE TEAM

Revenue Strategy & Operations is the team behind how Horizon3's go-to-market organization is planned, run and measured. We own budgeting and headcount planning, quota and compensation, territory planning and management (accounts, opportunities, leads and routing), goals for pipeline and performance, forecasting, performance management, and the operating process the sales organization runs on. Regional partners carry that scope for their sales leaders in AMER, EMEA and APJ. Global Centers of Excellence set the standards they all run on. This role is the GTM Planning center of excellence: the budget and headcount plan, the goals, and the performance standards the whole organization is measured against.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a Staff Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager to own Horizon3's go-to-market long-range plan: how the budget turns into headcount, capacity and targets, what has to be true globally and in each region to hit the number, and how we track whether we are on pace. The goal is one plan that top-down and bottom-up both agree with, and one set of numbers leaders trust.

You will work with Finance, Recruiting, Sales leadership and the regional Revenue Strategy & Operations partners. Finance owns the dollars. Recruiting owns the hiring. Sales Compensation owns how quota is constructed. Analytics builds and publishes the reports. The regional partners own the relationship with each sales leader and run the plan in their region. You own the plan, the goals and the model that connect all of it.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You build the models, pull the numbers and present them yourself. You need to be as comfortable with the executive team as with a regional sales leader, and able to get people at different levels to commit to the same plan. You will work closely with the Core Operations lead, who owns the standards and processes the organization runs on.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - GTM long-range plan: Own the go-to-market side of the long-range plan with Finance: headcount by role and region, hiring timing, ramp, productivity and capacity. Reconcile it to the budget every month so the plan, the roster and the projections tell the same story.

 - Capacity and headcount model: Build and maintain the model that shows how hiring turns into bookings capacity. Keep approved roles and start dates current, and work with Recruiting so the hiring plan and the capacity plan assume the same things.

 - Planning cycle: Run annual and in-year planning end to end: timeline, inputs, decision forums and sign-off. Territories, capacity and quotas are out before the fiscal year starts.

 - Quota allocation: Turn Finance-approved targets into segment, team and role-level quotas based on capacity, territory potential and productivity history. Check that quotas are attainable and fair before they reach the field. Sales Compensation owns how quota is constructed (buffer, proration, ramp, crediting); work with them so allocation and construction run as one method.

 - Goal framework: Set the goals beyond quota that spell out what has to be true globally and in each region: pipeline generation, conversion, SE and top-of-funnel targets agreed with Marketing, Channel and SDR. Keep them consistent so regional goals add up to the global plan.

 - Performance and efficiency metrics: Define the core performance and efficiency metrics, what they mean and how often they are reviewed. Pull and review the numbers, set the reporting calendar and requirements, and sign off that what Analytics publishes measures what the plan set.

 - Planning governance: Own how in-year changes to quota, territory and headcount are requested, approved and recorded, with clear thresholds. Run scenario planning for leadership with the assumptions written down.

 - Global and regional alignment: Be the operating partner to FP&A on heads, capacity and targets, and to the regional partners on their plans. Make sure every region's inputs land in the model, every region gets its plan and quotas back on time, and the global and regional plans tie.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - 8+ years in GTM planning, sales strategy and operations, revenue operations or sales finance in B2B SaaS, including end-to-end ownership of at least one global annual planning and quota cycle.

 - Planning expertise: You know capacity modeling, ramp and productivity assumptions, quota methodology and headcount planning. You have turned a top-down revenue target into a territory, capacity and quota plan that leaders could defend, across segments and regions, including direct and channel motions.

 - Modeling and data fluency: You build models in Excel or Google Sheets that someone else can pick up, follow and check, and you pull your own data from Salesforce. Experience with a planning platform or BI tool is a plus.

 - Analytical rigor: You notice when a number is wrong before it reaches a leader, you find out why, and you bring options rather than observations.

 - Executive influence: You hold your own with the executive team and with sales leaders. You can get stakeholders at different levels, across Sales, Finance and Recruiting, to agree on one plan without owning any of them, and you can tell a leader their numbers do not tie and what to do about it.

 - Execution: You run a planning cycle on a published timeline and land it. You set standards other teams adopt.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - The plan, the roster and the budget agree every month. When they drift, you know why before Finance asks.

 - Planning lands on time: territories, capacity and quotas are out before the fiscal year starts.

 - Every rep has a quota on day one, and the quotas hold up because attainability and fairness were checked before they went out.

 - Every GTM function has goals beyond quota, and the regional goals add up to the global plan.

 - There is one version of the performance numbers, leaders trust it, and it is the one you set.

 - Regional partners get what they need from the model on time, and nobody has to reconcile a regional plan to the global one by hand.

 

Perks of Horizon3

 - Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

 - Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

 - Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

 - Hybrid & Remote Work: We embrace a mix of remote and hybrid work models depending on role and location, including our Chicago office, where some roles require regular in-office presence.

 - Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.



Compensation and Values

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State’s transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

 - Base salary range: $170,000 - $210,000 annually. The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.

 - Additional compensation: All full-time roles are eligible for an equity package in the form of stock options.



You Belong Here

Horizon3 is not just an equal opportunity employer - we are a community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental principles of our culture and success. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, hair length or any other legally protected status by law.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion means we strive to attract, develop, and retain a workforce that reflects the varied communities we serve. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our ability to create cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions. At Horizon3, every team member is valued and supported in an environment that encourages personal and professional growth.

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we encourage all qualified individuals to apply. Come be a part of Horizon3, where your unique contributions are recognized, and your potential is limitless.



Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. 



Application Note

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

jobs.title: Sales Enablement Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Boostlingo is a leading language technology platform powering interpretation and translation services for healthcare, legal, government, and enterprise clients worldwide. Named an Inc. Magazine Best Workplace for four consecutive years, we are a high-growth, mission-driven company at the intersection of language access and AI innovation. Our team operates with urgency, operates with heart, and holds the bar high — for each other and for the people we serve.

WHAT IT MEANS TO BE A BOOSTIE

At Boostlingo, we operate through the lens of our four Core Values. These Core Values drive everything we do; from how we approach identifying talent we invite to join the team, to the energy and contributions we bring to our amazing culture, to the decisions we make at both the tactical and strategic level. To be a Boostie means to embody these Core Values every day:

• Positive Vibes: Bring positive energy and a solutions-oriented mindset to every interaction. High performance isn’t just about outputs — it’s about showing up with intentionality, resilience, and the belief that obstacles are problems worth solving.

• Drive Change: Stay curious, challenge assumptions, adapt quickly, and take action even when the path isn’t perfectly clear. Be proactive rather than reactive — and lean into AI as a force multiplier.

• Be Bold, Stay Humble: Growth lives in the tension between confidence and humility — be willing to stretch beyond what’s comfortable, own your development, and invest in the potential of the people around you. Every voice matters, and no one person is bigger than the team.

• Be Inclusive: Create and contribute to an environment where anyone can feel welcomed, supported, respected, and valued. Inclusive teams collaborate better — bring your full self, invest in others, and build the psychological safety that makes shared impact possible. Boostlingo is extremely honored to have been recognized as one of Inc. Magazine's Best Workplaces for the last three consecutive years (2022-2025). This esteemed recognition reflects the dedication that our incredible team has towards embodying our Core Values every day and we couldn’t be prouder of this team!

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

The Sales Enablement Manager builds the programs, content, and coaching that help Boostlingo sellers’ ramp faster, sell the full platform with confidence, and win more deals.

This role exists to make every Boostlingo seller measurably better, faster. As our first dedicated Sales Enablement leader, you will own the system that takes a new hire from day one to full productivity, keeps tenured reps sharp as our product evolves, and turns product and market messaging into conversations that win.

You will report to the VP of Sales and partner daily with the Product Marketing Manager: Product Marketing defines what we say and why it matters, and you make sure the field can say it, prove it, and sell with it. You will be especially important as we shift the market conversation toward AI Interpreter and a blended human plus AI language access model, a motion that requires new discovery skills, new objection handling, and new proof points across the team.

Because our platform is deep and evolving quickly, this role requires heavy product experience. You will be the sales team's product authority: equally credible running a demo, working through a technical discussion with a customer's IT or security team, or sitting in a roadmap session with Product and Engineering.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for someone who treats enablement as a revenue function, not a content library.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

1. Onboarding and ramp

• Design and own a structured 30/60/90-day onboarding program for AEs, SDRs, Account Managers, and Sales Engineers, with clear milestones, certifications, and role-play checkpoints

• Build a "time to first deal" and "time to full quota" ramp model, and continuously shorten it

• Partner with the People team and hiring managers so new sellers are prepared before day one and supported through their first quarter

2. Product mastery and technical fluency

• Master the Boostlingo platform end to end (for example, on-demand and scheduled interpretation, video and phone modalities, AI Interpreter, integrations, administration, and reporting) and stay current as releases ship

• Build and run a product certification program by role, with hands-on labs, demo assessments, and recertification after major releases

• Own demo environments, sandbox data, and demo scripts so every seller can run a credible, technically accurate demo

• Join product reviews, roadmap sessions, and beta or early-access programs, and turn what you learn into field-ready narratives before features reach customers

• Translate technical capabilities (integrations, APIs, security, compliance, and AI quality and limitations) into customer value, and equip reps to handle technical objections alongside Sales Engineers

• Maintain a living product knowledge base: feature guides, FAQs, release notes for sellers, and competitive feature comparisons

3. Sales content, playbooks, and tools

• Create and maintain the sales playbook: ICP and persona definitions, discovery frameworks, qualification criteria, objection handling, competitive battlecards, pricing and packaging guidance, and mutual action plans

• Build vertical and use-case playbooks for key segments such as healthcare, government, legal, education, and enterprise contact centers

• Develop pitch decks, demo scripts, one-pagers, case studies, ROI/value calculators, and email and call sequences, in close partnership with Product Marketing

• Own the content library so reps can find the right asset at the right moment; retire outdated material on a regular cadence

4. Training and continuous learning

• Deliver live and virtual training on product, messaging, sales methodology, negotiation, and competitive positioning

• Run recurring skill clinics, call-review sessions, deal-strategy workshops, and quarterly sales kickoffs

• Build AI-fluency training for the sales team, including how to position and demo AI Interpreter and how to use AI tools to prospect, prepare, and follow up

• Create certification paths and knowledge checks that verify sellers can apply what they learn

5. Coaching and sales manager enablement

• Equip front-line sales managers with coaching frameworks, call-scoring rubrics, and one-on-one and pipeline-review templates

• Use call recordings and conversation intelligence to identify skill gaps, surface winning behaviors, and scale best practices

• Support rep performance plans and development paths in partnership with the VP of Sales and the People team

6. Go-to-market launch partnership

• Work with the Product Marketing Manager to translate every product release, pricing change, and campaign into a sales-ready launch kit: messaging, FAQs, demo flow, objection handling, and training

• Run a repeatable launch-readiness process, with a clear "ready to sell" checkpoint before anything goes live to the field

• Capture field feedback, win/loss insights, and competitive intel and route them back to Product Marketing, Product, and Marketing

7. Sales process, systems, and operations

• Document and refine the end-to-end sales process and stage definitions with the VP of Sales and Revenue Operations

• Administer and optimize the enablement tech stack (for example, LMS or enablement platform, CRM, conversation intelligence, sales engagement, and content management tools)

• Partner with RevOps to embed guidance directly in the CRM, such as stage exit criteria, required fields, and in-workflow prompts

8. Measurement and reporting

• Define and track enablement KPIs tied to revenue outcomes, and report results to the VP of Sales and leadership on a regular cadence

• Analyze pipeline, conversion, and win-rate data to prioritize the highest-impact enablement investments

• Run pre- and post-training assessments, content-usage analytics, and rep feedback surveys to prove what works and stop what does not

How Success Is Measured

In the first year, success means faster ramp, higher win rates, and a field that sells AI Interpreter and the broader platform with confidence.

• First 30 days: Meet the sales team, the VP of Sales, and the Product Marketing Manager; shadow calls and demos; complete product certification and learn the platform hands-on; audit existing onboarding, content, tools, and training; interview reps and managers about their biggest gaps

• First 60 days: Deliver an enablement strategy and 12-month roadmap aligned to revenue goals; launch an improved new-hire onboarding path; publish a core messaging and discovery guide with Product Marketing; stand up a baseline KPI dashboard

• First 90 days: Run the first full sales training cycle and manager coaching session; ship the first launch-readiness kit with Product Marketing; roll out a product certification for the full sales team; launch a centralized, searchable content hub; report baseline metrics and the first measured improvements to leadership

• 6 to 12 months: Demonstrate shorter ramp time and improved win rate or conversion in targeted segments; certify the team on AI Interpreter positioning; operate a repeatable quarterly enablement and launch calendar

Ongoing KPIs (targets set with the VP of Sales):

• Time to first deal and time to full quota for new hires

• Quota attainment and percentage of reps at or above quota

• Win rate, stage-to-stage conversion, and sales cycle length

• Average deal size and AI Interpreter attach or adoption rates

• Training completion, product and sales certification pass rates, and pre/post assessment gains

• Content usage and content-influenced pipeline

• Launch readiness: percentage of reps certified before a release goes live

• Rep and manager satisfaction with enablement (survey scores)

Who You'll Partner With

• VP of Sales (manager): Set enablement priorities against revenue goals; align on sales methodology, coaching standards, and KPIs; report on impact

• Product Marketing Manager: Co-own sales messaging, positioning, battlecards, and launch kits; PMM owns the story, Enablement owns field readiness and adoption

• Sales managers and reps: Identify skill gaps, run training and coaching, and gather field feedback and win/loss insights

• Marketing: Align campaigns, content, and lead handoffs; make sure sales uses what marketing builds

• Customer Success and Support: Share customer proof points, handoff best practices, and expansion plays

• Product and Engineering: Partner as a peer to Product leadership: get early access to roadmap and releases, join product reviews, translate technical updates into sales-ready training, and bring field feedback into prioritization

• Revenue Operations: Align process, CRM guidance, reporting, and the enablement tech stack

• People team: Coordinate onboarding, performance development, and talent programs

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

• 5+ years of experience in sales enablement, sales training, sales operations, or a quota-carrying sales role, including 2+ years owning enablement programs for a B2B SaaS or technology sales team

• Heavy product experience: 3+ years in product management, product marketing, solutions consulting, sales engineering, or product-led enablement, with deep, hands-on fluency in how SaaS platforms are built, positioned, and sold

• Demonstrated ability to learn a complex technical product quickly, demo it credibly, and teach it at every level of technical depth

• Experience working directly with Product and Engineering on roadmap, releases, and beta programs, and translating technical capabilities (integrations, APIs, security, and compliance) into customer value and sales-ready content

• Working understanding of AI and machine learning products, including how to explain capabilities, limitations, quality, and responsible use to buyers

• Proven record of reducing ramp time and improving sales performance, with metrics to show it

• Hands-on experience building onboarding programs, playbooks, battlecards, and training curricula from scratch

• Working knowledge of a modern sales methodology (for example, MEDDICC, Challenger, SPIN, or Sandler) and how to operationalize it

• Strong facilitation and presentation skills, comfortable training reps, managers, and executives

• Experience with CRM (Salesforce or HubSpot), an enablement or LMS platform, and conversation intelligence tools such as Gong or similar

• Analytical mindset: able to connect enablement activity to pipeline and revenue and tell the story with data

• Excellent written communication and the ability to turn complex products into clear, compelling messaging

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Experience selling or enabling in language services, interpretation, translation, healthcare technology, government/public sector, or contact center technology

• Experience enabling a team through a major product shift, such as launching an AI-based product alongside a legacy offering

• Familiarity with both transactional and enterprise, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

• Experience in a PE-backed or high-growth environment where scale and speed matter

• Prior experience as a quota-carrying AE, SDR leader, or sales manager

• Enablement or training certifications (for example, Sales Enablement Society, ATD, or similar)

• Comfort using generative AI tools to build content, scale coaching, and personalize learning

• Bilingual or multilingual skills are a plus, not a requirement

How You'll Show Up

Core competencies

• Revenue orientation: you measure yourself by seller performance and business outcomes, not training hours delivered

• Business acumen: you understand how deals are won, how customers buy, and where reps get stuck

• Product depth: you go deep on the product, earn engineers' respect, and make complex technology simple for sellers and buyers

• Influence without authority: you earn trust with reps, managers, and cross-functional leaders alike

• Structured thinking: you turn messy problems into clear frameworks, programs, and repeatable processes

• Adaptability: you move quickly as product, market, and priorities change

• Learning agility: you stay ahead of AI, sales tech, and buyer behavior trends and bring them to the team

Boostlingo Core Values in Action

• Be Inclusive: Design learning that works for every seller, tenure, and learning style; reflect the diverse customers and communities we serve

• Positive Vibes: Create an energizing, encouraging learning culture where coaching feels like support, not scrutiny

• Be Bold / Stay Humble: Try new approaches, share what works, own what does not, and keep learning from the field

• Drive Change: Lead the team through new products, new motions, and an AI-first way of selling

WHAT MAKES BOOSTLINGO A GREAT COMPANY?

• Fun, energetic environment with an incredible culture (just ask about our eNPS scores!)

• Hybrid/Remote working arrangements

• Competitive compensation and robust benefits offerings, including 401(k) plan with match!

• Flexible PTO

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity here at Boostlingo. Boostlingo does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

No Agencies Please, C2C candidates will not be utilized at this time.
NO Relocation or Sponsorship are being offered for this position.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, State Estimation Foundations
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to build the software foundations of our state estimation program, spanning pose, calibration, and mapping. You’ll develop libraries, interfaces, and infrastructure used across the autonomy stack to enable safe, precise operation. You’ll help us track our excavator’s articulated arm, and represent the site it’s actively reshaping. You’ll leverage the type system to prevent coordinate-frame errors, and provide idiomatic, ergonomic interfaces for querying pose across a wide variety of vehicle platforms.

If you’ve built production software for localization, mapping, or calibration on robots or autonomous vehicles, this role is a natural fit. Experience with game engines, graphics software, or replay systems also applies. You don’t need a background in filtering or estimation theory. You’ll work daily alongside engineers who specialize in it. Depending on your background, you may focus on geometry and kinematics APIs, replay and evaluation infrastructure, or fleet and map data systems. We’re hiring at mid and senior levels, with scope matched to experience.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and own core geometry and kinematics libraries that teams across the autonomy stack rely on to represent coordinate frames, transforms, and machine motion consistently

 - Build pose and trajectory APIs that return machine state, including arm joint positions, at any timestamp, across machine types and sensor configurations

 - Develop infrastructure to routinely recompute pose estimates, calibrations, and maps on historical data for ML training datasets

 - Implement evaluation and regression testing tooling for pose estimation, calibration, and mapping

 - Build monitoring that detects when a sensor on a working machine has shifted out of calibration

 - Build storage and versioning for maps of sites that change every day

 - Diagnose issues from machines working on live job sites and optimize software performance, using recorded data, simulation, and testing on physical machines




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of professional software engineering experience, or a substantial record of shipping production systems or libraries that other engineers depend on

 - Working knowledge of linear algebra and 3D rigid-body transforms, including rotations, coordinate frames, and composing transformations

 - Ability to implement and test numerical code, including reasoning about numerical precision, boundary conditions, and correctness

 - Strong production software skills in Rust or modern C++. Our production stack is primarily Rust, and we will support experienced C++ engineers as they ramp up

 - Strong debugging and performance-analysis skills, including tracing problems across components and building tests and diagnostics to reproduce failures and prevent regressions

 - A degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience




WAYS TO STAND OUT

One or more of the following:

 - Experience shipping software on robots, vehicles, or other machines in the field

 - Production experience with Rust, including using types to enforce units, coordinate frames, or similar correctness guarantees

 - Experience with numerical optimization software

 - Experience with embedded or real-time systems




OTHER SPECIAL ASPECTS OF THE ROLE

 - Based in the Bay Area with the ability to be onsite at our SF office on a daily/weekly basis

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Program Manager, Government Manufacturing Contracts
jobs.description:
Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity.

Program Manager, Government Manufacturing Contracts

The Program Manager owns end-to-end execution of U.S. government manufacturing contracts from award through final delivery and closeout. This role coordinates internal functions (engineering, DFM, sourcing, quality, compliance, finance, shipping) and external stakeholders (government customer, DCMA/QAR, suppliers/subcontractors) to deliver parts on time, compliant, and at target margin. Success requires strong program control, manufacturing fluency, and practical knowledge of FAR/DFARS-driven contract requirements.

How You’ll Contribute:

Contract & Customer Execution

• Serve as the single accountable owner (single POC) for contract performance: schedule, cost, scope, and compliance

• Interpret contract requirements (CLINs, deliverables, CDRLs/data items, inspection/acceptance terms, packaging/marking, shipping instructions)

• Lead customer communications: status reviews, risk escalations, change requests, and delivery commitments

Manufacturing Delivery Leadership

• Build and maintain integrated master schedules (IMS) for production lots, first article, inspection, and shipment milestones

• Drive cross-functional execution: engineering release, process selection, sourcing, capacity planning, production, and logistics

• Manage subcontractors/suppliers: flow down requirements, manage lead times, track WIP, remove blockers, and ensure on-time delivery

Quality & Technical Compliance

• Ensure compliance with quality clauses and inspection requirements (FAI/AS9102 where applicable, source inspection, receiving inspection, certs, traceability)

• Coordinate quality events: First Article Testing, inspections, nonconformance (NCR/MRB), corrective actions (RCCA/8D), and customer dispositions

• Ensure documentation package completeness: CoC, material certs, process certs (heat treat, plating, NDT, etc.), test reports, and objective evidence

Government Contracting Compliance

• Ensure compliance with applicable FAR/DFARS clauses and program obligations (flowdowns, record retention, reporting)

• Manage controlled information and cybersecurity requirements (CUI handling, NIST 800-171/CMMC readiness as applicable)

• Support audits and government oversight (DCMA, DCAA support as relevant to program artifacts, cost/schedule evidence)

Risk, Cost, and Change Control

• Maintain risk register; lead mitigation plans for long-lead materials, capacity constraints, quality escapes, and design ambiguity

• Own change management: RFIs, engineering changes, waivers/deviations, and equitable adjustments (in partnership with contracts/legal)

• Track financial performance: earned value style tracking (as appropriate), cost-to-complete, margin impacts, and invoice readiness

Closeout & Continuous Improvement

• Drive contract closeout activities (deliverable completion, final invoicing support, lessons learned)

• Improve standard work for government manufacturing execution (templates, playbooks, supplier requirements, inspection readiness)

What You’ll Bring to Xometry:

• 7–9+ years program management experience in manufacturing (CNC machining, sheet metal, additive, fabrication, assemblies, or industrial production)

• 3–5+ years managing U.S. government contracts (DoD / federal), ideally involving hardware production and quality/inspection requirements

• Working knowledge of FAR/DFARS fundamentals (deliverables, changes, flowdowns, inspection/acceptance, recordkeeping)

• Strong understanding of manufacturing operations: routing, work instructions, lead-time drivers, supplier management, and constraints

• Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams, manage schedules, and deliver under tight timelines

• Experience running quality workflows: FAI, inspection planning, NCR/MRB, RCCA, certificate packages, traceability

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable engaging with government stakeholders and auditors

• Proficiency with program tools (Excel/Sheets, MS Project/Smartsheet or similar, ERP/MRP, basic dashboards)

Nice to Have:

• Experience as a prime contractor program manager (vs. only subcontractor) with full customer-facing ownership

• Familiarity with DCMA engagement (QAR source inspection, QMS expectations) and government acceptance processes

• Experience with DLA-style hardware contracting (NIINs, technical data packages, provisioning, packaging/marking)

• ITAR/EAR controlled work experience (export-controlled drawings, controlled tech data, visitor controls)

• Experience with CUI programs and NIST 800-171 / CMMC implementation coordination

• Knowledge of common manufacturing quality standards: AS9100, ISO 9001, NADCAP (special processes), AS9102 FAI

• Background in estimating/pricing support and contract change pricing support (REAs, mods)

• Familiarity with MIL-STD packaging/labeling, UID, and shipment compliance for government customers

• Experience managing multi-supplier networks (distributed manufacturing / marketplace / contract manufacturing models)

jobs.title: Sourcing Specialist (Starship)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOURCING SPECIALIST (STARSHIP)

SpaceX is committed to revolutionizing space travel, with the Starship program at the forefront of this mission. We are seeking a Sourcing Specialist with a track record of extreme ownership and a high sense of agency to own procurement and fulfillment of mechanical hardware necessary for mission success. The functions within the supply chain department include procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics and inventory.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Manage sourcing activities across a range of supported commodities including precision machined components, outside processes (e.g. heat treat, coatings, etc.), forgings, castings, and other complex manufactured parts.

• Quote out, negotiate, and place purchase orders for precision-machined mechanical components, ensuring alignment with technical specifications, cost targets, and delivery schedules.

• Forecast demand, evaluate supplier capacity, and proactively manage purchase orders to ensure uninterrupted supply of mechanical components in support of development and production schedules.

• Track and drive supplier performance metrics – such as quality, delivery, responsiveness, and cost – in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

• Interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications to align sourcing activities with suppliers possessing the optimal capabilities, ensuring manufacturability, quality, and cost efficiency.

• Manage frequent design changes by clearly and effectively communicating updates to the supply base, minimizing unproductive downtime and reducing lead times through proactive coordination.

• Taking the initiative to solve complex, open-ended supply chain problems in an ambiguous fast-evolving environment to ensure continuity of supply.

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with key internal and external stakeholders to confirm alignment, foster collaboration, and enable effective change management throughout the product lifecycle.

• Consistently complete tasks with a high level of efficiency and effectiveness, balancing speed and accuracy to meet critical program deadlines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree and 1+ year of experience working in one or more of the following; or 4+ years of experience working in one or more of the following: Engineering Supply Chain Purchasing Contract negotiation Material or production planning Operations management Material cost control Master production scheduling

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Strong track record for achieving results; must be able to reference wins and quantify impact

• Demonstrated ability to work in ambiguous situations and across organizational boundaries. History of self-learning & application of newly learned tools & techniques

• Ability to learn quickly and prioritize appropriately to meet customer and company needs

• Effective written and verbal communications skills, with strong ability to communicate complex ideas to an audience with a wide range of technical or product expertise

• Detail-oriented, self-motivated and able to respond quickly to a fast-moving and ever-changing environment. Proven capability to prioritize multiple on-going projects.

• Experience with MRP or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and with managing bill of materials, work orders, and purchase orders

• Experience with forecasting, demand planning, and lead time analysis

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing processes and machines including mills, lathes, forgings, castings, heat treatment, coatings, etc.

• Strong skills in data analysis using Excel, SQL and PowerBI

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be able to travel domestically and internationally for business needs - up to 50%

• Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed

• This position is based in Starbase, TX and requires being onsite - remote work not considered

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Calibration
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to develop calibration systems for the sensors and articulated geometry of our autonomous construction machines. Every machine we retrofit is different. There is no factory line to calibrate it on, and construction work shakes and knocks sensors out of place. You’ll build the algorithms and procedures that calibrate each machine, verify calibration accuracy to qualify it for autonomous operation, and detect when calibration degrades in the field.

Depending on your background, you may focus on sensor calibration, articulated-machine geometry, or validation and monitoring. You’ll write production software, test on real machines, and make sure field teams can run calibration independently across machine types. We’re hiring at mid and senior levels, with scope matched to experience.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Develop and deploy intrinsic and extrinsic calibration algorithms for our sensors (cameras, lidars, GNSS, IMU, encoders), and procedures for reasoning about machine geometry

 - Build calibration procedures that field teams can run without engineering involvement, on machines of varied types in active use at job sites

 - Own calibration verification methods used to qualify machines for autonomous operation, distinguishing a good numerical fit from accurate calibration through independent measurements and system-level testing

 - Define quantitative calibration quality metrics and acceptance criteria tied to machine performance

 - Develop methods to detect degraded calibration on working machines, and run these checks across the fleet

 - Diagnose calibration failures across sensor and kinematic models, timing, mounting, and data quality,

 - Test calibration improvements using recorded data and physical machines, working with estimation, perception, hardware, and field teams to resolve field issues




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of professional engineering or applied research experience in calibration, robotics, computer vision, or a related field, or a proven track record of delivering calibration systems for real-world applications

 - Strong foundations in linear algebra, 3D geometry, nonlinear optimization, and numerical methods

 - Hands-on experience developing sensor or kinematic calibration methods, including understanding the underlying models and what makes their parameters observable

 - Experience validating calibration accuracy beyond an optimizer’s residuals, and investigating failures using real sensor or machine data

 - Strong production software skills in Rust or modern C++. Our production stack is primarily Rust, and we will support experienced C++ engineers as they ramp up

 - A degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience




WAYS TO STAND OUT

One or more of the following:

 - Experience shipping software on robots, vehicles, or other machines in the field

 - Experience with in-field, targetless, or online calibration, or with calibrating articulated machines

 - Experience formulating and solving large nonlinear optimization problems, such as bundle adjustment or joint estimation of calibration, timing, and motion

 - Production experience with Rust




OTHER SPECIAL ASPECTS OF THE ROLE

 - Based in the Bay Area with the ability to be onsite at our SF office on a daily/weekly basis

We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Emergency Veterinarian (Part Time) - New Dorp/Staten Island, NY
jobs.location: Staten Island, New York, United States
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a part-time Emergency Veterinarian, you’re more than just passionate about helping people and their pets; you thrive on it, especially when they need you most. At VEG, we find a way to say yes to supporting you, so you can be the best, most confident ER professional possible and grow your career in unexpected directions. With a culture rooted in mentorship and continuous learning—from on-the-floor guidance to VEG Education programs and unlimited ER-focused CE—you’ll never stop learning. You’ll handle any emergency that comes through the door, from routine cases to complex surgeries, and treat every kind of pet, including exotics! As a leader on the hospital floor, you’ll have the chance to be a superhero for your customers, backed by a team and resources that empower you to take your career further than you ever imagined.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Answer medical questions over the phone

• See patients right away as part of the VEG Triage and VEG Spikes, our unique, customer-centered way of doing things—like ensuring people see a doctor right away and allowing families to stay with their pets

• Gather the signalment, presenting complaint, vitals, and physical exam

• Conduct physical examinations of animals, along with other required investigatory measures such as ultrasounds, X-rays, bloodwork, and biopsies

• Complete a diagnosis of each pet's condition to create a diagnostic and therapeutic plan

• Communicate diagnosis and treatment options directly with customers

• Prepare estimates and present them to customers

• Create and review medical records to ensure accuracy

• Demonstrate the value of tests and treatments performed by speaking with the customer and addressing their concerns

• Perform minor and major emergency surgeries

• Perform endoscopic procedures

• Educate customers on after care and preventative measures where appropriate

WHAT YOU NEED

• A DVM or equivalent degree

• Live and breathe emergency medicine, including emergency surgery (the soft tissue kind!) and endoscopy

• Thrive in team-oriented environments (think hospital retreats, team dinners, happy hours, and more)

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation (Base compensation $140,000 - $200,000k + production)

• A BIG focus on learning and growth from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to Unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (No really!). Part-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend. Part-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $400/year travel stipend

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart's Workplace Operations team supports the secure and efficient handling of critical business documents across the company. The Burlingame mailroom serves as the central hub for receiving, processing, and distributing sensitive mail for teams including Legal, Collections, Credit Disputes, Auto Title, Auto Recovery, Complaints, and Borrower Success. The team focuses on delivering accurate, timely, and compliant service while improving processes that reduce operational risk and increase efficiency.

As a Senior Mailroom Administrator at Upstart, you'll manage the day-to-day processing of inbound and outbound mail, ensuring documents are handled securely and routed accurately. You'll also help improve reporting, streamline manual workflows, and contribute to projects that make mailroom operations more efficient and scalable.

Please Note: This role is based in our Burlingame, CA office and requires working onsite five days per week.

How you’ll make an impact

• Manage daily inbound and outbound mail operations, including sorting, scanning, tracking, and routing documents while meeting established service levels.

• Handle confidential and time-sensitive documents in accordance with security, compliance, and operational procedures, escalating exceptions when appropriate.

• Maintain accurate mail records, operational metrics, and reporting using Salesforce, Jira, Google Sheets, and other business systems.

• Identify opportunities to improve reporting, automate repetitive tasks, and streamline mailroom workflows using available tools and technologies.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to resolve routing issues, address operational needs, and maintain reliable mail processing.

• Support operational improvement initiatives, including vendor transitions, process documentation, and updates to workflows that improve efficiency and reduce risk.

Minimum Qualifications

• 2+ years of experience in mailroom operations, logistics, document processing, facilities operations, or a similar operational environment.

• Experience processing, tracking, and routing inbound and outbound mail or physical documents in a high-volume environment.

• Experience handling confidential or sensitive documents in accordance with established security or compliance procedures.

• Experience using spreadsheet tools, including Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel, to organize, track, and report operational data.

• Experience using business systems such as Salesforce, Jira, or comparable workflow or case management platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

• Knowledge of spreadsheet functions, pivot tables, dashboards, or reporting tools used to analyze operational performance.

• Experience identifying and implementing process improvements or automating repetitive workflows using tools such as Google Apps Script or Generative AI.

• Familiarity with financial services, regulated environments, or document-handling requirements involving sensitive information.

• Ability to prioritize time-sensitive work, troubleshoot operational issues, and determine when escalation is appropriate.

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams or external vendors to improve operational processes and documentation.

In-Office requirements: You will be required to work from the Burlingame, CA office 5 days per week.
